description:
Medical Data Intern (x/f/m)

Set a new pulse for healthcare!

We are looking for a Medical Data Intern to join the Terminology and Ontology team within the Medical Excellence department at Doctolib in Berlin.

 

At Doctolib, we're setting a new pulse for healthcare. We create AI-powered solutions that help health professionals focus on care and help people prevent, detect, and treat health problems earlier. In this role, you will contribute to making medical information clear, structured, and usable across products for patients, healthcare professionals, and technical teams.

What you'll do

Your responsibilities include but are not limited to:

  • Collect and format sets of terms describing pathologies, allergies, treatments, and other medical concepts, based on standard medical terminologies such as ICD-10 and SNOMED CT.

  • Adapt medical labels to create versions that are understandable to patients and healthcare professionals.

  • Translate labels from English into German.

  • Map medical lists of terms across different products.

  • Select and filter terms, then validate your choices with medical experts.

  • Share your work and methodology with the Terminology and Ontology team and product teams.

  • Deliver sets of terms to technical teams in the correct format.



About our data environment

  • Our solutions are built on a single fully cloud-native platform that supports web and mobile app interfaces, multiple languages, and is adapted to the country and healthcare specialty requirements.

  • Our stack is composed of Dagster, dbt, Google Cloud Platform, BigQuery, and other technologies.

  • We leverage AI ethically across our products to empower patients and health professionals. Discover our AI vision here and learn about our first AI hackathon here!

If you would like to find out more about tech life at Doctolib, feel free to read our latest Medium blog articles!

Who you are

Before you read on, if you don't have the exact profile described below, but you feel this job description matches your skill set, we still encourage you to apply.

You could be our next teammate if:

  • You have medical skills gained through a diploma or degree that includes medical-domain learning.

  • You have knowledge of data management.

  • You are familiar with medical terminologies such as ICD-10 and SNOMED CT.

  • You have strong spreadsheet skills, including Google Sheets or Excel and the use of formulas. 

  • You are attentive to detail and demonstrate rigour in your work.

  • You speak German and English, which is a must have for this role.

Nice to have:

  • Experience using AI tools such as Claude.

  • Python programming skills.

  • Additional depth of medical knowledge.

  • Dutch language skills.

 

What we offer

  • A structured and personalized onboarding program through our Doctolib Academy, as well as a wide range of in-house training opportunities and masterclasses throughout the internship.

  • Regular breakfast in the office and subsidies for your lunch or grocery shopping.

  • A Deutschlandticket sponsored by Doctolib, or reimbursement of your semester ticket.

  • A flexible workplace policy offering up to 2 days of hybrid work per week.

 

The interview process

  • An interview with our Talent Partner (30 minutes).

  • An interview with the hiring manager (30 minutes).

Job details

  • Contract Type: Internship (Mandatory/Voluntary)

  • Working Time: Full-time

  • Duration: 6 months

  • Work model: Hybrid

  • Location: Berlin, Germany.

  • Expected start date: January 2027

At Doctolib, we are committed to improving access to healthcare for everyone. This commitment is reflected in our hiring process, where we assess applications based solely on qualifications, potential, and motivation, without discrimination of any kind.

We believe that diverse perspectives, backgrounds, and experiences help us build better healthcare products. We welcome applications from all candidates, regardless of gender, religion, age, sexual orientation, ethnicity, or disability.

To support equal opportunities, we encourage candidates not to include unnecessary personal information, such as a photo or age, in their application. If you need any accommodation during the hiring process, please let us know and we will do our best to support you.

title: Senior Software Engineer - Node.js/TypeScript (x/f/m)
description:
Set a new pulse for healthcare!

We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer to join the DIAL team in the Phone Assistant domain.

Your mission will be to design, build, and scale the AI-powered features that transform how practitioners and patients connect over the phone — making care more accessible for patients and reducing administrative burden for health professionals. You will work in a feature team developing the Phone Assistant, Doctolib's solution that combines LLM reasoning, speech recognition, and real-time backend systems, launching first in Germany and expanding to France and Italy. 

Working in the tech team at Doctolib means building innovative products and features to improve the daily lives of care teams and patients.

What you'll do

Your responsibilities include but are not limited to:

  • Build and operate backend services in Node.js/TypeScript (with Python exposure), designing for reliability, scalability, and real-time performance

  • Design, evaluate, and ship LLM-based features end-to-end: prompt engineering, tool calling, structured outputs, guardrails, and fallback strategies

  • Own AI feature quality: build evaluation datasets and scorers (e.g., in Braintrust), track regressions, and make evidence-based ship decisions before each release

  • Deploy and operate cloud-native services on Kubernetes across major cloud providers (AWS/Azure/GCP), and evolve CI/CD pipelines with GitHub Actions

  • Design data models and drive database migrations and performance tuning for real-time workloads (PostgreSQL: connection pooling, indexing, query optimisation)

  • Maintain a high testing bar (unit, integration, e2e), debug distributed systems in production with strong observability, and contribute to pragmatic, secure architecture decisions

Who you are

Before you read on: if you don't have the exact profile described below, but you feel this job description matches your skill set, we still encourage you to apply.

You'll be a great fit if you:

  • Have 5+ years of backend engineering experience building scalable, resilient systems in Node.js/TypeScript (with some Python)

  • Have hands-on production experience building LLM-based features: prompting, tool calling, structured outputs, eval frameworks, and handling real-world failure modes

  • Have proven experience deploying and operating services on Kubernetes within at least one major cloud provider (AWS, Azure, or GCP), with solid CI/CD practices

  • Have a strong testing culture (unit/integration/e2e), sharp debugging skills for microservices and distributed systems, and a focus on code quality

  • Are fluent in English, with a collaborative mindset and the drive to own problems end-to-end — from design to production

It would be fantastic if you:

  • Have experience with speech pipelines (ASR, TTS, streaming audio) or voice agents

  • Are familiar with event-driven architectures and message brokers (Kafka, RabbitMQ, NATS, or Redis Streams), and have hands-on PostgreSQL experience (EXPLAIN/ANALYZE, indexing strategies, connection pooling)

  • Have an interest in telephony and real-time communication (SIP, RTP, WebRTC) — no prior experience needed, we will teach you

Life at Doctolib Tech

  • Our solutions are built on a single fully cloud-native platform that supports web and mobile app interfaces, multiple languages, and is adapted to country and healthcare specialty requirements.

  • Our stack is composed of Rails, TypeScript, Java, Python, Kotlin, Swift, and React Native.

  • We leverage AI ethically across our products to empower patients and health professionals. Discover our AI vision here.

Want to learn more about our tech culture and environment? Visit the Doctolib Tech site.

  • A Deutschlandticket (Germany-wide public transport pass) fully paid for by Doctolib

  • 28 vacation days + 1 additional day for each full calendar year of employment (up to a maximum of 30 days)

  • Work from abroad for up to 10 days per year thanks to our flexibility days policy

  • Company health insurance with great supplementary benefits through our partner Allianz

  • Company pension scheme (bAV) through Allianz with an employer subsidy of 40% (15% within the probationary period)

title: Senior AI Specialist (Operations) (x/f/m)
description:
Doctolib is looking for you to join us as a Senior AI Specialist (x/f/m) at our Berlin location, starting as soon as possible.

Doctolib is becoming an AI-native company. We are redesigning the way we work, workflow by workflow, and are looking for people who will not only support this transformation, but actively build it. As a Senior AI Specialist, you will be the technical builder and AI Ops Owner behind AI-powered productivity for our Operations and Customer Success teams.

 

You will work in founder and product mode: you will own a workflow end to end, from context and agent design to evaluation, and continuously take it to a higher level of automation. Our ambition is to move away from manual case-by-case work towards workflows that run largely autonomously while maintaining a high quality bar. In this way, you will contribute directly to our mission of improving healthcare for everyone.

Your Responsibilities

  • Redesign workflows rather than simply automating them: You analyze the most critical Operations and Customer Success workflows, break down time-consuming processes that require limited judgment, and transform them through the use of AI agents. You set clear objectives for autonomy and quality, and continuously develop them further.

  • Build and operate AI agents as products: You develop and manage agents on platforms such as Dust or Claude. Each agent is deployed to production with a defined baseline and relevant metrics such as benefit, usage, and scalability.

  • Knowledge and context management: You deliberately curate the context agents need, from templates to core data. The guiding principle is quality over quantity. You ensure that knowledge sources in Confluence, Drive, or Salesforce are always up to date and well structured.

  • Evaluation and quality assurance: You define quality standards and establish evaluation routines to identify and address weaknesses such as hallucinations or prompt drift at an early stage. You continuously optimize prompts through systematic user feedback and A/B testing.

  • CRM and data integration: You own the interfaces between CRM systems such as Salesforce and our AI platforms. You automate data flows and work closely with IT to unlock new, valuable data sources for our agents.

  • Central interface and enablement: You translate business requirements into technical solutions and bring together stakeholders from Leadership, IT, and Product. You strengthen the team’s AI fluency in the areas of context, agent management, and evaluation.

  • Impact and measurement: Rather than inventing new KPIs, you make the success of AI measurable using existing metrics such as time, quality, and cost, and use these insights to guide the next steps in scaling.

Your Profile

Since production-ready AI workflows and agent technologies are still relatively new, years of market experience are rare. We therefore deliberately prioritize potential over years of experience alone. What matters to us is your ability to learn quickly, your strong product mindset, and your judgment. If you are passionate about this field and bring the necessary skills, we would be delighted to hear from you, even if your profile does not perfectly cover every single aspect.

What Really Matters to Us, Regardless of the Specific Tool:

  • Learning speed and a production mindset: You have taught yourself a new technical field from scratch and built something real that people actually used. You can describe precisely what went wrong, such as hallucinations, prompt drift, outdated data, or costs, and how you solved it.

  • An instinct for evaluation: You do not rely on something merely “looking good”. You define a quality bar and measure against it. For you, automation and quality go hand in hand.

  • Ownership and communication: You take ownership of a problem end to end, prioritize rigorously, feel comfortable with ambiguity, and make technical topics understandable to non-technical stakeholders.

  • Technical and data understanding: You can read and adapt scripts, understand APIs, webhooks, and automation tools such as Make, n8n, and Zapier, and know how CRM data, ideally Salesforce data, flows into AI systems.

  • Strong communication skills: You have a confident command of English and can operate at the highest level in our international environment. German at B1 level is sufficient.

We Are Particularly Interested in:

  • Expertise with agent platforms: You have practical experience with systems such as Dust, Claude, or LangChain. Since tools evolve quickly, we primarily rely on your process understanding and evaluation skills as a sustainable foundation.

  • Technical depth and data fluency: You are proficient in languages such as Python or JavaScript and can confidently navigate Salesforce architectures or BI environments such as Tableau and Metabase to manage data flows effectively.

  • Operations experience: You have solid experience working with scaled Customer Success or Operations teams and understand their specific dynamics.

What We Offer

  • A Germany-wide public transport pass sponsored by Doctolib if you work from the office or in hybrid mode

  • Company-sponsored health insurance with excellent additional benefits

  • 28 days of paid vacation, plus one additional day for every full calendar year of employment, up to a maximum of 30 days

  • Participation in Doctolib’s long-term employee equity program, DoctoGrowth

  • The opportunity to work from abroad for up to 10 days per year

  • An occupational pension scheme with an employer contribution of 40%, or 15% during the probationary period

  • The Doctolib Parent Care Program, which includes one additional month of parental leave and much more

  • Free mental health and coaching sessions through an external partner

  • In addition to healthy snacks and a regular breakfast buffet, we offer meal vouchers

  • A subsidized sports program with our partner Urban Sports Club

  • For caregivers and employees with disabilities, we offer support that includes more flexible working hours, additional leave for medical reasons, and psychological support

  • Interview with Talent

  • Hiring Manager interview

  • On-site case study

  • Final interview with VP

  • Reference checks

  • Offer

  • Permanent position

  • Full-time

  • Location: Berlin

  • Start date: July

  • Hybrid, 2 days working from home per week

The more diverse our team and ideas are, the more our product can contribute to improving the health of our users. That is why we invite you to apply, regardless of gender, religion, age, sexual orientation, ethnic origin, or disability.

 

To ensure equal opportunities, you may omit information such as photos, age, and similar details from your application. Please let us know what accommodations we can make to support you in the best possible way.

We look forward to digitalizing healthcare together with you!

  • Turn our free tools into real product entry points, where users get immediate value and then continue into Neural Frames without losing their song, lyrics, artwork, or progress

  • Run conversion experiments across the whole funnel: landing pages, calls to action, signup, onboarding, paywalls, packaging, and pricing

  • Ship on the core product when that's where the growth lever is, especially product-native loops: shareable creations, templates, embeds, referrals, and public pages that give creators a reason to spread Neural Frames for us

title: Senior Software Developer:in (m/w/d)
description:
KI verändert unseren Job gerade nicht jährlich, sondern monatlich. Und vielleicht merkst du, dass dein Umfeld da nicht mitkommt: KI ist verboten, wird ignoriert oder läuft als „mach mal KI“ nebenher. Bei uns ist das anders. Wir wollen KI nicht irgendwie in den Alltag kippen, sondern wirklich verstehen und als Werkzeug nutzen, das unsere Fähigkeiten erweitert, statt sie zu ersetzen. Wer die Veränderung gestalten will, muss schneller lernen, als sie passiert.

Das heißt auch: Umsetzen ist kein Hexenwerk mehr. Früher war der Job 70, 80 % Entwickeln, das dreht sich gerade. Umsetzung kann man delegieren, Entscheidungen nicht. Darum bist du bei uns der Übersetzer zwischen Fachlichkeit und Technik, und die Ownership für eine Entscheidung trägst du, keine KI.

Das machst du nicht in einem Bodyshop, der dir einen Stuhl beim Kunden besorgt. Und auch nicht in einer Beratung, die nach drei Monaten ein 200-Seiten-Dokument hinterlässt. Wir sitzen über Jahre als tragendes Element in den Entwicklungsteams unserer Kunden, meist in Digitalisierungsteams im Konzern, und schieben dort das ganze Team nach vorne.

Wie du startest

Du kommst in ein bestehendes Projekt mit einem von uns, gehst mit in die Termine und kommst schnell ins Doing, statt ewig Sachen zu lesen. Am Anfang hast du einen Paten, der dich im Team mitnimmt, und einen fachlichen Ansprechpartner. Nach etwa sechs Monaten führst du Termine alleine, setzt Themen eigenständig um und gehst in die Architekturplanung. Stück für Stück übergeben wir dir den Staffelstab, bis du in deinem Bereich die Verantwortung für den Kunden trägst. Leadership heißt bei uns: technische Führung nach außen, nicht nach innen.

Aufgaben

  • Du arbeitest bei einem Kunden, nicht bei dreien gleichzeitig. Mindestens einer von uns ist mit im Projekt, und ihr seid fester Teil der Routinen vom Kundenteam.

  • Du redest direkt mit dem Fachbereich und den Entscheidern. Keine Proxy-POs, kein Projektleiter dazwischen.

  • Du lernst die Fachsprache vom Kunden, modellierst die Domain und setzt sie um, im Backend mit Node/TypeScript, vorne mit React.

  • Du wartest nicht, bis dir jemand eine Aufgabe gibt. Du findest die Aufgaben, stimmst sie ab und übernimmst die Ownership dafür.

  • Ein Ticket ist schön. Und dann reden wir nochmal drüber, wie die Fachlichkeit wirklich ist.

  • Wir sagen nicht Ja und Amen zu allem. Wenn was keinen Sinn macht, sagst du das. Diplomatisch, aber klar.

  • Es geht um den Wert, der beim Kunden entsteht. Dafür baust du sauber und sagst dem Kunden transparent, was der nächste Schritt bringt und was er kostet.

Dein Profil

Was du mitbringst

  • Du bist eher in Fachlichkeiten und im Backend zu Hause als beim nächsten abgespacten UX-Feature. Denn sind wir ehrlich, das bekommt man mittlerweile gut automatisiert.

  • Du willst eine Fachdomäne durchdringen und im Großen mitdenken.

  • Du laberst keinen Bullshit, du stehst zu dem, was du sagst.

  • Offenheit und Interesse für die Chancen mit KI.

  • Rund 6 Jahre professionelle Softwareentwicklung, das meiste davon im Backend mit einer typisierten Sprache, am liebsten Node/TypeScript.

  • Node/TypeScript steht bei dir in einem echten Projekt, nicht nur in der Skill-Liste. Und dein letzter Backend-Einsatz in Produktion ist nicht ewig her.

  • Du hast Architektur nicht nur gesehen, sondern auch verantwortet und gestaltet.

  • Du kennst dich in einer Cloud aus, AWS, Azure oder GCP, und kannst sagen, welche Dienste du wofür genutzt hast.

  • Du hast Anforderungen selbst mit dem Fachbereich geklärt, Epics geschnitten und Aufwand mit Risiko benannt.

  • Du hast PoCs gebaut, Technologien ausgewählt und als ADR dokumentiert, Konventionen eingeführt und technische Schulden abgebaut.

  • Deutsch auf C1-Niveau, denn Deutsch ist unsere Domänensprache.

  • Du tickst nicht alle Boxen? Wenn dich das hier anfixt, bewirb dich trotzdem.

Nice to have

  • Du kennst die Baustoffbranche schon von innen. Einer unserer Kunden ist ein Baustoffhersteller.

  • Kubernetes löst bei dir keinen Angstschweiß aus.

  • Domain-Driven Design und hexagonale Architektur begeistern dich.

  • Du denkst eine API vom Vertrag her: OpenAPI, sauberes REST-Design, Backend for Frontend.

  • Du hast KI-Werkzeuge in einem Team eingeführt und weißt, wie man motiviert.

  • Du hast Leute gementort oder ein Projekt schon alleine verantwortet.

  • Du teilst gerne Wissen: Vorträge, Blog, Open Source oder ein Thema außerhalb vom Stack.

Wenn du nicht zu uns passt

  • Du willst ein Team führen. Wir sind zu sechst und planen keine mittlere Führungsebene.

  • Du nutzt KI, um Verantwortung abzugeben, statt deine Entscheidungskraft zu erweitern.

  • Du willst lieber am eigenen Produkt arbeiten als beim Kunden, oder lieber Konzepte malen als selbst bauen.

  • Du willst deine Arbeitsweise durchdrücken, statt aktuelle Praxis zu verstehen.

  • Der Teamtag alle 4 Wochen ist für dich eine lästige Pflicht.

  • Für dich ist es am Ende halt ein Job, und dich treiben vor allem Gehalt und Titel.

  • Du suchst eigentlich das nächste Freelance-Projekt und keine Festanstellung.

Der Prozess

Kurz und ohne fünf Gesprächsrunden.

  1. Erstgespräch mit mir, 30 Minuten remote. Du prüfst uns dabei genauso wie ich dich. Am Ende sage ich dir direkt, wie ich es sehe, und nicht hinterher in einer kalten Mail.

  2. Kennenlerntag mit dem Team, remote, 4 Stunden mit Pausen. Das ist keine Prüfung. Du reviewst Code und erklärst, was dir auffällt. Du baust mit deinem eigenen KI-Setup einen Fix, so wie du wirklich arbeitest. Und du führst ein Kundengespräch im Rollenspiel und lernst das Team in 1:1s kennen. Danach können wir beide klar sagen: passt oder passt nicht.

  3. Referenzen und Angebot. Wir entscheiden gemeinsam als Team und machen dir ein Angebot. Persönlich sehen wir uns spätestens beim Angebotsgespräch oder beim ersten Teamtag.

Nach jedem Schritt hörst du in ein, zwei Tagen von uns. Und wenn es nicht passt, sagen wir dir das persönlich und mit Begründung. Unser Ziel: höchstens zwei Wochen für den ganzen Prozess.

Benefits

Wie wir zusammenarbeiten

  • Wir arbeiten full remote, niemand sitzt im Büro. Alle 4 Wochen treffen wir uns in Darmstadt zum Teamtag. Das klappt gut, wenn du in etwa 4 Stunden bei uns bist.

  • Wir sind keine Family, wir sind gute Kollegen.

  • Warum wir suchen: Wir haben mehr Anfragen, als wir aktuell umsetzen können. Wir wollen nachhaltig wachsen sehen aber in unserer Größe in der aktuellen Zeit eine Stärke.

Unsere Formate

  • Check-in, jeden Morgen: nicht fachlich, sondern sozial. Und es ist voll okay zu sagen: Gerade ist echt nicht cool.

  • AI-Catchup, jede Woche: Wir schauen was letzte Woche in der KI-Welt passiert ist und wie wir unseren Workflow verbessert haben.

  • Weekend Checkout, jeden Freitag: 15 Minuten zum Abschluss der Woche.

title: Working Student / Intern Finance & Operations (m/f/d)
description:
Your mission

About GENUINE

GENUINE is Europe’s leading TikTok Shop agency, and we’re right in the middle of the social commerce revolution. We don’t just make content. We build shopping experiences that sell, at the speed of a viral trend. We’re growing fast, and so does our Finance & Operations team.

The Mission

Behind every viral LIVE and every creator campaign, a lot of money moves: platform fees, creator commissions, client payouts. You’ll help keep all of it clean, on time and under control. You’ll see how a hypergrowth agency really runs, and you’ll learn more in a few months than in most full-time jobs.

What You’ll Do

  • Follow the money: Match TikTok Shop settlements, fees and affiliate commissions against our records, and catch every gap.

  • Keep creators happy: Prepare payout lists, check invoices and make sure everyone gets paid correctly and on time.
  • Keep the books tidy: Collect and organize invoices and receipts so accounting and our tax advisor have everything they need.
  • Automate the boring stuff: Help set up tools that connect TikTok Shop data with our accounting software.
  • Have a say in strategy: Run analyses for pricing, client offers and leadership decisions.

Your profile

Who You Are

  • Student: You’re studying Business, Finance, Economics, Business Informatics or something similar, and you want a working student job or an internship.
  • Excel nerd: Pivot tables and XLOOKUP don’t scare you. You enjoy finding patterns in messy data.

  • Fast learner: You’re comfortable in organized chaos, you ask questions, and you get things done.
  • Bonus points: You’ve worked in finance or e-commerce before, or you already know TikTok Shop, Shopify, Moss or Spendesk.

Why us?

  • Flexible hours: 16 to 40 hours per week, so it fits around your studies or works as a full-time internship

  • Great team: We’re young, international and based in the heart of Cologne.
  • Room to grow: If it clicks, you can stay on longer or move into a full-time role.

Vous serez également amené(e) à interagir régulièrement avec les autres départements marketing tels que l'équipe média, l'équipe créative, le CRM ainsi qu'avec l'équipe commerciale. 

Vos missions consisteront à:

  • Mettre en avant sur l'application les restaurants et partenaires disponibles sur l'app.
  • Soutenir l'équipe commerciale dans la création et l'exécution de plans marketing destinés à mettre en avant les partenaires présents sur Deliveroo.  
  • Collaborer étroitement avec l'équipe commerciale et les équipes marketing transversales (marque, réseaux sociaux, CRM et influenceurs) pour développer et exécuter des plans partenaires basés sur les priorités commerciales (par exemple, objectifs régionaux, accords d'exclusivité, renégociations).

  • Contribuer à l'exécution des points forts des partenaires en collaboration avec le CRM et le Commercial (communications mensuelles d'exclusivité / bannières dédiées sur l'application / notifications push...).
  • Gérer le budget alloué pour le plan de chaque partenaire, en optimisant les ressources locales pour obtenir un impact maximal. 
  • Analyser l'impact de nos campagnes pour en tirer des recommandations pour les équipes commerciales

Cette alternance vous permettra d'appréhender de nombreux sujets marketing (création de campagne, analyse, sensibilité client) et vous permettra d'acquérir une bonne connaissance des enjeux marketing et de la gestion de projets complexes grâce à la collaboration transverse que vous aurez avec les autres pôles.

  • Vous avez une excellente communication écrite et orale en français ainsi qu'un bon niveau d'anglais.
  • Vous êtes à l'aise avec les chiffres et aimez analyser les performances pour en tirer des recommandations.
  • Vous appréciez le travail en équipe et la coordination de nombreux interlocuteurs.
  • Vous êtes curieux·se, proactif·ve et souhaitez évoluer dans un environnement dynamique et en forte croissance.

Voici un lien avec de la documentation pour vous préparer aux entretiens.

Nous offrons un environnement de travail dynamique et stimulant, où vous aurez l'opportunité de développer vos compétences et de contribuer activement à notre mission. Rejoignez notre équipe exceptionnelle dès maintenant et faites partie de cette aventure passionnante !

La vie chez Deliveroo :

Notre équipe est en forte croissance, notre impact très important, et nous cherchons à répondre aux questions les plus stimulantes du moment. Nous progressons rapidement, nous explorons toujours de nouvelles idées et nous sommes très transparents quant aux décisions que nous prenons et à ce qui motive nos choix.

Il y a tellement de questions que nous souhaitons résoudre, et encore plus que nous n'avons pas encore rencontrées. Comment les données et la technologie peuvent-elles aider les restaurants à développer leur activité à mesure que les habitudes des consommateurs évoluent ? Comment pouvons-nous prédire ce qu'une personne souhaitera pour dîner avant même que l'idée ne lui vienne à l'esprit ? title: Research and Development Engineer in Artificial Intelligence - 12 months contract
description:
Who we are ?

Télécom Paris, part of the IMT (Institut Mines-Télécom) and a founding member of the Institut Polytechnique de Paris, is one of France's top 6 general engineering schools.

The mainspring of Télécom Paris is to train, imagine and undertake to design digital models, technologies and solutions for a society and economy that respect people and their environment.

Modern distributed systems are increasingly complex, with multiple interconnected components, services, and autonomous agents interacting in dynamic environments. Ensuring their cybersecurity requires analysing potential attacks, understanding the strategies available to attackers and defenders, and verifying that critical security properties are preserved. Formal verification provides rigorous methods for addressing these challenges, allowing engineers to reason about system behaviours and establish mathematical guarantees. However, applying these techniques to realistic systems remains challenging. Verification problems can involve large state spaces and complex strategic interactions, while constructing formal models and specifying security properties often requires specialised expertise.

The VITAMIN-C (VerIficaTion of A MultI-ageNt system for Cybersecurity) project aims to address these challenges by combining formal verification with artificial intelligence. Building on VITAMIN, an existing modular model-checking platform for multi-agent systems, the project develops methods and tools for analysing cybersecurity properties in distributed and autonomous systems. Attackers and defenders are represented as agents with specific capabilities, objectives, and available actions. Their interactions are analysed using attack graphs, temporal and strategic logics, and model-checking techniques. The project also investigates how AI can improve the efficiency and accessibility of these verification processes.

A central objective of VITAMIN-C is to integrate AI techniques into the verification workflow. On the computational side, AI models will be investigated to guide the exploration of large state spaces and prioritise promising verification strategies. By learning from previously verified models and their associated results, these components can help identify relevant search directions and reduce the computational effort required by verification algorithms. On the usability side, the project explores AI-assisted interfaces that support engineers in constructing formal models and specifying security properties. These interfaces may exploit natural-language processing and large language models to interpret engineering descriptions, suggest formal representations, and assist users throughout the verification process. In both cases, the correctness of verification results remains the responsibility of the underlying formal methods, which validate the outcomes produced or suggested by AI components.

Within this context, the R&D engineer will contribute to the design, implementation, and evaluation of AI techniques for VITAMIN-C. The work will focus on developing AI components for verification guidance, investigating natural-language and LLM-based assistance for formal modelling, and integrating these capabilities into the existing platform. The engineer will also participate in the preparation of training and evaluation datasets, the development of experimental benchmarks, and the assessment of the proposed approaches in terms of effectiveness, computational efficiency, and reliability. The overall objective is to make formal verification more scalable and accessible while preserving the rigorous guarantees provided by the verification framework.

Your main responsibilities will include :

  • Carry out R&D work in artificial intelligence for formal verification

  • Contribute to the research profile of Télécom Paris and Institut Mines-Télécom


The candidate must have a solid understanding of artificial intelligence, Python programming, data processing and analysis, and software engineering. They must also be fluent in English and able to develop, train, evaluate, test and document AI components within a collaborative environment.

Experience in deep learning, natural language processing (NLP/LLM), graph learning, learning-guided search or the deployment of machine learning models would be an advantage. An interest in formal verification, cybersecurity, trustworthy AI, Docker and teaching activities would also be appreciated.

The role also requires strong organisational, analytical and problem-solving skills, as well as a good team spirit. The candidate must be able to communicate clearly, explain technical concepts in layman’s terms, draft documentation and contribute to teaching activities.

Notre croissance rapide reflète une ambition claire : équiper les forces armées avec des systèmes à la hauteur des enjeux actuels. Nous recherchons des profils prêts à s’engager dans un environnement technique exigeant, avec un fort sens de la mission et de l’impact.

 
 

Rôle

Nous recherchons un Technicien Qualité pour rejoindre notre bureau de Paris. En travaillant sur le terrain aux côtés des équipes d'ingénierie, de fabrication et de qualité, vous veillerez à ce que la qualité soit intégrée à nos produits, du prototype jusqu'à la livraison au client. Vous rapporterez au Responsable Qualité.

 
 

Responsabilités

Support à la fabrication de prototypes :

  • Fournir un support qualité lors de l'assemblage des prototypes, en veillant à ce que les constructions soient conformes aux plans, aux instructions de travail et aux spécifications.

  • Identifier et documenter les pièces non conformes, soutenir le traitement et les actions correctives aux côtés de l'équipe d'ingénierie.

  • Aider à définir les méthodes d'inspection et les critères d'acceptation pour les nouveaux composants.

 

Revue de premier article (FAI) :

  • Réaliser des revues de premier article sur les pièces de développement.

  • Préparer et maintenir les rapports FAI avec une traçabilité complète des résultats d'inspection.

  • Assurer le suivi des conclusions de la FAI et veiller à ce que les actions correctives soient clôturées avant la mise en production.

 

Mur Qualité – Produits en développement :

  • Gérer le point de contrôle du mur qualité, en vérifiant que chaque unité de développement répond aux critères définis avant de passer à la phase suivante.

  • Tenir à jour les registres du mur qualité et donner de la visibilité sur l'état des produits et les motifs de blocage.

  • Faire remonter les défauts récurrents à l'Ingénierie Qualité et à la Conception pour résolution.

 

Support après-vente et tri chez le client :

  • Participer aux activités de support après-vente, y compris l'inspection sur site et le tri des produits chez les clients si nécessaire.

  • Effectuer des contrôles visuels et dimensionnels pour identifier les unités non conformes, isoler les produits défectueux et documenter les résultats.

  • Agir en tant que représentant qualité sur site, assurant la liaison entre le client et les équipes internes pour résoudre efficacement les problèmes de qualité.

  • Remonter les observations du terrain au centre de développement pour piloter les actions correctives et l'amélioration des produits.

 

Système Qualité et Amélioration Continue :

  • Veiller à ce que les rapports d'inspection et de non-conformité soient correctement documentés dans les outils appropriés (Jira, Confluence ou QMS).

  • Contribuer à l'amélioration des processus d'inspection et des critères du mur qualité au fil du temps.

 

Prérequis

  • Diplôme technique en qualité, génie mécanique, fabrication ou domaine connexe.

  • Première expérience dans un rôle d'inspection qualité ou de qualité fabrication, idéalement dans les secteurs de l'aérospatiale, de la défense ou de la haute technologie.

  • Capacité à lire des dessins d'ingénierie et à utiliser les outils d'inspection standards (pieds à coulisse, micromètres, etc.).

  • La connaissance des processus de revue de premier article (FAI) est un plus.

  • Connaissance des normes ISO 9001 et EN 9100.

  • Minutieux, rigoureux et à l'aise pour travailler en atelier.

  • Esprit d'équipe et bonnes compétences en communication.

  • Bon niveau d'anglais ; disponibilité pour se déplacer sur les sites des clients si nécessaire.

  • Adhésion totale à la mission de Harmattan AI et volonté de s'investir pleinement pour soutenir notre croissance.

title: Senior Structural Analysis Engineer
description:
About Pangea Propulsion:

We are a company dedicated to developing advanced propulsion systems for the space industry based on three key principles: high efficiency, sustainability, and reusability. We are revolutionizing the space industry with ground-breaking innovations that allow us to offer the best performance to cost propulsion systems.

Our goal is to be the propulsion provider for the next generation of spacecraft, which is essential to meet demands and compete in the booming space market of the next decade.

We are a passionate, multicultural, and multidisciplinary team pushing the boundaries of what is possible in space propulsion technology.

We have already made history by successfully testing the world's first 3D-printed Methalox Aerospike engine, marking a significant milestone for the space industry.

We are looking for talented professionals to join our international teams in Barcelona and Toulouse. We want to be a key player in improving diversity in the Aerospace sector as, in Pangea, we believe that diversity (gender, age, race, sexual orientation, beliefs, disability, culture, etc.) is a key to success. Within Pangea, everyone can grow with the same opportunities. We encourage you to apply. Individually we are different, but together we are an amazing team!

We are looking for a Structural Analysis Engineer in Toulouse.

About the role:

As a Structural Analysis Engineer, you will be a key technical contributor within Pangea Propulsion’s Structural Analysis team, operating with autonomy on thermomechanical, dynamic, and nonlinear structural problems.

You will own analysis campaigns end-to-end: from problem framing, modelling, validation, to results interpretation and design recommendations - directly influencing the architecture, performance, and robustness of the next generation of propulsion systems.

Within the team, you will serve as a technical reference point for advanced structural analysis methods, help shape internal best practices, and elevate the quality of analyses across projects.

A core part of your role will be coaching and guiding junior and consolidated analysts, transferring knowledge, reviewing technical work, and contributing to a high-performance engineering culture.

In this position, you will also take ownership of complex structural analysis problems and contribute to defining modelling strategies and analysis standards for the team.

Familiarity with rocket propulsion hardware - or strong motivation to learn - will allow you to make an immediate impact.

Key responsibilities

· Perform and lead FEA campaigns including static, modal, thermo-mechanical, dynamic and transient analyses, dealing efficiently with non-linear problems (contacts, plasticity, large deformation etc.)

· Plan, build, verify, document and maintain high-fidelity and robust FE models with traceability to loads, material properties, requirements, and assumptions.

· Provide clear, high-impact design feedback to mechanical design and propulsion teams at both part and subsystem level.

· Develop and improve analysis methodologies, scripts, subroutines, benchmarks, and guidelines.

· Lead cross disciplinary interactions with mechanical design, fluidic analysis, and test teams to ensure coherent modelling strategies and proper load mapping.

· Participate in design reviews, presenting methods, assumptions, results, and recommendations with clarity, conciseness and technical rigor.

· Mentor junior and consolidated engineers, helping them develop modelling skills, physics intuition, validation strategies, and efficient workflows.

· Review and challenge analysis approaches to ensure modelling robustness and consistency across projects.

What you need to be successful

· Experience in the aviation or space industry is strongly preferred.

· Master’s degree (or higher) in Aerospace, Mechanical, or related engineering disciplines.

· Minimum 5+ years of professional experience performing advanced structural analyses using commercial FEA tools (preferably Abaqus).

· Proven ability to run non-linear, thermo-mechanical, and dynamic analyses with a high level of autonomy and technical ownership.

· Strong understanding of structural mechanics, vibrations, fatigue, fracture, material behavior, and numerical methods.

· Demonstrated experience framing analysis problems, defining assumptions, and ensuring consistency with loads and system requirements.

· Ability to interpret results critically, identify anomalies, and propose sound engineering solutions.

· Excellent communication skills—able to articulate assumptions, limitations, and design implications clearly to multidisciplinary teams.

· Proactive mindset, ownership attitude, and passion for sharing knowledge and elevating team capability.

· Fluent English.

Other useful skills

· Experience in any of the following topics: fatigue (high cycle and low cycle), fracture mechanics, rotodynamics, test-correlation, topology optimization or probabilistic structural methods.

· Knowledge of rocket propulsion systems: injector heads, thrust chambers, turbomachinery, feed systems, thermal & dynamic environments, etc.

· Proficiency with meshing tools (e.g., MeshWorks) and scripting languages (Python, MATLAB).

· Experience writing Abaqus subroutines (UMAT, USDFLD, UEL, etc.).

· Experience working with ECSS, AIAA and other aerospace structural verification standards.

Not hitting every requirement? Research suggests that some people tend to hesitate when it comes to job applications if they don't meet all the desired qualifications. Here at Pangea Aerospace, we're committed to fostering a workplace that values diversity, inclusivity, and authenticity. So, if you're enthusiastic about this role but your prior experience doesn't align perfectly with every qualification mentioned in the job description, we still strongly encourage you to apply. You might just be the ideal candidate for this position or other opportunities within our organization.

More about us…

We are an international and very multicultural team. Our work is guided by these core values:

Teamwork: We strive to work together as an aligned team towards our common goals.

Respect & tolerance: we value people with integrity that treat other people with respect. We enjoy having diverse views to enrich the debate and take better decisions.

Passion for growth: we are passionate about space and about being pioneers; also, we value personal and organizational growth aiming to a constant improvement.

Sustainability: because a long-term vision and strategy is not possible if sustainability is not in the team’s core values.

Daring: we do things that sometimes seem impossible, but we always go the extra mile to find a path to do them and we are ready to take the necessary risks to achieve our goals.

If this sounds good to you and you want to join the New Space revolution, we really want to meet you!

Senior Software Engineer - OpenCRQ
description:
🌀 The Company

Founded in 2022, Filigran is a global cybersecurity company on a mission to empower defense teams to be proactive through open-source solutions that uncover threats and drive action.

Filigran stands out in the cybersecurity ecosystem through its open-source, AI-powered and threat-informed approach to Continuous Threat Exposure Management (CTEM). Our eXtended Threat Management (XTM) platform brings together threat intelligence, exposure validation and cyber risk reduction, enabling organizations to better understand their threat landscape and take action.

At the heart of Filigran is our open-source approach. Our vision is to unite defenders into a global community to make security more open, resilient and collaborative.

As Filigran continues to scale globally, we are building the organization, infrastructure and capabilities needed for our next stage of growth. How we scale matters just as much as how fast we scale: our CORE values: Cohesion, Openness, Responsibility and Equity shape how we work together, make decisions and build for the future.

 

🎯 The Role

We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer who is curious about the modeling problem underneath cyber risk and wants to help shape a young product.

You will join OpenCRQ as its fourth engineer and work across the data model, backend and product surface. Many foundations are still being defined, giving you meaningful influence beyond the features you directly own.

You will shape these decisions with the squad and experienced engineering and product leaders across Filigran. We value constructive disagreement, clear reasoning and shared outcomes, and we expect everyone to ask for context, challenge assumptions and learn from one another.

🧩 The problem you would be working on

Ask a CISO what a cyber risk could cost, and the answer often still begins with a color: red, amber or green, often produced by a spreadsheet disconnected from current evidence.

OpenCRQ replaces that color with a financial estimate and a traceable chain of evidence: which threat actors are active, which assets they can reach, which controls have proven effective and what the remaining exposure could cost.

Every step is computed from live data and must withstand a simple question from a board: “Where does that figure come from?” That is what makes this an engineering problem rather than a reporting one.

OpenCRQ is Filigran’s cyber risk quantification product. It combines threat intelligence from OpenCTI, exposure and control validation from OpenAEV, and agentic workflows through XTM One. As these products become more connected, the squad will define what agents can ask of the risk model, which evidence they can use and how their answers remain safe and explainable.

🛠️ What you would work on

  • End-to-end product ownership. Take product problems from early ideation and technical design through implementation, end-to-end testing and validation with users. You will have the autonomy to drive the work, while using the squad to challenge assumptions and improve the outcome.

  • The quantification engine. Turn threat frequency, control effectiveness and asset value into probabilistic loss distributions. Build general-purpose quantitative models that can evolve as assumptions and available evidence change, without losing reproducibility or explainability.

  • The correlation layer. Model complex relationships across OpenCRQ, OpenCTI, OpenAEV and customer systems. Map threat intelligence, including intrusion sets, techniques, campaigns and observations, to assets, vulnerabilities, exposures and control coverage. This includes adapting OpenCRQ to open standards and schemas such as STIX and OCSF, without coupling the product to a single representation.

  • Reliable ingestion at scale. Process hundreds of thousands of findings per tenant through delta syncs, long-running backfills and feeds with imperfect timestamps. You will help design observable, recoverable pipelines while extending tenant isolation as the domain grows.

  • The agentic surface. Design the contracts used by XTM One agents and the plain-language explanations behind risk figures. Together, the squad will define what models can safely do in a product whose outputs inform board-level decisions.

🏆 What success could look like

Priorities will evolve with the product, but within your first 6 to 12 months you could have:

  • Taken a meaningful product problem from early ideation through implementation, end-to-end testing and validation with users.

  • Shaped a core part of OpenCRQ’s interconnected data model or quantification engine and documented the trade-offs behind it.

  • Made a major ingestion or calculation path more observable, recoverable and reproducible.

  • Defined or implemented a durable contract between OpenCRQ and another Filigran product or an open standard, without making the internal model brittle.

  • Helped ship risk results that users can trace back to the evidence that produced them.

  • Contributed to the open-source release and to engineering practices the growing squad can build on.

🌐 Open source, like the rest of Filigran

OpenCRQ is about to become Open source, alongside OpenCTI and OpenAEV. You will contribute visibly to a product whose risk calculations can be inspected, challenged and improved by the organizations running it.

👥 The squad

You will join two senior engineers and a staff engineer, reporting to OpenCRQ’s Engineering Manager. The squad is small enough for you to influence its direction, without working in isolation.

You will collaborate with the VP of Technology, CTO and Principal Engineers on technical standards, and with the OpenCTI, OpenAEV and XTM One teams on cross-product contracts and integrations. These relationships bring domain knowledge and broader technical context into the squad’s decisions as it grows.

✨ What will help you succeed

We do not expect you to arrive with expertise in cyber risk or every standard named below. We are looking for a strong software engineer who can learn quickly, work autonomously and use the squad to challenge and improve decisions.

  • A track record of taking complex product problems from an ambiguous idea to a validated outcome: framing the problem, making technical decisions, implementing the solution, testing it end to end and checking that it solves the user’s need.

  • Strong experience with a modern TypeScript stack and practical knowledge of PostgreSQL beyond the ORM. You treat failure modes and observability as part of the design.

  • The ability to reason about complex relationships across systems and design interconnected data models that remain coherent as concepts and integrations evolve.

  • Comfort turning quantitative concepts into maintainable software. Formal training in statistics is not required, but you should be willing to work with probability distributions, orders of magnitude and models whose assumptions evolve over time.

  • Thoughtful use of coding agents: you know where they accelerate engineering and where their output needs careful verification.

  • Fluent English is required.

💡 Useful, but not required

Any of the following would help, but none is expected:

  • Experience in cybersecurity, GRC or risk quantification.

  • Familiarity with STIX/TAXII, OCSF, MITRE ATT&CK or other open cybersecurity standards and frameworks.

  • Experience shipping features involving LLM agents, RAG or MCP.

⚙️ The stack

TypeScript end to end: React, Vite and TanStack Router on the frontend; Node.js, Fastify and tRPC on the backend; PostgreSQL with a code-first schema and Drizzle, all in one monorepo.

OpenCRQ ships as a container, both as SaaS and on customer-managed infrastructure. We use OpenTelemetry for traces, metrics and logs, alongside Prometheus and continuous profiling.

A significant part of the design work happens at the boundaries between OpenCRQ, the rest of Filigran’s product suite and customer security tooling. You will work directly with the teams that own those systems rather than having to navigate those boundaries alone.

🌱 Why Join Filigran? More than just a job.

We are a fast-growing, global and remote-first company, and we believe the best work combines purpose, impact and innovation. You’ll work alongside talented people across the world who care about what they build, how they build it, and the impact they make on the broader cybersecurity ecosystem.

⭐ Be part of something bigger

We believe we do work that matters. Our open-source approach means that work extends beyond Filigran. You’re contributing to technology and ideas that strengthen a global community of defenders and help make cybersecurity more open and collaborative.

💻 Work at the edge of what’s next

We bring together cybersecurity, open source and AI — giving you the opportunity to work with emerging technologies, experiment with new ways of working, and contribute to how they are applied in practice.

🌍 Global opportunity without borders

Be part of a fast-growing, truly international team — collaborating across Europe, North America, APJ and beyond, with the flexibility of a remote-first environment. As we grow, you’ll have opportunities to expand your scope, take ownership, learn quickly and grow with us.

🧭 A culture grounded in CORE

Cohesion, Openness, Responsibility and Equity define how we work together — with openness, ownership, collaboration and respect. These are the principles that guide how we make decisions, treat people and grow together, especially when no one’s watching.

💰 What you can expect

  • Competitive compensation + equity — everyone shares in our success

  • Remote-first flexibility — work from wherever you’re based, with flexibility built into how we operate

  • 25 days PTO baseline — real time to disconnect, recharge and enjoy life outside work

  • Volunteer days — paid time to contribute to causes that matter to you

  • Set up for success — choose the equipment that works for you, with additional support for your remote work and development needs as our programs evolve

  • Two annual in-person get-togethers — one global company get-together and one team get-together, creating dedicated time to connect, collaborate and strengthen our culture beyond the screen

🌍 Equal Employment Opportunity

We enable cybersecurity through inclusion — from code to culture.

At Filigran, we are proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We believe the diversity of our people makes our products and our team stronger. We welcome talent of every background, identity and lived experience, regardless of race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, age, disability or veteran status.

What matters here is what you bring, not what you look like, where you’re from or how you identify.

Our entrepreneurial spirit drives us in what we do and what we are passionate about. Our mission is to become the premier health partner in the insurance business. Recognising the need for innovation in the traditional employee insurance model we are set to revolutionize the employee insurance industry. We help companies support people before and after they get sick and to make more of their time. Our insurance solutions reduce monotonous and manual work for employees, doctors, HR & payroll managers. As we strive to lead a technology-driven transformation, we put employees first.
 
At grape we pride ourselves on our people and our culture. We continue to grow fast and that’s where you come in. Our team is dynamic, diverse and full of creative ideas. Want to join? We can’t wait to get to know you!

Your role

Our data and tech give us an edge in risk assessment, pricing and premium calculation. title: Sales Manager CH, KI-Software für Psychotherapeut:innen
description:
Über VIA HealthTech

VIA macht aus einer Therapiesitzung ein fertiges Sitzungsprotokoll und aus Sitzungsprotokollen vollständige psychologische Berichte. Arbeit, die Therapeut:innen bisher mehrere Stunden pro Woche gekostet hat.

Wir sind die marktführende KI-Assistenz für Psychotherapeut:innen. Über 4.000 Psychotherapeut:innen im DACH-Raum nutzen VIA, wir verarbeiten Hunderttausende Sitzungen pro Monat. Wir sind nach ISO 27001:2022 zertifiziert und verfügen über ein BSI-C5-Testat.

Wir sind ein multidisziplinäres Team in Berlin-Mitte. Marktführer in Deutschland zu sein, ist erst der Startpunkt. Die Schweiz ist unser nächster Markt, und du baust ihn mit auf.

Die Rolle

Du bist unsere erste Person im Schweizer Markt. Du baust die Pipeline von Grund auf, entwickelst das Playbook und führst es selbst aus.

In Deutschland läuft unser Funnel vor allem über Webinare: Therapeut:innen melden sich an, testen VIA 14 Tage und buchen selbst. Du findest heraus, was davon in der Schweiz funktioniert und was anders laufen muss: Qualifizierung am Telefon, Cold-Calling, andere Outbound- und Inbound-Kanäle, Verbände, Weiterbildungsinstitute, grössere Organisationen als eigener Kanal. Du testest, misst und skalierst, wo der Hebel am grössten ist.

Du arbeitest eng mit Marketing an Zielgruppen, Kampagnen und Botschaften für den Schweizer Markt und gibst direkt zurück, was im Gespräch wirklich zieht.

Die Rolle ist senior gedacht. Wenn du mid-level, aber aussergewöhnlich schnell und hungrig bist, bewirb dich trotzdem.

Deine Aufgaben

  • Den Markt öffnen. Du identifizierst die wichtigsten Zielgruppen in der Schweiz: selbstständige psychologische Psychotherapeut:innen, Psychiater:innen, Organisationen der psychologischen Psychotherapie, Ambulatorien und Kliniken. Du priorisierst, wo wir zuerst gewinnen.
  • Leads in Kund:innen verwandeln. Qualifizierungsgespräche, Webinare, Demos, Follow-up während der Testphase, Abschluss. Du bist die zentrale Ansprechperson für Schweizer Kund:innen.
  • Neue Kanäle erschliessen. Berufsverbände wie FSP, ASP und SBAP, Weiterbildungsinstitute, Fachveranstaltungen und Kongresse. Erstansprache per Telefon, E-Mail und LinkedIn, wo sie sich lohnt.
  • Playbook bauen, während du verkaufst. Was konvertiert, welche Einwände in der Schweiz wirklich kommen (etwa zu Datenschutz und Datenhaltung), welche Sequenz funktioniert.
  • Zahlen verantworten. Deine KPIs entlang des Funnels, gemeinsam mit unserem Commercial Engine Lead, der Tracking und Infrastruktur baut.
  • Sales-Enablement-Material. Du passt an, was zum Verkaufen und Vermarkten in der Schweiz am besten wirkt, von Sprache bis Preisdarstellung in CHF.
  • Feedback ins Produkt bringen. Was Schweizer Kund:innen brauchen und woran Deals scheitern, besprichst du direkt mit dem Produktteam.

Dein Profil

Must-have

  • Nachgewiesene Abschlüsse im B2B-Vertrieb in der Schweiz, idealerweise SaaS oder Digital Health, belegbar in Zahlen
  • Echte Hunter-Mentalität. Du hast bereits aktiv Erstkontakte am Telefon gemacht und hast damit kein Problem. Wenn dich 40 Gespräche am Tag abschrecken, ist das die falsche Rolle
  • Kenntnis des Schweizer Gesundheitswesens oder die Fähigkeit, dich sehr schnell einzuarbeiten: Grundversicherung, Anordnungsmodell, Rolle von Kantonen und Verbänden
  • Glaubwürdigkeit gegenüber Therapeut:innen. Psychotherapeut:innen vertrauen vor allem Psychotherapeut:innen. Entweder bringst du diesen Hintergrund mit, oder du arbeitest dich so schnell und so tief ein, dass man es dir im Gespräch nicht anmerkt
  • Systemdenken. Du baust reproduzierbare Prozesse statt Einzelfälle, mit dem Ziel, dass dein Ansatz auch ohne dich funktioniert
  • Hunger und unternehmerischer Ehrgeiz. Du willst einen neuen Markt aufbauen, nicht eine Quote abarbeiten
  • Kommunikationsstärke mit Abschlussfokus. Empathisch und auf Augenhöhe, denn Psychotherapeut:innen merken sofort, wenn jemand verkauft, statt zu verstehen
  • Selbstständige, strukturierte und datengetriebene Arbeitsweise, auch remote und ohne Team vor Ort, sowie sicherer Umgang mit CRM-Systemen
  • Deutsch auf verhandlungssicherem Niveau (C2), auch Schweizerdeutsch, gutes Englisch
  • Verfügbarkeit am frühen Abend. Unsere Zielgruppe ist häufig erst nach der letzten Sitzung erreichbar, Termine zwischen 17 und 19 Uhr gehören dazu. Im Gegenzug gestaltest du deinen Tag frei

Von Vorteil

  • Französisch und/oder Italienisch, um später auch die weiteren Gebiete anzusprechen
  • Ein bestehendes Netzwerk in der Schweizer Psychotherapie- oder Psychiatrieszene
  • Erfahrung mit Funnels, in denen Marketing und Vertrieb ineinandergreifen: Performance-Marketing, Webinare, Trials, Self-Service
  • Anerkennung als Psychotherapeut:in, psychologische Ausbildung oder mehrjährige Erfahrung im Gesundheitswesen
  • Vertriebserfahrung mit Praxen, Heilberufen oder Spitälern in der Schweiz
  • Hands-on-Erfahrung mit Sales-Automation, LinkedIn Sales Navigator oder Outbound-Tooling
  • Erfahrung im Markteintritt oder Aufbau eines Vertriebs von 0 auf 1

Diese Rolle ist nichts für dich, wenn

  • Du ein Team suchst, das für dich telefoniert.
  • Du eine fertige Pipeline oder ein bestehendes Länderteam erwartest. Du baust beides.
  • Du weder Hunger noch besonderen Ehrgeiz mitbringst. Wir sind ein ambitioniertes Team und stellen entsprechend ein.

Was wir bieten

  • Einen Markt, den du prägst. Du bist die erste Person von VIA in der Schweiz. Was du aufbaust, wird zum Fundament unseres Schweizer Geschäfts
  • Ein Team, das überperformt. DACH-Marktführer für KI-Assistenz in der Psychotherapie in zwei Jahren, bootstrapped. Unsere Pläne von hier sind deutlich grösser, und wir stellen Menschen ein, die das mitgestalten wollen
  • Hohe Autonomie und Erfolgsbeteiligung. Bei uns zählen Kompetenz und Umsetzung. Wir legen dir keine Steine in den Weg, und du verdienst an dem, was du aufbaust
  • Attraktives Paket. Wettbewerbsfähiges Fixum in CHF plus ungedeckelte Provision, dazu Beteiligung am Unternehmen
  • Direkter Draht. Du arbeitest täglich mit den Gründern und dem multidisziplinären Team, Entscheidungen fallen in Stunden statt in Wochen
  • Sinnstiftende Arbeit. Jede Praxis, die du gewinnst, bedeutet mehrere Stunden pro Woche, die wieder Patient:innen zugutekommen
  • Flexibel arbeiten. Remote aus der Schweiz, freie Zeiteinteilung, moderne Ausstattung und regelmässige Teamtage in unserem Büro in Berlin-Mitte

Wir suchen keine:n klassische:n Vertriebler:in, sondern eine:n Macher:in, die oder der mit Hunger und Hands-on-Mentalität VIA in der Schweiz zur ersten Wahl macht.

title: Senior Backend & AI Engineer (Remote)
description:
This role is open only to candidates living in the EU or EEA. We can't consider applications from other locations.

If you've built something before, start here

The hardest part of a startup usually isn't the code. It's finding customers who really need what you build and getting them to change how they work. At Scalera, that part is done: manufacturers, suppliers and contractors across Switzerland, Austria and Germany already run their tenders through us every day.

What we need now are people who can take the next unsolved problem and turn it into a product customers can't do without. If you've founded a company (whether it worked out or not), been the first engineer somewhere, or built something people paid for, this role was written for you.

About Scalera

Scalera is an ETH Zurich spin-off building AI for the €200B+ European construction industry. Large manufacturers and suppliers still run their most document-heavy processes by hand, from reading 300-page tenders to retyping purchase orders into their ERP. We automate them one by one. Our product matching already handles 1,400 tender positions in 16 minutes at 98% precision, work that used to take a sales rep most of a day.

What you'll do

You'll be part product manager, part engineer. You'll spend real time with customers and help shape what we build. Sometimes you'll spot the next problem yourself, and sometimes we'll hand you a clear priority to run with.

  • Spend real time with customers. Join calls and site visits, sit with the people who do the work, and understand why they do it the way they do. You'll know their problems firsthand, not from a ticket.

  • Shape what to build. Turn what you hear into a clear problem, a scope and a plan, and push back when the obvious request isn't the real need. When we bring you a priority, you'll own how it gets solved.

  • Build it. Design and build backend services in Go and Python that turn messy tenders, catalogs and purchase orders into data customers can rely on.

  • Ship, then check. Get it in front of customers fast, watch how they actually use it, and iterate.

  • Own it in production. When something breaks at a customer, it's yours to understand and fix.

  • Build with AI. Use AI heavily in how you work, and design systems that agents can use as well as people.

What success looks like after 3 months

  • There's a part of the product people now think of as yours, and you're the one deciding what happens to it next

  • You've spotted a problem nobody asked you to solve, made the case for it, and shipped a first version

  • You've shipped features from both sources: priorities we set and ideas from your own customer conversations

  • At least once, you've talked us out of building something customers didn't really need

  • You've left a part of the platform simpler than you found it

You'll probably thrive here if

  • You've taken something from zero to one: a company, a product line, or a side project with paying users

  • You've built and run backend systems in production that other people depend on. We care more about your judgment than your language; you're strong in Go or Python and happy to work in both

  • You're solid on data modeling, API design and messy real-world data

  • You'd rather talk to a customer than wait for a spec

  • You're comfortable with ambiguity. You can make progress while the problem is still half-defined, which at a startup it usually is

  • You want a large scope of responsibility and are happy to own things well beyond your job title

  • Rapidly changing requirements don't throw you. When customers or priorities shift, you adapt and keep going

  • You enjoy direct customer contact and want to be on customer calls

  • You make things simpler over time, not more clever

  • You write clearly in English. German is a plus, not a requirement

You probably won't enjoy it if

  • You just want to code and go home

  • You don't like talking to customers, whether on calls or on the occasional site visit

  • Ambiguity and chaos bother you

  • You want a well-defined backlog handed to you

  • Your main goal is managing people soon. Here, scope grows with what you own, not with headcount

Our stack

Go and Python (FastAPI), PostgreSQL, GCP, and LLMs throughout the document pipeline. You don't need to know all of it on day one.

How we hire

  1. Screening call (30 min) with our VP Engineering. It's two-way: ask us anything, including the hard questions.

  2. Technical deep-dive call: walk us through something you built from scratch, the decisions you made and what went wrong.

  3. Meet Scalera Day: join us remotely to work on a real problem with real (anonymized) construction documents, and meet the team.

  4. Offer: if it's a fit on both sides, we'll move quickly to an offer.

Working at Scalera

  • Remote within the EU or EEA

  • Small team, no bureaucracy. You'll work directly with the CEO, CTO, VP Engineering and Customer Success

  • Competitive compensation

Founders and former founders: if you're unsure whether you fit, send a few lines about what you built and why you moved on. We read every one.

If you've built something before, start here

Most ML jobs hand you a benchmark. This one hands you a business problem with paying customers and their real data. Construction tenders are long, messy and full of trade jargon, and every decision a customer makes on our platform becomes a labeled example you can train on.

We need someone who can turn that data into models that customers notice: from the first experiment to the model serving production traffic, and back again when a customer says it got something wrong. If you've founded a company (whether it worked out or not), been the first ML engineer somewhere, or shipped a model people paid for, this role was written for you.

About Scalera

Scalera is an ETH Zurich spin-off building AI for the €200B+ European construction industry. Manufacturers, wholesalers and suppliers in Switzerland, Austria and Germany still run their most document-heavy work by hand, from reading 300-page tenders to retyping purchase orders into their ERP. We automate that work one process at a time, and ML sits at the center of every one of them.

What you'll own

You'll own the ML behind our products, end to end. In practice that means:

  • Training and fine-tuning: embedding models, rerankers, classifiers and LLMs, trained on our own data.

  • Document understanding: models that pull structure, quantities and product specs out of tenders, orders and catalogs.

  • Product matching: retrieval and LLM agents that match tender positions to the right products.

  • Evaluation: offline benchmarks, per-customer evals and gates that keep a new model from shipping if it makes things worse.

  • Training and serving infrastructure: automated retrain pipelines, GPU serving and vector search in production.

  • Customer problems: when a model gets something wrong for a customer, finding out why and fixing it.

What success looks like after 3 months

  • There's a model or part of the pipeline people now think of as yours, and you're the one deciding what happens to it next.

  • You've spotted a problem nobody asked you to solve, made the case for it, and shipped a first version.

  • A model you trained runs in production, and customers can see the difference in their results.

  • Retraining runs automatically, and nothing reaches customers without passing an eval you designed.

  • You've cut LLM cost or latency by replacing an expensive step with a smaller model of your own.

  • You've decided at least one thing we should stop building.

You'll probably thrive here if

  • You've taken something from zero to one: a company, a model in production, or a side project with real users.

  • You've trained and fine-tuned models yourself, ideally embeddings, retrieval or document models, and evaluated them honestly on held-out data.

  • You've built with LLMs in production and know where agents fail.

  • You write strong Python and can run what you build: Docker, CI/CD, and cloud on GCP, AWS or Azure.

  • You measure before you believe, and a single aggregate score doesn't convince you.

  • You'd rather open a customer's actual document than wait for a spec.

  • You're comfortable with ambiguity. You can make progress while the problem is still half-defined, which at a startup it usually is.

  • You want a large scope of responsibility and are happy to own things well beyond your job title.

  • Rapidly changing requirements don't throw you. When customers or priorities shift, you adapt and keep going.

  • You enjoy direct customer contact and want to be on customer calls.

  • You write clearly in English. German is a plus, not a requirement.

You probably won't enjoy it if

  • You just want to code and go home.

  • You don't like talking to customers.

  • Ambiguity and chaos bother you.

  • You want a well-defined research agenda handed to you.

  • You'd rather hand a model to someone else to deploy and debug.

  • Your main goal is managing people soon. Here, scope grows with what you own, not with headcount.

Our stack

Python and PyTorch, open-weight and frontier LLMs, LangGraph, Langfuse, PostgreSQL with pgvector, Pinecone, and GCP. You don't need to know all of it on day one.

How we hire

  1. Screening call (30 min) with our VP Engineering. It's two-way: ask us anything, including the hard questions.

  2. Technical deep-dive call: walk us through a model or system you built, the decisions you made and what went wrong in production.

  3. Meet Scalera Day: come to our office in Zürich, work on a real problem with real (anonymized) tender data, and meet the team.

  4. Offer: if it's a fit on both sides, we'll move quickly to an offer.

Working at Scalera

  • Zürich HQ, four days in the office, Fridays remote. If not located in Zürich then this role is open to remote within the EU or EEA,

  • Occasional customer visits across Switzerland, Austria and Germany

  • Small team, no bureaucracy. You'll work directly with the CEO, CTO, VP Engineering and Customer Success

  • Competitive salary and meaningful equity

Founders and former founders: if you're unsure whether you fit, send a few lines about what you built and why you moved on. We read every one.
