title: Chief Customer Officer
description:
Work from anywhere, impact everywhere 

Diversity is at the heart of who we are at Xapo Bank.
We're a fully distributed team of over 160 Xapiens that work remotely from 50+ countries around the world.

Our beginning: A world that enjoys economic freedom and wealth protection,no matter where you live or who is running your country.
To achieve that, we search the world for the best people for the job.
We work hard, think globally, and inspire each other to learn and grow.
We are committed to changing the way things are done.

Although we are headquartered in Gibraltar, this is a full time, 100% remote position 
Work from anywhere!

Position overview

Xapo's product suite has grown from a Bitcoin vault into a full member proposition: BTC and USD accounts that pay interest, a global card with Bitcoin cashback, Bitcoin-backed loans, a growing suite of BTC wealth and credit products, and access to stocks, ETFs, and stablecoins, all inside one regulated relationship. 

Xapo is a bank, and a bank earns on the money its members choose to hold with it. Each of those products shipped well. What hasn't yet existed is a single owner of the economics of the customer relationship: one person accountable for winning the right members, growing what they hold with us, and keeping them, and for the balance-sheet products that make that possible.

The Chief Customer Officer is a new role at the top of the house, reporting to the CEO. You will run the stream that grows what members hold with Xapo, and you will own the Customer P&L, retail and institutional. It brings growth, client coverage, product management, and product design under one leader who is judged on customer contribution, the assets attracted and kept, and the members who stay. This is a customer-focused role in the most commercial sense: what a member earns from us, not the feature we shipped, is the centre of every decision.

The measure of success is a Customer P&L that grows on what members hold and keep: LTV:CAC improving, approved-to-paid rising, churn falling, and customer contribution the business can plan against.

This is a banking role, not a requirements-gathering role, a marketing role, or a role you can run from a dashboard. Products are priced on the balance sheet and judged on the money they attract and keep.

The mandate

  1. Own the Customer P&L, retail and institutional.
    You own customer contribution: customer gross profit from what members' balances earn, secured lending, Bitcoin yield, and conversion, stocks and ETFs, less the cost of winning and keeping members. We earn on what members hold, not on what they tap, send, or click, so you run on assets held and the margin they earn, not payment volume. Good looks like a Customer P&L the Exco and Board can plan against, where every line has a number you own and can explain, up or down.
  2. Grow what members hold with us, through earning products run like a banker would.
    You own the roadmap for the balance-sheet products: deposits and savings, lending and credit, and trading and structured. Each is led by a mission PM who is a banker, owning a product's contribution and its price on the balance sheet, not a backlog. Requirements go through the gate; the economics are the job. Every item is priced by Finance before it is built, on a shared risk appetite with Risk and Treasury. Good looks like products that scale assets held and member lifetime value at a risk profile the Board actually approved.
  3. Win the right members, efficiently.
    You own Growth: audience, lifecycle, and content, with one head accountable for the path from approval to paid. You own CAC and approved-to-paid, find the members who bring other members, and activate them in week one. Every incentive is priced before it runs. Good looks like net paid-member growth that improves every quarter, at a CAC that LTV comfortably justifies, because you diagnosed where the funnel leaks rather than spending more to fill it.
  4. Keep members, and deepen the relationship with the ones who hold balances.
    Retention is the most efficient growth we have. You own churn, and you own Client Coverage: relationship managers who sell the missions' products to the members who hold balances, and loop demand back into the roadmap. You are accountable for net new AUM flow, covered-book retention, and products per covered member, and for growth that is broad-based rather than concentrated in a few accounts. Good looks like falling churn and AUM growth from members who stay and expand rather than members re-acquired at cost.
  5. Make the value of Xapo visible, and the experience effortless.
    You own Product Design: one design system and one shell, so that members see the value of what they are earning clearly and early, and find every task simple. You design the proposition in the stream with Finance and partner with Operations, who run onboarding, KYC, support, cards, and payments, to remove friction at the points that affect members most. Good looks like members who understand their return, complete what they set out to do, and stay.
  6. Build one Customer organisation, not four.
    Growth, Client Coverage, Mission PMs, and Product Design come together under one operating model: one set of key results read weekly from one source, shared frameworks for discovery and prioritisation, and real career paths for the people in it. Engineering is pulled to a single ranked roadmap, and nobody in your line has engineers of their own. Good looks like fewer hand-offs per outcome and a number for every cell that its owner explains every week.
  7. Bring the regulated-bank and crypto-native lens to every customer call.
    You understand that a KYC onboarding decision and an AML monitoring decision carry different risk appetites, that a false positive at the gate is a paid-for member lost, and that a proposition built for a crypto-native power user can still fail a first-time bank customer. You can sit in the same room as a CRO, an MLRO, a CFO, and an engineering lead and make a customer case that survives all four conversations.

How you'll operate

This part matters as much as the mandate. The known failure mode for this role, in any company, is a CCO with a polished customer-insight deck and no ownership of the number. That is disqualifying here.

  • You lead from inside the work. You sit in on growth reviews, mission PM reviews, client meetings, and member calls, not just steering committees. PMs, designers, and relationship managers three levels down know your name because you've solved problems with them.
  • You move people with the business case, not the whip. When a priority needs to change, you diagnose the problem, build the case with data and the economics, and show teams why it matters, so they re-prioritise because they're convinced, not because they were told. Your authority comes from being right and being useful, not from your title.
  • You have extreme ownership. You own the Customer P&L and the member metrics beneath it, not the feature ship date. If a launch didn't move contribution, LTV:CAC, approved-to-paid, or churn, you don't report "the roadmap item shipped", you change the approach.
  • You have genuine gravitas. Senior, experienced leaders welcome your input because you've earned the standing to give it. You can challenge any executive's plan, including the CEO's, constructively, with evidence, and be thanked for it, because your challenge makes their work stronger.
  • You diagnose before you prescribe. You can walk into a leaking funnel, a churning segment, or a product that isn't earning and find the structural cause, then fix the economics, not just the symptom.

What you'll have done 

  • 10+ years in senior commercial or customer leadership (CCO, Chief Growth or Commercial Officer, MD or Head of Retail or Wealth, or equivalent) in digital banking, fintech, or payments, including meaningful time in a regulated environment (banking licence, e-money, or equivalent prudential/conduct regime).
  • Crypto-native credibility: hands-on experience building and growing customer propositions on or around digital assets, custody, on-chain flows, Bitcoin-backed lending, or similar. You don't need Bitcoin explained to you, and you don't need banking explained to you either.
  • Customer P&L ownership: you have owned a customer or product P&L judged on contribution, balances, and margin rather than transaction volume, and you are fluent in NIM, unit economics, customer contribution, and LTV:CAC.
  • Growth and lifecycle: a track record of acquiring, activating, and retaining members in a regulated, KYC-heavy environment, improving approved-to-paid and churn while holding CAC to a level that LTV justifies, not just growth-hacking a free consumer app.
  • Banking-grade product leadership: you have led product management for balance-sheet products such as savings, lending, or structured products, priced with Finance, with PMs who own a product's economics rather than a backlog. Experience with client coverage or relationship-managed models for high-balance and institutional clients is a strong advantage.
  • Commercial and risk fluency: you can build a customer business case that survives scrutiny from Finance, Risk, and Compliance in the same meeting, and you know the difference between growth that's sustainable and growth that's borrowed from tomorrow's risk appetite.
  • A track record of outcomes you can narrate: specific LTV:CAC, approved-to-paid, churn, AUM, or contribution numbers you owned, bets you killed when the data didn't support them, and outcomes you can prove.

 

The first 90 days

Day 30: The Customer P&L baseline is documented across retail and institutional: customer contribution, LTV:CAC, approved-to-paid, churn, net paid-member growth, and assets attracted and kept. You have formed your own independent view of where members are won, lost, and under-served, and shared it with the CEO and Board.
Day 60: The unified Customer operating model is live: one set of key results across Growth, Client Coverage, Mission PMs, and Product Design, read weekly from one source. Every mission PM owns a product's contribution and its price, and the roadmap is ranked on what it earns, built with Finance and the line leads.
Day 90: At least one measurable improvement in LTV:CAC, approved-to-paid, churn, or net new AUM flow is live and attributable to a change you made, not a feature ship, an outcome moved. Every cell in your line has defined key results and an owner who explains the number every week.

What this role is not

  • Not a requirements-gathering role. Mission PMs are bankers who own a product's contribution and price, not a backlog. You partner with Technology, Finance, and Operations on execution; you don't run those functions.
  • Not a volume role. If your primary output is card spend, transfer volume, or a shipped list rather than assets held and the margin they earn, we have both failed.
  • Not a reporting layer. If your primary output is a customer-insight deck or a roadmap deck, we have both failed.
  • Not a role that can be done from a distance. Remote-first means distributed, not detached.

Other requirements

  • A dedicated workspace.
  • A reliable internet connection with the fastest speed possible in your area.
  • Alignment with Our Values and the Xapo Values-Driven Leadership principles.

Why work for Xapo?

Impact Globally, Work Remotely.

  • Shape the Future
    Improve lives through cutting-edge technology, work 100% remotely from anywhere in the world.

  • Great work-life balance
    Build amazing things with a balance of autonomy and collaborative teamwork. Set your own work schedule and make use of a flexible PTO plan when you need to recharge. 

  • Expect Excellence
    Collaborate, learn, and grow with a high-performance team. Learn how you learn best - from books to conferences, you'll get a yearly budget for your individual learning and development goals.

At Xapo, we prioritize consumer protection and adhere to regulatory requirements by ensuring that all Xapiens are accountable for upholding principles of fair treatment, transparency, and ethical conduct in their interactions with customers and stakeholders.

title: DevOps Engineer
description:
In a world where geopolitical tensions and security threats are accelerating, the way nations protect people and preserve peace is being redefined. For a long time, innovating in defense was about making tougher hardware. But with the evolution of software and the recent AI disruption, the future of defense is shifting to software-powered unmanned systems that save lives by removing humans from the front line. This is our mission.

At Intelic, we're building the intelligence layer for unmanned systems in defense. As a software-first company, we enable autonomous platforms to operate together - faster, smarter, and more reliably - across complex, mission-critical environments. Our technology turns disconnected assets into coordinated forces, helping operators make accurate decisions when it matters most.

Based in Amsterdam and growing fast, Intelic offers a rare opportunity to work on products that don't just move metrics - they meaningfully impact safety, resilience, and the future of Europe's security.

Why This Role Exists

Nexus has to run in places most software never goes: offline, in the field, installed and operated by people who are not developers. Getting it there in one piece, and keeping it running, is a job on its own.

Right now that job sits mostly with three backend engineers who cover this alongside their own work. As Nexus grows, so does the team, and we're adding someone to take real ownership of the pipelines, installers, and infrastructure that turn Nexus into something operators can trust, and who treats security as part of how the work gets done, not a separate project bolted on afterwards.

What You Will Do

You will join Product Adoption, the team that owns the last stretch between working software and a field-ready product: deployment, installers, monitoring, and everything that keeps Nexus running once it leaves the building. We are hiring at medior to senior level, roughly a 2 to 3, with room to flex higher for the right person.

  • Build and maintain the CI/CD pipelines that turn Nexus into an installable, field-ready product across Linux and Windows

  • Maintain and harden our software supply chain, including dependency scanning and package security

  • Own the Windows installer and service orchestration, and help developers debug the platform-specific issues that come with it: permissions, firewalls, services, "works on my machine"

  • Secure the software update server, the one online touchpoint in an otherwise offline system, and keep telemetry from the field reliable without leaking sensitive data

  • Harden APIs and authentication on the surfaces that face the outside world

  • Maintain and gradually take over our on-prem infrastructure: physical servers, backups, and disaster recovery, as we move away from renting machines in the cloud

  • Build small internal tools, mostly in Python, Rust and shell or PowerShell scripts: installers, updaters, and the occasional internal or customer-facing web app

  • Support incident response when things break in production, and help build the monitoring that catches problems before customers do

  • Write down what you learn, so the next person, including future you, doesn't have to debug the same thing twice

You'll Thrive Here If

  • You bring solid experience with CI/CD pipelines and build automation

  • Comfort working across both Linux and Windows, with the ability to actually debug problems on either, not just deploy to them

  • Experience with infrastructure as code (Ansible, OpenTofu, or similar)

  • A security mindset: hardening, secure defaults, and attack surface are just part of how you build things, not an afterthought

  • Enough scripting or programming ability to read and contribute to Python, Rust, or shell scripts. There is there is plenty of custom tooling to build.

  • A level head under pressure. You can prioritise and stay steady when a few things break at once

Nice to have:

  • Experience with on-prem, bare-metal or virtulized infrastructure, not just cloud consoles

  • Familiarity with Docker

  • Exposure to dependency and package scanning tools such as Sonatype

  • An interest in platform or infrastructure engineering as its own discipline. We expect this to split into a dedicated function over time

  • Ability to build in-house tooling where needed and integrate vendor solutions where they fit

What Your First Year Will Look Like

  • You've taken over meaningful parts of the CI/CD pipeline and installer work independently, without needing step-by-step instructions

  • You've hardened at least one exposed surface end to end, the update server, an API, or similar

  • You've helped move part of our infrastructure off rented machines and onto hardware we run ourselves

  • Developers come to you when something breaks on Windows or Linux, because you've built a track record of finding the actual root cause

  • You've documented enough of what you know that the team is less dependent on any one person, including you

Why Intelic

  • We are setting up an environment, largely from the ground up that has to approved by MoDs

  • You won't be bored. New projects, new problems, and a steady stream of things nobody has solved here before

  • Real ownership from day one, not ticket-taking. If you see a better tool or approach, you're free to try it

  • You'll work with hardware that matters: servers you can walk up to, deployments running in places with no internet, problems that cloud-only engineers rarely see

  • A small team that leans on each other. When someone's on leave, the rest pick up the slack, and vice versa

  • The mission is real. Nexus supports operators in the field, and how well you build and secure it has a direct effect on whether it works when it counts

What We Offer

  • Stock Appreciation Rights programme (equity)

  • A vibrant office at NDSM Plein, Amsterdam Noord — where we come together in person every day, because we believe it matters for the kind of work we do

  • Flexible pension plan

  • 25 vacation days

  • Travel allowance

  • Urban Sports corporate membership

  • Lease a Bike option

Please note that, as part of our recruitment process, we may request a Certificate of Conduct (VOG) and conduct a background screening in accordance with our screening policy. We appreciate your understanding and cooperation throughout this process.

title: Senior Backend Engineer (Rust)
description:
About Intelic

In a world where geopolitical tensions and security threats are accelerating, the way nations protect people and preserve peace is being redefined. At Intelic, we're building the intelligence layer for unmanned systems in defense: software that enables autonomous platforms to operate together, faster, smarter, and more reliably, across complex, mission-critical environments.

Based in Amsterdam and growing fast, we offer a rare opportunity to work on products that don't just move metrics. They directly affect safety, resilience, and Europe's security.

Why the role exists

Our drones carry more and more hardware: cameras, gimbals, servos and more. The European market is fragmented, so we need to support many different types of hardware. Right now, adding a new piece of hardware usually means our own engineers have to integrate it. We want to change that. We're building a platform that lets partners and other teams connect their own hardware and write their own driver.

You'll work alongside robotics engineers and help set the team up from the start. The APIs and system design you create will be what everyone else builds on.

If you like hard backend problems where good design directly affects how fast other people can move, this role is worth a look.

Your impact

Credit, IRRBB and capital models sit at the heart of how a bank measures its own risk. Mollie already uses models in day to day processes, but nobody challenges them independently from a second line perspective yet. As Model Risk Officer, you'll help build the second line model risk function that gives Mollie, and its regulator, confidence that models can be trusted before they're used.

This is a true 0 to 1 role. Mollie isn't a bank today, so there's no model risk framework, validation methodology or model inventory to inherit. You'll design the policy, validation approach and governance from scratch, starting with the credit, IRRBB and capital models already in design for our future capital and liquidity planning. Your work feeds into our licence application and, once authorised, into how we manage model risk every day.

You'll also work with our Machine Learning team and the Domains already deploying models, so you can shape how we manage model risk today, not just in a banking future. Your challenge and sign off will be visible to senior leadership, audit and, eventually, our regulator. As Mollie grows and matures its model risk management, your scope grows from building the framework to running an ongoing model risk cycle.

What you'll ship

  • Build and own Mollie's model risk management framework and policy, including model risk appetite, validation standards and the model risk lifecycle.

  • Set up and maintain the model inventory for credit, IRRBB and capital models, with materiality and risk tiering for each.

  • Coordinate independent second line validation and challenge before models are used, including credit risk and ECL, IRRBB, and Pillar 1 and Pillar 2 capital models.

  • Design the ongoing monitoring and re-validation cycle with the Machine Learning team, covering performance testing, limitation tracking and re-validation triggers.

  • Partner with model owners in Credit Risk and Treasury ALM, and coordinate within the second line Risk function, so model risk challenge is built into the wider risk and capital frameworks.

  • Coordinate clear, well documented validation reports and model risk information that stand up to scrutiny from DNB/ECB, external auditors and internal audit.

What you'll bring

  • Around 5 to 7 years of experience in model risk management or model validation within a bank, preferably across at least one of credit, IRRBB and capital models.

  • Solid working knowledge of ECB model risk expectations and how model validation should be structured and evidenced.

  • Comfort building a model risk framework and validation approach from the ground up. You're excited to write the first playbook.

  • Strong quantitative skills to critically assess model methodology, assumptions and performance, and the discipline to document your findings so others, including a regulator, can follow them.

  • The ability to explain model limitations and validation findings to model owners and senior stakeholders, and the confidence to hold your ground under challenge.

  • Genuine curiosity about how AI can speed up the parts of model validation that don't need a human, so more of your time goes toward judgement and challenge.

Grow your way

At Mollie, growth is personal. We believe everyone should have the chance to develop their skills, explore new challenges and shape their career on their own terms.

You'll get regular feedback and performance reviews to support your development, with fair and transparent salary reviews along the way. Many Mollies move into new roles or take on new projects to stretch themselves, and we actively hire from within to help you take the next step.

No matter if you're aiming for promotion, exploring a different career path or building new skills, you'll be supported with the tools, trust and opportunities to grow your way.

title: Chief Investment Officer (CIO)
description:

Reporting directly to the CEO and working closely with the Executive Committee, Board and shareholders, the CIO will play a central role in shaping the future direction of SkyNRG. The Opportunity

The Chief Investment Officer will be responsible for leading SkyNRG's Investment Management capability and driving value creation across the business.

Working closely with the Executive Committee, Board and shareholders, the CIO will help shape the strategic direction of SkyNRG by ensuring investment decisions, capital allocation and growth initiatives are aligned with long-term value creation.

This role combines the analytical rigor of an investment professional with the strategic perspective of a business leader. It offers the opportunity to influence some of the most significant decisions facing the company while contributing directly to the development of projects and partnerships that support the future of sustainable aviation.

Your Role

You will:

  • Lead SkyNRG's Investment Management capability and establish the frameworks, governance and standards that support disciplined decision-making.

  • Further improve SkyNRG’s investment strategy, building on 17 years of SAF experience, network and track record, and the company’s overall strategic plans

You will oversee investment evaluations, valuation methodologies, business case development and portfolio prioritization to support informed decision-making at Executive Committee and Board level.

Portfolio Development

You will help maximize value across SkyNRG's portfolio by strengthening investment discipline throughout the project lifecycle.

Growth opportunities are expected to come from a combination of project development, strategic partnerships and selective corporate development initiatives.

You will play a leading role in identifying, assessing and executing opportunities that enhance SkyNRG's position within the sustainable aviation ecosystem and support the company's long-term ambitions.

You will collaborate closely with teams across Projects, Commercial, Finance, Legal and Strategy to strengthen how investment opportunities are evaluated and executed.

By embedding a common investment framework across the business, you will increase transparency, improve decision quality and support a culture focused on value creation and accountability.

Who we are looking for

We are looking for a strategic and collaborative leader with a strong track record in investment, infrastructure, energy or related capital-intensive industries. You are able to build trust across diverse stakeholder groups and bring people together around complex decisions.

You combine strategic thinking with strong commercial judgment and have experience evaluating complex investment opportunities in capital-intensive environments.

You are comfortable influencing senior stakeholders, engaging with boards and shareholders and navigating situations where commercial, financial and strategic considerations intersect.

You bring:

  • 15+ years of relevant experience in infrastructure, energy transition, project finance, private equity, corporate development or investment management.

  • A proven track record of evaluating and executing complex investment opportunities.

  • Deep expertise in valuation, financial analysis, capital allocation and investment decision-making.

  • Experience working with executive teams, Boards and institutional investors.

  • Strong leadership and stakeholder management capabilities.

  • The ability to balance strategic vision with pragmatic execution.

  • A genuine interest in accelerating the transition toward more sustainable aviation.

Based at SkyNRG's Amsterdam headquarters, this role offers the opportunity to work across an international network of partners, investors and project stakeholders that are helping shape the future of sustainable aviation.

We offer a flexible hybrid working model, recognizing that impactful leadership can be delivered through a combination of in-person collaboration, stakeholder engagement and remote working.

Why join SkyNRG

This is an opportunity to play a defining role in one of the most dynamic and ambitious companies operating within the sustainable aviation sector.

As Chief Investment Officer, you will influence investment decisions that shape the future of the company, contribute to the development of large-scale SAF projects and help create long-term value for shareholders, partners and the aviation industry as a whole.

You will join an entrepreneurial and mission-driven organization where commercial success and sustainable impact go hand in hand, and where your decisions will directly influence the growth trajectory of both the business and the broader SAF ecosystem.

About The Role

About the role

What You'll Do

What you'll do

Join activation and retention initiatives before anything is built, whether they come from CRM, growth or product. Define the primary metric, check against historical data whether the effect is detectable at our volumes, and turn solution-shaped requests into problem-shaped ones.

Design and analyse experiments end to end: hypothesis, guardrails, audience split, MDE and power, stopping rule, and a readout that ends in ship, iterate or kill. 

Correct for channel and engagement bias (not everyone opens email, and open and click populations are self-selected). When a clean A/B is impossible, use causal inference: diff-in-diff, matching, synthetic control or geo designs.

Build deliberately simple models: segmentation, propensity, churn and dormancy scoring. They feed audiences, personalisation and incentive targeting. You own the logic and the measurement of whether it beats the current rules.

Automate your own recurring work: audience refresh jobs, readout templates, dashboards for Activation, Onboarding and Retention. Your mission

About GENUINE

GENUINE is Europe’s leading TikTok Shop agency, and we’re right in the middle of the social commerce revolution. We don’t just make content. We build shopping experiences that sell, at the speed of a viral trend. We’re growing fast, and so does our Finance & Operations team.

About Ambio:

Ambio is the world’s first AI-native physical commodity trader. Our mission is to accelerate the transition to sustainable materials, and this mission is progressing fast in our first domain, recycled plastics.

We work closely with industrial manufacturers through the full procurement cycle, making sustainable material options an easy choice. With our AI-native approach and proprietary trading technology, we can offer the widest selection of recycled plastics on the market.

We’re a Helsinki-based startup with 19 employees in Helsinki, Berlin, and Stockholm, and funding from e.g. Lifeline Ventures, b2venture, and SpeedInvest.

More information about Ambio: https://ambiomaterials.com/

Position

Join Ambio’s Supply team to find, validate, and deliver recycled plastics to our growing customer base across Europe! We make sure our customers get the best recycled plastics to manufacture new products.

We do whatever it takes to drive customers’ success, and to grow our delivered volumes and our positive impact. We are continuously looking for great new materials and suppliers to complement our current offering - to then match them to new and existing customer needs.

This role is about leading our sourcing in France & BENELUX regions. It is a fantastic opportunity to work at the forefront of sustainable materials and operational-AI applications, and to make a difference in how circularity becomes reality. You will own and drive supplier cooperation, grow our supplier pool and build strong relationships, and ensure efficient delivery of high-quality materials. You also get to develop our software (the Ambio Platform) with our Product team to help us grow faster.

In your work, you will be given full ownership of what is in your responsibility, and the full support of the team to succeed in it.

Key responsibilities

  • Growth & Pace: You are the main driver together with our Sales team to drive our revenue growth - you are Supply owner for key accounts and projects.

  • Sourcing: You source suppliers and build business and long-term relationships between Ambio and them. You own your region, and you make sure we know the partners’ team, materials and production operations inside-out, ensuring high two-way trust and efficient sales and delivery.

  • Purchasing & Negotiation: You will ensure both high standards of service and quality assurance as well as a competitive price for Ambio’s customers. Your role is to excite partners to go the extra mile to meet our standards and service our demanding customers.

  • Product management: The whole Ambio team provides their expertise and context understanding of their function to the benefit of our Product team. You will support our software developers to make our service to our customer’s even more stellar, our pace of growth even faster, and your life easier.

Requirements

To excel in this role, we believe the ideal candidate:

  • Takes initiative, drives things forward without waiting for instructions, and turns ideas into action even when everything is not fully defined

  • Has a strong will to build, improve our company, and grow with it

  • Is excited to face new things daily and open to jump into new things, to meet new people and build a relationship with them

  • Likes to work with and talk to people, can communicate effectively and make our partners laugh and love working with us

  • Learns new things quickly, doesn’t hesitate in front of uncertainty, and adapts to situations

  • Can work independently and take full ownership of their work

  • Can keep their head cool and move forward steady even when adversity or problems arise

  • Is C2 or native-level in French & Dutch, and able to work in English. Other language skills are viewed as an asset (German, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese, Slavic and Baltic languages)

Typical recruitment process:

title: PR Manager DE
description:
A fight lasts minutes. A great story travels much further.

The comeback nobody saw coming. The rivalry that divides an arena. The person behind the fighter, with a story that deserves to reach people who have never watched MMA.

At OKTAGON, those stories are everywhere.

We’re building a sports brand with international ambitions, passionate fans and events that bring thousands of people together. Germany is a major part of that journey. And we’re looking for a PR Manager who knows how to make our stories matter to German media.

Someone who can earn the trust of a sports editor, spot an angle for a business title and understand why a digital format might reach an audience a traditional press release never will.

You’ll help decide which stories we tell, who we tell them to and how far they go.

Your stories need to travel beyond the cage.

Sports media will be your home ground. But your curiosity should take you further.

A fighter’s journey can belong in a mainstream interview. Our growth can start a business conversation. Training, personality and culture can open doors to fitness and lifestyle coverage.

You’ll find those opportunities and turn them into pitches that give each outlet a reason to care.

Here’s what you’ll take ownership of:

  • Build real relationships with German media. Develop and maintain a network across sports, digital and mainstream outlets. Get to know the journalists, their audiences and the stories they actually want.

  • Earn coverage for OKTAGON, our events and our fighters. Create opportunities around upcoming fights and recognise stories that deserve attention outside the event calendar.

  • Find new routes to our audience. Follow how the media landscape is changing, from digital publishers and podcasts to emerging editorial formats. Know where a story will work and adapt it accordingly.

  • Create sharp German press materials. Write press releases, translate and localise event Media Info Cards, research fight cards and prepare tailored angles for individual outlets.

  • Make interviews happen. Connect journalists with fighters, coordinate opportunities and prepare written interviews when needed.

  • Get the right assets into the right hands. Distribute photos, video and relevant information, including captioned fight photography for dpa-picture alliance and Imago.

  • Keep the foundations organised. Own accreditations, maintain the media database and keep fighter information accurate and up to date.

  • Show what your work achieves. Monitor online and offline coverage, prepare monthly reports and summarise results after German events. Use what you learn to improve the next campaign.

  • Keep our communication connected. Work closely with the PR lead, Marketing DE and Social Media so our messaging stays consistent, including across German-language video content.

When fight week starts, you’re in the middle of it.

The plans are ready. The journalists arrive. Interview requests change. A result creates a new headline.

You’ll be the person who keeps media operations moving.

At German events, that means overseeing accreditations and the media room, coordinating interviews, supporting weigh-ins and press conferences, and making sure journalists have what they need before and after the fights. Where needed, you may also moderate a press conference.

You’ll handle post-fight releases, follow-ups and coverage reviews. During selected events outside Germany, you’ll be available for relevant German media requests and breaking stories.

And when a sensitive situation comes up, you’ll be the first point of contact for German media, working closely with the PR lead on the response.

This role includes travel and weekend work. Fight weeks can run from Thursday through Sunday, and you need to be comfortable with the pace and responsibility that come with live events.

What you bring into the team

You already know how a newsroom works. You understand deadlines, editorial judgement and the difference between a story we want to tell and a story someone will want to publish.

We’re looking for:

  • At least 2–4 years of relevant experience in PR or sports journalism. You’ve pitched stories, worked with journalists and delivered under pressure.

  • An existing network in German sports newsrooms. Relationships you can build on, alongside the initiative to open new doors.

  • Native-level German and very good English. Your German writing is precise, natural and adaptable. You’re comfortable collaborating with an international team in English.

  • Strong editorial instincts. You can spot an angle, ask the useful question and turn a complicated story into a clear pitch.

  • Digital confidence. You understand how people discover and consume stories today and stay curious about what is changing.

  • Independence and ownership. You can organise your work remotely, follow through on commitments and keep colleagues informed.

  • Willingness to travel and work weekends. You want to be there when the action happens.

An interest in MMA or combat sports, experience with press conferences and crisis communication, and a driving licence are all advantages.

You don’t need to know every fighter’s record on day one. You do need the curiosity to learn the sport and understand the people in it.

Ready to tell the next story?

Send us your CV (English version) or LinkedIn profile and a few examples of your work: coverage you secured, a campaign you helped deliver or journalism you’re proud of.

Tell us what you contributed and why it worked.

We’d also love to hear what interests you about bringing OKTAGON’s stories to German audiences.

Let’s talk.

description:
You support a group of fellows through the AI Safety Fellowship, so that each one does strong work and leaves with a clear next step.

  • Salary: £86,750–£121,500 per year. We may be able to pay more for exceptional candidates.

  • Location: London, at our office at LISA

  • Hours: 0.5 to 1 full-time equivalent

  • Focus: From technical AI safety to AI governance possible

  • Visa: We can sponsor a Skilled Worker visa, but approval isn't guaranteed.

Why work at Pivotal

Pivotal finds people who can work on the biggest risks from advanced AI and gets them working on them. Since 2024, 135 fellows have taken part in our fellowships, and alumni now work at METR, Apollo Research, UK AISI and GovAI. We have grown from 2 staff in 2024 to 10 today, and we plan to reach at least 16 in 2027. Read more about us at pivotal-research.org, and about what it is like to work here.

What you will own

You'll be the Research Manager for about 6 research fellows, supporting each project from scoping through to publication. You'll collaborate closely with our whole research management team.

You'll engage deeply with your fellows' work: reading drafts, questioning experimental designs, suggesting framings, and helping projects stay ambitious but tractable. You’ll also hold the thread that keeps projects moving and fellows well supported.

The research support includes:

  • Run weekly 1:1 check-ins with each fellow; resolve bottlenecks quickly and adjust plans based on results.

  • Give clear, actionable feedback on drafts, figures, methodology, and experimental design.

  • Work with fellows and their mentors to scope projects that are both tractable and high-impact.

  • Coordinate mentors effectively: identify gaps in mentorship coverage and fill them yourself or through targeted introductions.

  • Help fellows with career planning, grant applications, and post-fellowship transitions.

  • Collaborate with the rest of the Pivotal team on infrastructure, and the overall fellowship experience.

Research management at Pivotal

As an individual researcher, you might advance one or two projects. In this role, you'll have a hand in about 6 projects simultaneously (and about 18 projects every year). Your leverage comes from making each fellow meaningfully more effective than they would be on their own.

The AI safety field still has a limited talent pipeline, and many of the people who will shape it over the next few years are early in their careers, still developing their research taste, and often short on high-quality guidance. This role sits at that bottleneck. You’ll help the next generation of researchers produce stronger work, find the right collaborators, and move into positions where they can have outsized impact.

If you get energy from seeing other people's work click into place, this role may let you shape the field more than you could as a single researcher.

Who does well in this role

We don’t expect candidates to arrive as fully formed research managers. We do expect strong potential, good judgment, and real motivation to grow quickly in the role. The traits & backgrounds below are signals we think may matter.

  • Research experience in AI safety, machine learning or AI governance, enough to judge whether a project is on track and to give useful feedback.

  • Good research taste: you can tell which projects matter and which are likely to stall.

  • Strong project management across many projects at once.

  • Ability to keep momentum across multiple projects simultaneously — balancing attention to detail with the ability to context-switch.

  • Care for people: fellows trust you and tell you early when things go wrong.

  • Clear, direct communication, in writing and in person.

  • A network in the AI safety field is a plus, because it helps with mentors and with fellows' careers.

We don’t expect anyone to be strong in all of this. If the role excites you, please apply, even if you match only part of what we describe here.

How we hire

We review applications as they come in, so applying early helps. The process has these stages:

  • Written application. A short form and your CV. It takes about 30 minutes.

  • Automated video interview. About 10 minutes. You record short answers to a few questions, at a time that suits you.

  • Work task. About 2 hours, based on real work in this role. We pay you for this time. You may use AI tools, as you would in the job. Tell us which ones you used and how.

  • Personal interview. About 45 minutes. We discuss your work task and how you would approach the role. With your consent, we record it so that more of the team can review it.

  • Work trial and references. Up to three paid days working with us at our office in London. We also speak to two referees, after asking you.

If you need an adjustment at any stage, such as extra time, tell us and we will arrange it. If you have questions, email ----- £86,750 – £121,500

🔍 The Opportunity:

Lottie is building the AI operating system for social care. Families find care through our marketplace. Care providers use Found to manage enquiries, occupancy and finances, with Eliza, our AI agent, answering family calls and chats on their behalf.

Lottie is growing fast. Care providers want what we're building, and we're heading into our next stage of growth. We need someone to get under the skin of the numbers, understand what's driving our success, and turn that into the plans, budgets and decisions that shape where we go next.

That's where you come in. You'll be the technical, commercially minded person at our CEO's side - writing the SQL, building the models and bringing the numbers that shape our biggest decisions. No middle man between the founder and the data: you go to the source yourself, work it out from first principles, turn it into a clear recommendation and then help make it happen.

With 2027 set to be Lottie’s most ambitious year yet, you'll own business planning and budgets, support investor relations and future M&A, and partner with teams across Lottie, including our commercial and marketing teams, to help them hit their goals. If you love both the data and the commercial story behind it, this is the role for you!

 

💻 What does this role involve?

  • Shape where Lottie goes next: Work directly with the execs on the biggest calls we make - pricing, where we invest, what we build - and own the analysis that decides them.

  • Sit at the heart of the business: Partner with Commercial, Marketing, Product, Ops and Finance to uncover what's really driving performance, and help each team act on it.

  • Own the financial model: Build and own the company's plans, budgets, forecasts and scenarios, track performance against them, and turn the variances into actions with the teams who own the numbers.

  • Board and investor numbers: Own the numbers for board packs and investor updates - clear, defensible and ready for scrutiny.

  • Turn insight into change: Take a question from analysis all the way to delivery, running it like a PM so the business actually moves.

  • Build, don't inherit: Use SQL, Python and AI to build the tools and processes a scaling company needs, from first principles.

💪 What problems will you be solving?

  • The data behind our success: Why is a new growth channel working so well, and how do we double down on it?

  • Pricing & unit economics: What drives margin in each product, and where pricing and packaging can lift it.

  • Board-ready numbers: Models, metrics and reporting that stand up to the scrutiny of investors.

  • M&A: Identify, evaluate and understand strategic acquisitions that accelerate Lottie growth.

  • Getting to the "why": Moving from what the numbers say to why they say it, and what we should do about it.

👀 We think you'll be a great fit if you…

  • Strong financial modelling: you can build a budget or forecast from scratch, read a P&L, balance sheet and cash flow, and turn it into a clear recommendation for Will. No FP&A title or accountancy qualification needed - a strong data or commercial background with real modelling depth is enough.

  • You are genuinely technical - you write your own SQL, work in git, are comfortable in Python and build financial models from scratch.

  • Work deeply with AI - you use tools like Claude every day to query data, build models and move faster.

  • Think from first principles and get quickly to how a business really makes money.

  • Can take a messy question, get to the data yourself and present a clear recommendation to a founder and leadership team.

  • Enjoy working closely with a founder - direct, curious and comfortable challenging up.

  • Are a builder, not just a modeller - you take a topic, run it like a PM and make it happen across the business at startup pace.

Sound like you but not quite 100%? Apply anyway - we're looking for potential and passion, not a perfect CV match.

 

💔 This role isn't for you if you...

  • Need someone else to pull the data. Here you write the SQL, build the model and own the answer.

  • Want to hand over a deck and walk away. We need someone who sees the decision through and makes the change happen.

  • Like analysis but shy away from action that comes from it. You'll be expected to make the call and defend it with the CEO and the leadership team.

  • Need a clear playbook and constant direction. Most of what you'll work on hasn't been done here before.

  • Want to stay in your lane. This role spans Growth, Product, Ops and Finance, often in the same week.

  1. First interview with Lottie's Talent Acquisition Lead - 20 mins (remote)

  2. Interview with Will Donnelly, Lottie's Co-Founder & CEO - 30 mins (remote)

  3. Technical interviews - SQL, Python and financial modelling (using AI tools is encouraged)

  4. Final interview with Will Donnelly in Lottie’s office.

  • Technical Interviews: If you are not successful after the technical stage, you'll receive constructive feedback via email and be offered a debrief call with our Talent Lead.

  • Final Interview: For final-stage candidates who are not offered the role, we will provide your feedback live via a phone call.

🚀 Meet Lottie

Founded with a mission to build the care sector of the future, Lottie is creating the AI operating system for social care - designed to unlock profitability for care providers and to make finding care as easy as booking a holiday on Airbnb.

Launched in London in July 2021, Lottie is widely recognised as one of Europe's fastest growing tech companies. Most recently, Lottie was the acclaimed winner of Deloitte Fast 50, LinkedIn Top Startups, The Sunday Times Tech 2026 and Startups 100.

As of today, Lottie offers three core products:

  • Lottie (B2B2C Marketplace) - Free service that helps families find the UK's best care homes and home care services.

  • Found by Lottie (B2B Vertical SaaS) - AI-native OS software supporting care providers to effectively manage their enquiries, occupancy and finances. Eliza by Found is our newest Found module: AI agents that handle care home enquiries - so no family goes unanswered. Launch video here.

  • Seniorcare by Lottie (B2B Vertical SaaS) - Employee benefit helping companies deliver outstanding eldercare support to their employees.

🤩 Why Lottie?

  • Career Opportunity - A career-defining opportunity to work side by side with our CEO on the data and numbers that shape Lottie's next stage of growth.

  • Early Hire Benefits - Be an early hire at one of the UK's fastest growing startups and benefit from fast career progression, as well as a generous stock options package.

  • Mission - Tech for good that aims to build the care industry of the future and to positively impact millions of people's lives. Care is one of the final remaining large consumer industries that is yet to be disrupted and positively revolutionised by technology.

Tech stack: FastAPI · Pydantic · TypeScript · React · OpenAI / Anthropic · PostgreSQL · Turbopuffer · Promptfoo · Azure

Modern tools, real-world impact in a regulated industry, and the chance to define how AI transforms aerospace from the ground up.

title: Design System Manager - Consultant.e
description:
Mindset
Chez Thiga, nous considérons qu’un Design System n’est pas seulement un ensemble de composants ou de règles : c’est un produit à part entière. Un produit pensé pour évoluer, répondre aux besoins des équipes, et accompagner la croissance de l’entreprise.
Créer et faire vivre un Design System demande une vision, une stratégie claire, et une gouvernance solide. Il faut piloter son adoption, anticiper ses usages à grande échelle, et s’assurer qu’il réponde aux enjeux à la fois du Design et de la Tech. C’est un levier puissant pour faire monter en maturité les organisations, structurer la collaboration entre les équipes, et diffuser une culture produit forte.

Aujourd'hui, un Design System bien structuré est aussi la condition sine qua non pour tirer
pleinement parti de l'IA dans les workflows design et prototypage. Tokens cohérents,
composants documentés, nomenclature rigoureuse autant de fondations qui permettent
d'exploiter les outils d'IA générative (Figma Make, Lovable, v0...) de manière fiable et scalable.
Le.la Design System Manager de demain est celui.celle qui anticipe ces usages et structure son système en conséquence.

Les Design System Managers que nous recherchons pensent leur système comme un produit
vivant, automatisé au maximum, et conçu pour connecter Design et Ingénierie dans un workflow
sans friction.

How we work together 🤝
  • Mettre en place des rituels d'adoption et d'amélioration continue :offices hours, sessions de feedback, contribution guidelines pour que le DS soit co-construit et adopté par toutes les équipes.
  • Aligner Design et Engineering en continu : organiser des syncs réguliers avec les équipes dev pour garantir la cohérence entre les composants Figma et leur implémentation code. Le DS ne vit pas dans Figma seul; il vit dans la production.
  • Piloter l'alignement stratégique multi-équipes : s'assurer que Produit, Tech, Design et business partagent la même vision et roadmap du DS, intégrée au même niveau que les autres produits.
  • Répondre aux besoins des utilisateurs et contributeurs : centraliser les demandes, prioriser les évolutions, et faciliter la contribution fluide de designers, développeurs et PMs.
  • Fédérer autour d'une culture DS partagée : faire du DS un produit vivant et co-créé, en favorisant des échanges transparents et en embarquant les équipes dans sa vision long terme

    • How we get work done 🚀
  • Définir et piloter la roadmap du DS : feuille de route alignée sur les priorités produit et business, avec des objectifs mesurables à court et long terme.
  • Automatiser les workflows du DS au maximum : pipelines de tokens, synchronisation design to code en temps réel, scripts de génération de documentation, réduire au minimum les tâches manuelles et les risques de désynchronisation.
  • Structurer le DS pour l'IA et le prototypage rapide : concevoir une architecture de composants et de tokens qui rende le DS exploitable par les outils d'IA générative (Figma Make, Cursor, v0, Lovable...). Cela implique : nomenclature stricte,variantes bien définies, props documentées, et une logique de composants qui s'aligne avec les patterns du code.
  • Garantir la cohérence design-code : mettre en place des outils de vérification automatique pour s'assurer que ce qui est designé est bien ce qui est développé sans avoir à le vérifier manuellement.
  • Promouvoir les bonnes pratiques à grande échelle : formations, ateliers, documentation vivante pour que le DS soit utilisé de manière fluide et scalable par toutes les équipes.
  • Mesurer l'impact et itérer : KPIs d'adoption, indicateurs de qualité, retours qualitatifs pour évaluer l'impact du DS et ajuster les priorités

    • How our work creates impact 🎯
  •  Accélérer le delivery produit : composants prêts à l'emploi, pipelines automatisés et prompts IA calibrés sur le DS. Les équipes conçoivent et développent plus vite, avec moins de friction
  • Rendre le prototypage IA fiable et scalable : un DS bien structuré devient le langage commun entre les designers et les outils d'IA les prototypes générés sont cohérents avec la prod, pas jetables
  • Garantir la qualité et la cohérence design à l'échelle : expérience utilisateur homogène, identité de marque renforcée, dette design et technique réduite
  • Réduire la dette et simplifier la maintenance : moins de doublons, moins de variantes inutiles, un code plus accessible et plus performant
  • Faire monter l'organisation en maturité design : culture de collaboration Design × Tech structurée, vision stratégique du design renforcée, documentation vivante comme levier de montée en compétence

    • Compétences 💼
  • Vision système et stratégie DS : u sais définir une stratégie de DS et la décliner en roadmap concrète, en alignement avec les priorités produit, tech et business. Tu fais preuve de leadership pour porter cette vision et embarquer les équipes.
  • Alignement Design-Engineering : tu as une solide compréhension des enjeux front-end (tokens, design-to-code, systèmes de composants) et tu dialogues en égal avec les développeurs pas seulement pour les convaincre, mais pour co-construire les bonnes solutions.
  • Automatisation et tooling DS : tu maîtrises les pipelines de tokens, les outils de documentation (Storybook, Zeroheight) et tu as une appétence pour l'automatisation des workflows DS.
  • IA et prototypage avancé : tu comprends comment un DS structuré permet de tirer parti des outils d'IA générative pour le design et le prototypage. Tu anticipes ces usages dans les décisions d'architecture du DS.
  • Gestion de produit interne : tu pilotes le DS comme un vrai produit : besoins utilisateurs, priorisation, KPIs, itération continue.
  • Communication et influence : tu sais formuler des livrables synthétiques et stratégiques (vision, roadmap, modèles de gouvernance, dashboards) pour aligner des interlocuteurs variés équipes opérationnelles, direction produit, stakeholders.
  • Outils : figma (Variables, Dev Mode, Make), Storybook, Zeroheight, Notion, Jira/Linear, Style Dictionary, et une bonne aisance avec les environnements no-code/low-code et outils IA de prototypage.
  • Anglais courant : à l'écrit comme à l'oral

    • Qualités 🌟
  •  Tu penses en systèmes : tu comprends les logiques systémiques et sais structurer un DS cohérent, extensible, et exploitable par l'IA
  • Tu automatises par réflexe : tu cherches à réduire les tâches manuelles et à construire des workflows robustes qui s'auto-maintiennent.
  • Tu es le pont entre Design et Tech : tu parles les deux langages et tu sais créer les conditions d'un alignement durable entre les équipes.
  • Tu portes une vision : tu es capable de convaincre, d'aligner et d'embarquer des designers comme des ingénieurs, des opérationnels comme des dirigeants.
  • Tu pilotes ton DS comme un produit : besoins utilisateurs internes, KPIs, roadmap priorisée tu traites le DS avec la même rigueur qu'un produit client.
  • Tu restes curieux·se et en veille : sur les outils, les pratiques et l'évolution rapide des Design Systems et des usages IA dans le design

    • Expérience 📇
  • Tu as au moins 5 ans d'expérience en Product Design, Design System Management ou un
    rôle similaire, avec une trajectoire confirmée ou senior
  • Tu as déjà créé ou fortement structuré un Design System de zéro ou à grande échelle, pas
    seulement contribué à l'un
  • Tu as mis en place des pipelines de tokens, des processus d'automatisation et des
    intégrations design to code
  • Tu as expérimenté avec des outils d'IA générative, dans un contexte design ou DS (Figma
    Make, Cursor, v0, Lovable, ou équivalent)
  • Tu as travaillé aussi bien en scale-up qu'en grand groupe, ce qui te donne une bonne
    lecture des modèles d'organisation et des leviers pour faire évoluer la maturité design.
  • Tu as travaillé en méthodologie agile et sais comment intégrer le DS dans ces processus de
    delivery.

    • Ce que nous offrons 🎊
  • Un on-boarding pour rencontrer tes collègues 
  • De l’apprentissage avec minimum 5 jours de formations à l’année, des sessions de partage hebdomadaires et du contenu pour te faire monter en compétences
  • Du mentoring sur ta mission par un pair plus confirmé 
  • Du confort avec deux jours de télétravail par semaine (selon ton client) complétés par un accès à un catalogue de matériels, ainsi qu’un Macbook Air ou un PC selon ta préférence.
  • Du fun avec des Thigapéros, des Team building et un séminaire (en prêtant attention à notre empreinte carbone).

title: Senior Security Engineer
description:
About Kestra

Kestra is the universal orchestration platform: open source, declarative, and designed to orchestrate data pipelines, IT automation, business workflows, and AI/agentic systems.

Trusted by over 10,000 organizations worldwide, including JPMorgan Chase, Bloomberg, FILA, and Crédit Agricole, Kestra orchestrates mission-critical workloads at scale. The open-source project has close to 30,000 GitHub stars, hundreds of contributors, and a fast-growing global community.

About the role

Kestra runs arbitrary, user-defined code at scale. Our users write workflows that execute scripts, containers, and queries against their own production systems, through hundreds of community-built plugins, on a platform whose entire source code is public. That is an unusually rich attack surface, and securing it is a genuinely hard engineering problem rather than a checklist exercise.
You would be our first dedicated security hire. We're looking for a Senior Security Engineer to own and elevate the end-to-end security posture of our platform, infrastructure, and open-source ecosystem.
This is a unique, hybrid role for someone who excels at both sides of security: actively breaking systems to find vulnerabilities (hands-on penetration testing) and actively fixing them (opening PRs, patching infrastructure, and managing supply chain risks). If you want to build a world-class security foundation for a fast-growing open-source and SaaS platform, this role is for you.
This is a hands-on engineering role, not a GRC or compliance one.

What you would do

Your first six months would focus on the first three points below. The rest is where the role grows.

  • Conduct hands-on penetration testing and threat modeling across our web application, APIs, control plane, and cloud environments.

  • Manage end-to-end vulnerability tracking across our codebases, software dependencies (SCA), container images, and cloud infrastructure.

  • Proactively fix security flaws by writing patches, submitting Pull Requests (PRs), or collaborating directly with product teams to guide remediation.

  • Audit and harden our cloud infrastructure (GCP, Kubernetes clusters, and networking configurations) against external and internal threats.

  • Automate security tooling into our CI/CD pipelines (SAST, DAST, dependency scanners) to catch CVEs before code reaches production.

  • Perform security code reviews and evaluate third-party dependencies, open-source integrations, and supply-chain risks.

  • Lead incident response efforts and establish continuous monitoring, detection, and mitigation strategies.

  • Own our public security posture as an open-source project: vulnerability disclosure process, CVE handling, security advisories, and the trust model of our plugin ecosystem.

Our Tech Stack

  • Security & Vulnerability Tools: Trivy, GitHub Security / Dependabot, Elastic Security

  • Infrastructure: Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform

  • Cloud: GCP

  • Programming language: Java, Typescript, Javascript

  • Datastore: PostgreSQL, Elasticsearch

  • Queuing: Redis, Kafka, AMQP

  • Monitoring & Logs: ELK, Prometheus, Grafana

  • Deployment & Repository: GitHub Actions, ArgoCD

What we are looking for

  • 5+ years of experience in Security Engineering, Product Security, DevSecOps, or a combined Offensive/Defensive role.

  • Strong hands-on penetration testing background, with proven ability to discover application, API, and network-level vulnerabilities.

  • A builder/fixer mindset: You don't just export scanner PDFs; you can read code, understand exploits, write fixes, or provide clear remediation steps to engineers.

  • Deep familiarity with cloud security (AWS or GCP) and containerized environments (Kubernetes, Docker).

  • Experience with dependency and supply-chain security (CVE management, open-source licensing, SCA tools).

  • Fluent in English and comfortable working autonomously in a fully remote environment.

  • Adaptability to a fast-paced open-source startup environment where pragmatism and execution speed matter.

Perks & Benefits

  • Work from anywhere: We’re a remote-first company, so you can work from wherever feels like home. Plus, you’ll have access to coworking spaces worldwide if you ever need a change of scenery.

  • Health coverage: From medical support, dental, and vision, we've got you covered.

  • Home office setup on us: We’ll provide all the equipment you need to work comfortably.

     

Our Hiring Process

We aim to move quickly (2-3 weeks), but we can adjust the timeline if needed.

  • Intro call with the hiring manager (30 min)

  • Technical scenario / Practical assessment (2 hours, asynchronous homework focusing on threat assessment and remediation)

  • Team chat with one of your future colleagues (30 min)

  • Final discussion with one of our co-founders (30 min)

Streaming TV is no longer just a brand awareness channel. It’s becoming a core part of the performance marketing mix, alongside search and social. Vibe.co is building the platform that makes TV work like the rest of the acquisition stack: targeted, measurable, and optimized for results.

Vibe.co is an Audience First Streaming TV Advertising platform that gives marketers the tools to reach the right audiences, optimize campaigns in real time, and understand what’s actually driving business outcomes. With hyper-targeted segmentation, AI-powered recommendations, real-time optimization, and incrementality measurement, Vibe brings the precision and accountability of digital advertising to the biggest screen in the house.

Today, more than 12,000 brands use Vibe.co to reach 120 million+ households. And in August 2026, Vibe.co became a Walmart company, opening up a new chapter for the business and the industry. With Walmart’s first-party data and purchase signals now part of the Vibe platform, advertisers can connect TV advertising to real-world transactions and measure the impact of CTV with a level of precision previously associated with platforms like Google and Meta.

This is a unique moment to join Vibe. With Walmart’s scale, data, and reach behind us, we’re building the next generation of TV advertising and creating a more measurable, performance-driven future for the channel.

About the Role

You'll be Vibe's founding security hire. Security has been part of how we build since day one and we're already SOC 2 Type 2 compliant, but nobody has owned it full-time. Ad spend and headcount have both roughly doubled every year since 2022, enterprise partnerships keep expanding, and the more visible Vibe becomes, the more scrutiny comes with it. Now it needs an owner.

You'll define the risk model, set the roadmap, decide what we harden and what we accept, and turn policies into running procedures in code on the paths engineers and AI already use. That work happens in a cloud native ecosystem across AWS and GCP, with most of our services running on Kubernetes, everything as code and a GitOps deployment model.

Reporting to our, Head of Infrastructure, and joining a lean six-person Infrastructure and IT team. You won't do it alone, but you'll be the main contributor, and the person every team turns to on security. Since we joined forces with Walmart, you'll also coordinate directly with their cloud security teams.

What You'll Do

Risk & Governance

  • Map Vibe's risk model across every major system.

  • Set the security roadmap with clear priorities.

Security Engineering

  • Pave the road with guardrails and secure defaults enforced across the engineering tool set.

  • Ship the golden paths so the safe way is the easy one.

  • Harden security across our cloud native ecosystem (AWS and GCP) and third-party providers.

  • Own access management from onboarding to offboarding, and get it to the point where it runs without you.

Detection & Response

  • Prioritize vulnerability findings by real exposure, assign them to the team that owns the code, and follow remediation through to closure.

  • Own security incident response from detection through resolution.

  • Turn manual processes into pipelines that run on their own.

  • Launch and run Vibe's private bug bounty program.

Trust & Compliance

  • Own SOC 2 compliance end to end and maintain current certification.

  • Drive Vibe's future compliance initiatives and requirements.

  • Define Vibe's security posture and make it self-serve so enterprise deals clear security without routing through you.

Security Culture

  • Set clear, practical rules for safe AI use, built into the tools themselves, covering both the AI we ship in our products and the AI our teams work with every day.

  • Run security awareness training and measure behavior changes so the whole company raises its bar.

What You Need

  • Built a security function as a company's first security hire.

  • Write code comfortably and bring deep cloud-native security experience.

  • Managed a compliance framework at scale, such as SOC 2, ISO 27001 or HIPAA.

  • Managed AI security risk hands on, both in what a company ships with AI and in how its employees use it day to day.

Nice to Haves

  • Ran a private bug bounty program.

  • Ad tech security background, including exposure to US privacy law (CCPA/CPRA, VPPA) in a data-heavy environment.

  • Navigated security through a company acquisition.

Our Values

At Vibe, we run on three values: Impact, Ambition, and Urgency. We tie every goal to a real business outcome, think 10x rather than settling for good enough, and move daily rather than waiting for perfect conditions.

You'll thrive here if you own outcomes without needing direction, default to action, and hold yourself to results, not effort.

This is a high-performance environment with high-performance rewards: you'll work alongside people who push you, with real ownership over hard problems in a market that's moving fast.

If that sounds like the best version of your career, we want to meet you.

What We Offer

The pay range for this role is €127,000-€171,000. We will support relocation to Paris for great candidates.

At Vibe, we want you to build something, own something, and grow fast. Here's how we back that up:

  • Variable pay — Based on real Vibe business goals.

  • Hybrid flexibility — We're in the Heart of Paris and our team is in 3x a week!

  • Health insurance — Full coverage via Alan.

  • Meal vouchers — Via Swile.

  • Annual offsite — The whole team, once a year, somewhere worth the trip.

  • Tech Syncs — Engineering and Product meet in person at least quarterly, worldwide.

Our Interview Process

We respect your time. Here's exactly what to expect, no surprises, no ghosting.

  1. Recruiter Screen — 30 minutes. We’ll share more context on the role and team, and learn more about your background and what you’re looking for.

  2. Hiring Manager Interview — 45 minutes. Meet with the person you’d work with directly and dive deeper into your experience, technical background, and approach to the role.

  3. Technical Assessment — 90 minutes. A deeper technical conversation covering core engineering skills, problem-solving, and a technical use case relevant to the role.

  4. Bar Raiser Interview — 30 minutes. Meet with a senior leader at Vibe for a final conversation and an opportunity to ask any remaining questions.

  5. Offer — We move quickly once we’ve made a decision. We don’t let good decisions sit.

Equal Opportunity

Vibe is an equal opportunity employer. We evaluate all applicants without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

We believe the best ideas come from teams with different backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences. If you need a reasonable accommodation during the application or interview process, please let us know.

title: Stage M2 : Recherche en optique non linéaire appliquée à la caractérisation de dispositifs électroniques neuromorphiques - 6 mois
description:
Mines Saint-Etienne est une Ecole de l’Institut Mines-Télécom (IMT), 1er groupe public d’écoles d’ingénieurs et de management en France. L’IMT est un EPSCP (grand établissement) sous la tutelle du Ministère de l’Économie, des Finances et de la Souveraineté Industrielle et Numérique.

L’École Nationale Supérieure des Mines de Saint-Étienne (Mines Saint-Etienne) est chargée de missions de formation, de recherche et d’innovation, de transfert vers l’industrie et de culture scientifique, technique et industrielle.

Mines Saint-Etienne représente: 2 400 élèves-ingénieurs et chercheurs en formation, 480 personnels (150 Chercheurs et Enseignants-chercheurs), un budget consolidé de 46 M€, 3 campus dédiés à l’industrie à Saint-Etienne et Lyon (région AURA), à la microélectronique et aux objets connectés à Gardanne (Métropole Aix-Marseille Provence, région SUD) et à l’ingénierie pour la santé à Saint-Etienne ; 6 unités de recherche ; 5 centres de formation et de recherche ; un centre de culture scientifique technique et industrielle leader en France « La Rotonde » (> 50 000 visiteurs / an).

 

Contexte scientifique et objectifs du stage :

Des dispositifs d’électronique organique ultra-flexibles, conformables et implantables incorporant une intelligence artificielle promettent de révolutionner la surveillance et le traitement en temps réel de maladies chroniques [1]. De tels systèmes pourraient être basés sur des transistors organiques électrochimiques (OECTs), exploitant des conducteurs polymères mixtes ion-électron (PMIECs) comme couches actives. En effet, les PMIECs sont apparus comme une excellente plateforme matérielle pour interfacer la biologie avec l’électronique conventionnelle ; identifié comme le domaine de la « bioélectronique organique ou plastique ». L’OECT est considéré comme l’éléments clé pour réaliser une telle interface [2]. Son efficacité est évaluée suivant des figures de mérite (FoMs) telles que i) la transconductance (gm), et/ou ii) les temps de commutation (ionique vs. électronique) dans le dispositif. Au-delà des applications de transduction, à court terme, l’OECT est aussi intéressant pour créer des applications émergentes en matière de circuits neuromorphiques bioélectroniques [3].

La réalisation de tels circuits est freinée par un manque de compréhension et d’optimisation des processus de conduction mixte dans ces matériaux polymériques ; notamment une asymétrie des temps de commutation des transistors lors des séquences de dopage (i.e « ON ») vs dédopage (i.e « OFF ») dans le canal de l’OECT. Des outils de caractérisation in-situ & operando permettant de quantifier et cartographier les paramètres de transduction électronique et électrochimique dans le canal de l’OECT se révèlent être indispensables pour comprendre les limitations actuelles en performances des PMIECs et/ou pour construire des PMIECs optimums dans de tels circuits neuromorphiques.

 

Dans ce contexte scientifique, le.la stagiaire développera une nouvelle mesure de spectroscopie et instrumentation d’optique non linéaire, appelée microscopie par génération de second harmonique résolue en temps, afin d’enregistrer le mouvement spatio-temporel des espèces chargées, ion et électrons (ou trous), et ainsi donc cartographier les mobilités électroniques in-situ & operando le canal de l’OECT.

La.le stagiaire fabriquera ces dispositifs OECTs en salle blanche de microélectronique, et bénéficiera d’un accompagnement technique pour leur réalisation. Il.elle enregistrera et analysera les FoMs clés grâce à l'expérimentation d’optique non linéaire développée et aux caractérisations électriques et électrochimiques afin d’établir, de manière plus globale, des règles d’ingénierie dans ces PMIECs qui serviront de socle de connaissances incontournables à l’avenir, pour mettre en œuvre et appliquer des circuits neuromorphiques à base d'OECTs, comme première brique d’une intelligence artificielle d’électronique organique.

description:

Together, we imagine and build a sustainable future by educating the leaders who will shape tomorrow’s transitions.

🎯 What we expect from you

As a Postdoctoral Researcher or Research Engineer, you will perform research and innovation activities in the field of soft electronics and optical sensing for artificial skin applications. Within the Centre of Microelectronics and the Flexible Electronics Department (FEL), you will contribute to the development of stretchable optical waveguides and their integration into artificial skin demonstrators.

The flexible electronics department develops technological and scientific knowledge in the field of soft electronics. The department has a strong knowledge in the field of material and interface electrical and mechanical characterization. The activities of the department are regrouped in the 660m2-area platform. This technological platform regroups facilities and technological equipment for R&D activities in Micropackaging, micro and nano-electronics, in a clean room of 220m² 1000-class and 400m² 10000-class.
