  • Real ownership. Meaningful equity and a direct hand in how Qorelo runs in the field. We are looking for people who want to shape a company, not join one.

  • Competitive salary, benchmarked for senior customer-facing technical talent in Berlin.

  • The problems. Fortune 500 and DAX 40 production landscapes, including Mercedes-Benz. You work at the core of SAP systems most engineers never get to touch.

  • The team. Short paths, fast decisions, and a direct line to our CTO, our founding engineer and our solution architects.

  • 25 days paid vacation + German public holidays.

  • Company offsites with the whole team.

Our Senior Talent Partner has moved into the Head of People and Talent role, so we're looking for someone to take over day-to-day hiring processes for the whole company. We're growing across every team, and you'll be the person who makes sure each of them gets great people when they need them.

Roughly half your roles will be in engineering and half in other functions, so one week you're calibrating an engineering loop and the next you're hiring for sales or operations. The other part of the job is building a talent community around WunderGraph. We're an open-source company with a real developer community, and hiring should draw on that. Events, content, memes, a community experiment that might not work: you'll have room to try things, and we'd rather you tried.

One thing this isn't - a sales role. We don't need someone to push candidates over the line. We need someone who tells our story honestly and specifically enough that the right people lean in and the wrong ones opt out early. That includes the less glamorous parts, like a small distributed team and meetings that stretch into your evening so we can work with the US.

  • Reports to: Head of People and Talent

  • Collaborates closely with: every hiring manager across engineering and non-engineering teams, plus the CEO, COO, VP of Sales and our engineering principals on key hires

  • Acts as each hiring manager's partner on a search, not an order-taker: shaping the brief, setting the bar together, and holding the process to it

You are succeeding if:

  • Hiring managers across engineering and non-engineering teams get strong shortlists when they need them, not a quarter later.

  • Regardless of source, the candidates are some of the best talent around, rather than people who happened to apply - and you can recognise the difference.

  • Candidates keep telling us ours is the best hiring process they've been through, including the ones we don't hire. You keep it that way as we hire more.

  • Hiring managers trust your judgement enough to change their minds when you push back on a brief, and leadership trusts the plan because your hiring metrics are clear.

  • Our hiring processes are better because you changed them, not just because you ran them.

ROLE TASKS

The role focuses on, but is not limited to:

Full-cycle recruiting

  • Running multiple searches at once across engineering and non-engineering teams, from intake to accepted offer, prioritised by urgency

  • Running role kickoffs with hiring managers to agree outcomes, competencies and the interview loop

  • Writing job profiles and adverts with the People team, tailored to each audience

  • Pre-screening candidates and sharing shortlists with a clear recommendation

  • Coordinating interviews and running debriefs, with blind scorecards in Ashby before any group discussion

  • Keeping every candidate updated, with no one waiting more than 3 days to hear from us

  • Managing offers and closing candidates honestly, without pressure, ensuring each conversation with the candidates is meaningful and insightful for both us and the candidate.

Sourcing

  • Finding and engaging people who aren't looking, through sourcing, open-source projects, communities, meetups and conferences

  • Headhunting directly for senior and hard-to-fill roles

  • Writing outreach specific enough to each person that they actually reply

  • Keeping warm pipelines for roles we hire repeatedly

Stakeholders and reporting

  • Advising hiring managers on market realities: who's available, what they expect, and what that means for the brief

  • Keeping leadership updated with clear hiring metrics and progress

  • Escalating blockers early, with a proposed fix

Talent community and employer marketing

  • Building a community of people who know WunderGraph before they ever see a job post

  • Running creative, low-budget activity: events, content, community-led hiring, the odd meme that lands

  • Working out what worked, and dropping what didn't

Hiring process

  • Documenting our recruitment workflows so they don't live in one person's head

  • Keeping hiring compliant across the countries we hire in, and handling contracts, background checks and documentation with the People team where needed

  • Keeping our hiring data and Ashby setup useful for planning, not just record-keeping23w

Bonus points

  • You've hired in, or for stakeholders in, the US market.

Why WunderGraph?

  • Pick your preferred work hardware

  • We focus on getting stuff done, and on having fun whilst doing so: work hard, play hard!

What you will own:

1. Third-party security assurance

- Run security due diligence on new suppliers, maintain initial questionnaire to risk sign-off, working with Procurement and Legal on security and data protection schedules.

- Maintain a supplier tiering model based on criticality and run the periodic re-assessment cycle for tiered suppliers: certification expiry, subprocessor changes, breach notifications, SLA performance.

- Maintain the supplier and outsourcing registers, including preparation for the FCA's material third party register under PS26/2 (rules in force 18 March 2027).

- Track concentration risk and exit plans for critical suppliers.

2. Inbound due diligence and customer assurance

- Own our response to security due diligence from funders, banking partners, institutional investors, commercial partners and prospects.

- Build and maintain a reusable trust pack: answer library, security whitepaper, current certifications, pen test attestations, standard questionnaire pre-fills (SIG, CAIQ).

- Turn a 40-hour bespoke questionnaire response into a 4-hour one.

3. The assurance calendar

- Maintain the annual calendar of security activities and make sure each one happens, produces evidence, and closes its actions: penetration tests, access reviews, disaster recovery tests, tabletop exercises, policy reviews, supplier re-assessments, awareness training.

- Coordinate external penetration tests: scoping, vendor selection, scheduling, findings triage, remediation tracking, retest.

- Facilitate tabletop exercises, including scenario design and post-exercise action tracking.

4. Risk and control administration

- Maintain the information security risk register: run the assessment cycle, record treatment plans with named owners and dates, chase closure.

- Administer the policy exception and risk acceptance process, ensuring every exception is owned, time-bound and reviewed on expiry.

- Perform first-line control testing: sample-test where key controls operate as designed and retain the evidence.

- Produce security MI for the Head of Security to take to ExCo and the Risk Committee.

5. Vulnerability and findings management

- Consolidate findings across sources — EDR, cloud security posture, SAST/DAST/SCA, secrets scanning, penetration tests — into a single view with agreed severity definitions and remediation SLAs.

- Triage, route and chase remediation with engineering teams; escalate ageing findings.

- Own the reporting on remediation performance.

6. Security awareness

- Run the awareness programme: induction, annual refresher, phishing simulation, role-based training for engineers, completion tracking.

- Coordinate pre-employment screening with People.

- Incident response: you will maintain the IR plan and playbooks, facilitate post-incident reviews, track remediation actions, and support regulatory notification (ICO personal data breach reporting within 72 hours; FCA notification under Principle 11 / SUP 15.3).

- Business continuity and DR: you will maintain the documentation and the testing evidence.

- Secure development: you will help embed security requirements into the SDLC and support threat modelling sessions.

- Data protection: you will support RoPA maintenance, DPIA completion and DSAR handling alongside Legal.

What success looks like:

First 90 days: you know our supplier estate and have tiered it; the assurance calendar for the next 12 months is published and owned; inbound due diligence requests come to you and go out without the Head of Security rewriting them.

Six months: the trust pack exists and is being used; the risk register is live with owned treatment plans; ISO 27001 evidence collection is systematic rather than a scramble; the exception register exists.

The Role

We are hiring a Product Lead to own our Express / Mid-prime personal loan product, one of our highest-priority growth areas. This is unsecured personal lending in the higher-APR mid-prime space (30% to 50% APR), with loans typically from £2,000 to £10,000, and customers acquired primarily through price-comparison and aggregator marketplaces. Our ambition is to grow this product many times over while improving its economics, and this role owns the product that makes that happen.

This is a product role first. You will own the Express/Mid-prime proposition end to end: who we serve, how we quote and present offers on marketplaces, how the journey converts, how we price, and how the product performs once the loans are on the book. What makes it different from a typical product role is that the product is credit. The levers that drive growth, such as eligibility, pricing, offer design and underwriting, are the same levers that drive loss rates, so you need to be comfortable working with risk and data science rather than handing that part off.

We think this is a great role for someone with around four to five years of experience who has built a strong foundation in lending or fintech, has worked hands-on with data and credit decisioning, and is ready to own a product outright rather than a slice of one. You will set the direction for the segment, run the roadmap, and be accountable for the results, with the backing of experienced risk, data science and commercial leaders around you.

Our decisioning is built on Open Banking and cashflow underwriting rather than credit scores alone. For a higher-APR population acquired through marketplaces, seeing real affordability is what lets us select and price better than the market. The interesting product problem is that richer data comes at a cost to conversion, so the job is to capture that data advantage while designing a journey and offer that customers actually complete.

The defining challenge is balance: scaling volume by an order of magnitude while building a book of genuinely good credit quality. The best people in this space know that those two goals can be reconciled rather than traded off, and are curious enough to work out how.

  • Understand and actively manage adverse selection in marketplace-acquired lending, shaping offer, pricing and decisioning strategy to attract the customers we want and screen out the risk we do not.

  • Work with data science to make sure our credit models are calibrated and tuned for this population rather than inherited unchanged from prime or adjacent segments, and be able to get into the data yourself when needed.

  • Use credit and commercial insight to optimise unit economics, balancing approval rates, pricing, loss rates and volume so the product scales profitably.

  • Monitor product and portfolio performance across the customer lifecycle, spotting emerging trends, risks and opportunities early.

  • Design and evaluate experiments and strategy changes, and turn the analysis into clear, actionable recommendations.

  • Own the management information for the segment: define the metrics, monitoring and reporting that let the business make consistent decisions about the product.

  • Assess new initiatives, customer segments and product changes with both a commercial and a credit lens.

  • Present clear, structured updates on product performance to senior leadership and governance forums, and support funding and due diligence conversations where the product is in focus.

  • Credit-literate. You understand how eligibility, pricing and underwriting decisions shape the book you end up with, and you have a working understanding of adverse selection and why it matters in marketplace lending.

  • Commercially sharp, with a solid grasp of unit economics and a clear understanding that product decisions in lending have to work for both growth and portfolio performance.

  • Curious about trade-offs rather than defensive about them: alert to the fact that deeper affordability assessment can hurt conversion, and motivated by the challenge of capturing its value without sacrificing growth.

title: (Senior) Data Systems Lead
description:
Help us make a big green dent in the universe. We're on a mission to drive the global renewable energy revolution, and we need many more people to help us make our vision a reality. 

Octopus Energy Generation (OEGEN) is a leader in sourcing, investing in, and managing a wide range of utility-scale renewable energy assets. As we continue to expand our investment base, we are dedicated to building a diverse team that reflects the communities we serve. Currently, we manage a global portfolio of over £8 billion in renewable energy assets. 

We are committed to delivering best-in-class responsible investment activity, offering like-minded investors the means and products to invest their capital sustainably. It is our ambition to change the entire energy lifecycle and make every green electron matter, delivering the best outcomes for customers, investors, the environment and society, accelerating the transition to net zero. 

OEGEN Data, Tech & Transformation Team 

We are embarking on a comprehensive transformation program designed to drive significant advancements in our business operations and technology landscape. Our primary goal is to transition from our current reliance on legacy systems and specialized off-the-shelf tools to a more integrated, AI-driven, and data-centric operational model. 

Leveraging insights and guidance from our other technically mature entities like Kraken and OE, we plan to adopt cutting-edge tools and capabilities, particularly in AI and Python-driven solutions. 

By investing in a diverse range of skills, we aim to create a hybrid team capable of operating in both our legacy and future environments, ultimately transforming OEGEN into an efficient, data-driven organization. 

About the role 

The tools are already here. Like the rest of OE Group, OEGEN runs on Databricks, we're moving onto our own Microsoft 365 tenant, and Octopus Energy Group gives us access to a powerful set of shared data and AI capabilities. What we're missing is someone whose job is to make all of it work together for our Fund Management business - and then build genuinely useful things on top of it. 

This is a two-sided role. On one side, you'll integrate: wiring third-party systems, internal apps and document storage into the environment we already have, setting sensible guardrails around access and cost, and adopting existing Group capability wherever it does the job rather than rebuilding it. On the other, you'll build: turning those connections into data products, internal tools and AI-enabled workflows that fund management, asset management and finance use every day. Tying the two together, you'll develop and own the playbook - the documented, repeatable patterns for how a new system gets connected, how a tool gets built and shipped, and how both get supported afterwards - so that what you learn once becomes how the whole team works. The two halves feed each other: you'll understand what's possible because you built the plumbing, and you'll build better plumbing because you know what people actually do with it. 

We want someone with genuine ideas about where AI can take a business like ours, and the pragmatism to ship them. Our team has already built an Excel data mart plugin that puts gold-layer tables directly in the hands of non-technical staff, a metrics taxonomy app that keeps third-party definitions aligned with our own, and AI-assisted workflows that scaffold documentation automatically. There's a long list of things we haven't got to yet. Expect roughly half your time on integration and enablement and half on building, and expect to work closely with the central data platform team so what we do in OEGEN stays consistent with the wider estate and our specific needs get onto their roadmap. 


What You'll Do

  • Integrate the systems our business runs on - third-party providers, internal tools, our own SharePoint and Microsoft 365 tenant - into our existing Databricks environment, via APIs and existing connectors. 

  • Build data products on top of what you connect: well-modelled, documented, reusable datasets that the business consumes directly through Excel, dashboards and natural-language querying, rather than one-off extracts. 

  • Design and ship internal applications and AI-enabled tools - using Python, Streamlit, Databricks Apps (HTMX), Lakebase, FastAPI or similar - that put data and AI directly into the hands of fund management, asset management and finance teams. 

  • Prototype, evaluate and productionise new AI capability, from document AI and retrieval to agentic workflows, and turn the ideas that prove out into supported products rather than abandoned experiments. 

  • Take an adopt-first approach: work with Octopus Energy Group's data platform and AI teams to reuse capability that already exists, and configure it for OEGEN rather than building parallel versions of it. 

  • Set up practical guardrails inside Databricks and Unity Catalog - schema and workspace access, permissions, environment hygiene - so more teams can use it without stepping on each other. 

  • Bring cost management from reactive to proactive: tagging, budgets, alerting and usage monitoring, so Databricks and AI token spend can be attributed to the right team, project or fund before the invoice arrives. 

  • Get our AI usage properly credentialed and logged - managed keys and access rather than API keys sitting in individual password managers - and provide clean patterns for embedding AI into the tools we build. 

  • Standardise how we build and ship internal apps: shared templates, authentication, deployment and documentation, so a tool remains supportable by someone other than the person who wrote it. 

  • Consolidate the ad-hoc scripts, spreadsheets and no-code workflows we've accumulated into fewer, better-understood integrations that don't need babysitting, and automate the repetitive parts of our own workflow. 

  • Work directly with non-technical teams to understand their problems and translate them into things we can build. 


What You'll Need

  • Strong systems integration experience - connecting business systems, SaaS tools and data sources via REST APIs, connectors and authentication flows. 

  • A track record of building and shipping data products or internal applications that people actually use, not just pipelines that feed someone else's reports. 

  • Solid Python and SQL, used daily for building, automation and data modelling. 

  • Hands-on experience with a cloud data platform in production (Databricks preferred): workspaces, catalogs, permissions and compute. 

  • Practical experience integrating AI into real tools - LLM APIs, retrieval, agents - with a clear-eyed sense of what works and what's still a demo. 

  • Practical identity and access experience - SSO, service accounts, credential management and access lifecycle - enough to make sensible, secure choices without a security team holding your hand. 

  • Experience with Microsoft 365 / SharePoint integration, or a comparable enterprise document and collaboration stack. 

  • Real experience keeping cloud or AI usage costs under control: you know what drives the bill and how to attribute and cap it. 

  • A pragmatist's instinct for adopting over building where infrastructure is concerned - you'd rather configure something that exists than write something new - paired with a bias toward shipping when it comes to solutions. 

  • Clear communication. You can explain a trade-off to a fund manager and hold your own in a technical review with a central engineering team. 

  • Comfort with real ownership in a small team, where you set the working patterns rather than inherit them. 


Bonus Points For
 

  • Full-stack or application development experience, particularly with Streamlit, FastAPI or HTMX. 

  • Familiarity with the Databricks ecosystem - Unity Catalog, Databricks Apps, Lakebase, Genie - or equivalent tooling. 

  • Experience with vector search, embeddings, document AI or retrieval-augmented generation in production. 

  • Experience with Terraform, GitHub Actions or similar, to keep configuration version-controlled and repeatable. 

  • FinOps experience: usage monitoring, budgets, showback and chargeback. 

  • Having supported analysts and non-specialist builders using a shared data environment. 

  • Experience in a regulated or audited setting such as financial services, infrastructure investment or energy. 

  • Familiarity with renewable energy, infrastructure investment or financial services data.

description:
Fastned is on a mission to accelerate the transition to electric mobility. Since 2012, we have been building and operating a rapidly growing network of iconic fast-charging stations across Europe powered entirely by solar and wind energy. With 500+ colleagues, we now operate over 450+ stations across nine countries, with an ambitious goal of reaching 1,000 stations by 2030. We are not building infrastructure for its own sake. Every station we open is a tangible step in the transition away from fossil fuels. This role offers you the unique opportunity to be at the forefront of driving this transition across France, Italy and Spain.

The role

As Head of Expansion South-West Europe, you will accelerate the reliable, high-quality expansion of sites for our charging stations across France, Spain and Italy. You will translate strategy into clear regional priorities, practical plans and effective ways of working. You will lead and coach the Expansion Leads and Expansion team members across your region, support cross-functional collaboration and ensure that risks, dependencies and opportunities are visible and addressed. The role combines people leadership, strategic implementation and governance. You will strengthen local ownership while creating alignment, sharing learnings and improving execution across the South-West region.

This role is based in Paris (France) and requires regular travel within Europe.

1. Tactical support and people leadership

  • Lead, coach and develop the Expansion Leads and additional team members across France, Spain and Italy.

  • Establish a consistent operating rhythm covering performance, funnel reviews, forecasting, risks and action tracking.

  • Use data and business insights to identify blockers, support needs and capacity requirements.

  • Coordinate cross-functional support and help resolve dependencies while strengthening country autonomy.

2. Strategic implementation

  • Translate ‘Network Development’ priorities into clear regional and country actions.

  • Support Expansion Leads and Country Directors in developing aligned expansion plans and strategic roadmaps.

  • Drive the adoption of new initiatives, processes and tools across the region.

  • Monitor market, competitor, regulatory and customer developments and turn relevant insights into recommendations.

  • Assess projects and initiatives based on value, risk, dependencies, capacity and strategic fit.

Le stockage d’énergie thermochimique stocke la chaleur sous forme d’énergie chimique, grâce à des réactions solide-gaz réversibles. Les hydrates de sels inorganiques absorbent de la chaleur lors de leur déshydratation et la restituent lors de leur réhydratation, ce qui en fait des matériaux candidats pour le stockage de chaleur. Leur performance en cyclage dépend des structures cristallines traversées entre les états d’hydratation, dont le volume de maille et la symétrie peuvent différer fortement.

Les hydrates de SrBr₂ servent de système modèle ; l’approche s’étend à d’autres hydrates de sels et à d’autres réactions gaz-solide.

• Vous menez des cycles de déshydratation/réhydratation suivis par diffraction des rayons X in situ, sous température et humidité contrôlées.

🎯 Ce que nous attendons de vous

La production de béton est responsable d'environ 8 % des émissions mondiales de CO2. Ces émissions sont principalement liées à la combustion et à la décarbonatation du calcaire nécessaire à la production du ciment Portland conventionnel.

Les liants à base de magnésie (MgO) sont étudiés comme alternatives potentielles aux ciments conventionnels, avec une empreinte carbone réduite. Le magnésium nécessaire à leur production pourrait être extrait de roches non carbonatées ou de saumures riches en magnésium. Ces ressources constituent des sources alternatives de matières premières et pourraient permettre d'éviter les émissions de CO2 liées à la décarbonatation du calcaire.

Cependant, ces liants alternatifs sont encore en cours de développement et leurs mécanismes d'hydratation, leur composition et leurs propriétés mécaniques doivent être mieux compris. En particulier, la nature et la réactivité de la source de magnésium, ainsi que les conditions de formulation et de préparation, peuvent influencer la microstructure et les performances mécaniques du matériau obtenu.

L'objectif de ce stage est d'étudier différentes sources de magnésium et d'évaluer leur potentiel pour le développement de liants de type MgO-SiO2 présentant de bonnes propriétés mécaniques et un impact environnemental réduit.

Plusieurs formulations de liants seront préparées et étudiées en faisant varier la source de magnésium et différents paramètres de formulation. Les matériaux obtenus seront caractérisés à l'aide de techniques complémentaires afin d'évaluer leur composition chimique, les phases formées lors de l'hydratation, leur microstructure, leur porosité et leurs propriétés mécaniques. Les principales étapes du stage seront les suivantes :

·        Étude bibliographique : synthèse des connaissances sur les liants magnésiens, leurs mécanismes d'hydratation et leurs applications potentielles.

·        Caractérisation des matières premières : étude de la composition chimique et minéralogique, de la distribution granulométrique (PSD) et de la réactivité des matières premières sélectionnées.

·        Formulation et préparation des liants : élaboration de pâtes de ciment de type MgO-SiO2 en utilisant différentes sources de magnésium et différents paramètres de préparation.

·        Caractérisation des matériaux : analyse des pâtes hydratées par diffraction des rayons X (DRX), analyse thermogravimétrique (ATG), microscopie électronique à balayage couplée à la spectroscopie à dispersion d'énergie (MEB/EDS), mesure de la porosité accessible à l'eau et essais mécaniques.

Analyse des résultats : comparaison des différentes formulations afin d'identifier les principaux paramètres influençant leur microstructure et leurs propriétés mécaniques.

title: Stage : Construction automatique de modèles de processus hospitaliers multi- flux par grands modèles de langage (LLM)
description:
Projet porté par : Marwa Trabelsi - IMT Mines Albi Centre Génie Industriel (CGI)

Partenaires IMT impliqués :

  • Telecom Sud Paris, Département Electronique et Physique, Laboratoire Services répartis, Architectures,

Modélisation, Validation, Administration des Réseaux (SAMOVAR): Nel Samama

  • Mines Saint-Etienne : Centre Ingénierie Santé (CIS), Marius Huguet

Sujet proposé (5-6 mois à partir de Février):

Acronyme : HOPAL : Hospital Process Automatic Learning

Titre long : Construction automatique de modèles de processus hospitaliers multi-flux par grands modèles de langage (LLM)

Description du projet :

L’étude du processus de prise en charge aux urgences est essentielle pour comprendre et résoudre le problème croissant de surcharge, qui touche de nombreux pays. Cette surcharge, souvent liée à un déséquilibre entre la demande de soins et les ressources disponibles, a des conséquences graves : retards de traitement, allongement des temps de triage, et même une augmentation de la mortalité. Elle révèle aussi des défis systémiques, comme l’accès difficile aux soins primaires, qui poussent les patients vers les urgences.

Optimiser l’utilisation des ressources humaines et matérielles permet non seulement de réduire les files d’attente, mais aussi d’améliorer la qualité des soins et l’efficacité globale du système. Enfin, analyser ces processus aide à identifier des solutions durables, comme une meilleure organisation ou une réallocation ciblée des moyens.

Ces processus laissent des traces numériques dans le système d'information hospitalier (SIH), mais leur modélisation reste aujourd'hui largement manuelle, coûteuse et rapidement obsolète.

Le process mining permet de découvrir des modèles de processus à partir de ces traces. Les techniques classiques de découverte atteignent toutefois leurs limites face à des logs hétérogènes, bruités et multi-flux.

Les grands modèles de langage (LLM) ouvrent une voie nouvelle : générer automatiquement des modèles de processus (BPMN, graphes de processus) directement à partir de traces organisationnelles, sans intervention humaine, et en produire une lecture compréhensible par les acteurs de terrain.

Par ailleurs, des travaux menés au CGI ont démontré la faisabilité de la prédiction de parcours patients par LLM. La question scientifique au cœur de ce stage est l'articulation de ces deux briques : comment relier la prédiction de parcours à la construction automatique de modèles, pour passer de modèles rétrospectifs (ce qui s'est passé) à des modèles prospectifs (ce qui va se passer) ?

Ce projet s’inscrit dans une dynamique inter-écoles IMT autour de l’IA explicable pour la santé publique. Les équipes CGI, CIS et SAMOVAR collaborent déjà via le projet TRACKING (Carnot M.I.N.E.S – CARINGS), avec des travaux sur la géolocalisation indoor au sein des urgences de l’Hôpital Le Corbusier de Firminy. Cette synergie s’est prolongée par un stage M2 en 2025, financé par le Fonds d’amorçage Santé, dédié au prototypage d’une application mobile de localisation indoor/outdoor des patients. Une thèse INTERCARNOT a été lancé dans la continuité avec la validation des deux instituts Carnot (M.I.N.E.S et TSN) et va démarrer en Octobre 2026.

Objectif du stage

L'objectif est de concevoir et prototyper un pipeline dans lequel un même module de construction automatique de modèles par LLM est alimenté par deux sources :

  • Branche A (rétrospective) : les logs SIH réels, normalisés en event logs, produisent des modèles as-is des processus observés ;

  • Branche B (prospective) : dans la suite des travaux réalisés, les parcours prédits par LLM sont sérialisés au même format de traces (activité, timestamp, ressource) via un adaptateur, et produisent des modèles to-be des processus à venir.

description:
PROJECT OVERVIEW

We are looking for a highly motivated Postdoctoral Researcher to develop innovative deeplearning models that predict the structure of functional-oxide thin films directly from their growth dynamics. Positioned at the interface between Artificial Intelligence and materials physics, the OXYD-IA project aims to design a deep model able to predict the final X-ray Diffraction (XRD) spectrum of an oxide thin film from the sole Reflection High-Energy Electron Diffraction (RHEED) video recorded during its growth by Molecular Beam Epitaxy (MBE).

The resulting tool will open the way to predictive, in situ control of oxide epitaxy – a process today dominated by a costly trial-and-error approach, in which the structural and functional properties of the films are only validated ex situ. You will join a genuinely multidisciplinary collaboration between the INL (Institut des Nanotechnologies de Lyon), which provides the operando experimental data and materials-physics expertise, and the LIRIS (équipe Imagine), which provides the deep video-learning and probabilistic-modelling methodology – both at École Centrale de Lyon.

A high-impact opportunity. AI for experimental physics is a fast-growing field, and OXYD-IA offers a genuine first-mover advantage within it: you would work on a unique, unpublished dataset of paired RHEED videos and XRD spectra to build one of the first video-to-spectrum models with calibrated uncertainty for oxide growth. By learning directly from experimental 1 data, such a model can short-circuit the traditional trial-and-error loop, accelerate discovery and drastically cut experimental time, cost, precursor consumption and instrument occupancy – turning routine in situ diagnostics into predictive tools.

Scientific context. Epitaxial perovskite-oxide thin films exhibit rich, tunable functional properties (thermoelectricity, ferroelectricity, piezoelectricity) governed by their structure and composition, themselves correlated with the growth conditions. MBE offers independent control of each element but, applied to oxides, is notoriously unstable and poorly reproducible because of the oxidising atmosphere. RHEED tracks the surface dynamics in real time (lattice parameter, surface reconstructions, roughness) but does not give access to the final bulk microstructure, which is only reachable ex situ via XRD / XRR. There is therefore a strong physical link – so far unexploited quantitatively – between RHEED dynamics and final XRD microstructure, which OXYD-IA proposes to learn directly.

Figure 1 – OXYD-IA pipeline. At inference, the RHEED video acquired during growth (INL) feeds a deep video encoder (LIRIS) and a probabilistic regression module that predicts the final XRD spectrum together with its uncertainty. During training, the predicted spectrum is compared with the ex situ XRD / XRR spectrum measured at INL (ground truth); this discrepancy is the supervised learning signal that adjusts the model parameters.

KEY RESEARCH AREAS AND RESPONSIBILITIES

You will drive the core computational research along a risk-managed, phased 12-month roadmap. The primary target is a versioned RHEED / XRD dataset, growth-regime classification and probabilistic regression of the key structural parameters with calibrated uncertainty; full-spectrum prediction, a real-time demonstrator and cross-oxide generalisation are stretch and follow-on objectives. The work is organised around three technical pillars:

1. Corpus structuring and spatio-temporal RHEED representation • Build a versioned dataset by cleaning, temporally aligning and pairing the RHEED video sequences, the associated MBE parameters (temperature, oxygen pressure, source fluxes) and the ex situ XRD / XRR spectra (SrTiO3 reference system). • Pre-train, in a self-supervised manner, a spatio-temporal video encoder (3D CNN, e.g. R(2+1)D, or temporal Vision Transformer) fine-tuned on the laboratory corpus. • Perform fuzzy / Bayesian classification of the growth regimes (2D vs. 3D modes, transitions, RHEED oscillations), building on LIRIS expertise in the statistical analysis of sequences.

2. Probabilistic RHEED →XRD regression with uncertainty quantification • Design a latent representation that couples the video encoding with the physical MBE parameters. • Learn stepwise – first scalar structural parameters (lattice parameter, density, mosaicity), more robust at small N, then the full 1D XRD spectrum. • Provide calibrated uncertainty estimates (Bayesian approaches or deep ensembles), indispensable for guiding real-time decisions during growth.

3. Real-time demonstrator and dissemination (stretch / follow-on) • Validate the model on new SrTiO3 growths and prototype an in-growth inference tool at the end of the NANOFUTUR MBE line. • Mitigate the small-data and generalisation challenges through temporal data augmentation, transfer learning from pre-trained video encoders and domain adaptation towards other functional oxides. • Contribute toward a high-impact joint publication at the AI / materials interface (the project milestone is the submission of a joint paper).


REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

• A Ph.D. in the field of Artificial Intelligence – Computer Science, Machine Learning, Computer Vision or Signal Processing, and we are looking for a senior postdoc with 2–5 years of post-PhD experience.

• Deep learning on sequential / video data: demonstrable, hands-on experience with 3D CNNs, temporal transformers and / or probabilistic models. Proficiency in Python and PyTorch (or TensorFlow) is mandatory.

• A genuine appetite for physics: a strong curiosity for, or prior exposure to, experimental physics and materials science. The ideal candidate carried out an AI-focused Ph.D. and is eager to apply it to a real materials-physics problem.

• Research mindset: a track record of innovation and the ability to work autonomously on a complex, multidisciplinary project. • Software skills: experience with Git version control and reproducible research.

• Excellent communication and scientific-writing skills in English.

ADDITIONAL SKILLS AND COMPETENCIES

• Self-supervised video pre-training, uncertainty quantification (Bayesian / ensembles), fuzzy classification, or domain adaptation.

• Experience with small-sample / transfer-learning settings and handling large-scale experimental datasets.

HOW TO APPLY

Please prepare a single PDF file containing:

1. A detailed Curriculum Vitae, including a list of publications.

2. A 1-page motivation letter explaining your specific interest in this project and how your background addresses the key responsibilities and qualifications listed above.

3. The names and contact information of at least two academic references.

title: Responsable enquêtes & plaidoyer
description:
Green-Got est une institution financière française qui permet à chacun de choisir ce que son argent finance. Nous avons été distingués pour notre exclusion des énergies fossiles par Reclaim Finance, bank.green, Bank for Good ou encore Moralscore. Green-Got est aussi lauréat de l'Impact 40 depuis 3 années consécutives.
Depuis cinq ans, nous montrons où va l'argent. Nos membres ont sorti 300 millions d'euros des grandes banques. Notre mission est de définir de nouveaux standards pour le secteur financier, alignés avec la science, et non pas les intérêts des industries fossiles.

Pourquoi ce recrutement ?
Les banques traditionnelles ont des lobbyistes. Ils défendent leurs profits et les industries qu'elles financent. Les citoyens, eux, n'en ont jamais eu. C'est désormais le cas.
Pendant plusieurs mois, nous avons enquêté sur le financement des pesticides par les banques françaises. Mais dénoncer ne suffit pas : la prochaine étape, c'est la loi. Nous recrutons la personne qui enquêtera à nos côtés, dévoilera ce que le système préfère laisser dans l'ombre et proposera des solutions concrètes pour changer les règles. Elle racontera chaque étape du combat à nos membres, en toute transparence.

Missions

Ton travail tient en trois verbes : enquêter, dévoiler, proposer. Tu portes 2 à 3 grandes campagnes par an, de la première piste jusqu'au texte de loi, et tu les incarnes.

1. Enquêter

  • Faire la veille de l'actualité politique, réglementaire et scientifique (Parlement européen, Assemblée nationale, comitologie, ONG), et nourrir l'équipe Média pour nos contenus réactifs.

  • Repérer les sujets de nos grandes campagnes de mobilisation et les valider avec nous : fludioxonyl, TotalEnergies financé par les Livrets A .

2. Dévoiler

  • Mener les recherches sur les campagnes validées. Ce n'est pas de la réaction à chaud : ce sont 2 à 3 combats de fond par an.

  • Creuser les rapports, les bilans et les sources primaires que personne ne lit, et en sortir des informations inédites.

  • Trouver les angles : quelles personnes interroger (un agriculteur, une famille touchée), comment les contacter, quels contenus en tirer avec l'équipe Média.

  • Incarner l'enquête pendant qu'elle se fait, face caméra et sur le terrain :

  • Prendre la parole face caméra (vidéos, lives, interventions médias) et partager régulièrement où en est le combat.

  • Répondre aux commentaires sur tes sujets et publier dans l'onglet Communauté de l'app. Tu vois comment nos membres réagissent, et cela nourrit tes prochaines enquêtes.

3. Proposer : plaidoyer et lobbying institutionnel

  • Construire la feuille de route plaidoyer à partir de nos enquêtes : quelles demandes, auprès de quelles institutions, avec quel calendrier.

  • Évaluer la faisabilité juridique et politique des leviers possibles : interdire certaines substances, encadrer ou interdire les financements aux producteurs de pesticides, exiger la transparence sur la présence d'entreprises fossiles ou de pesticides dans les produits d'épargne.

  • Repérer les fenêtres déjà ouvertes : renouvellements d'autorisation de substances, textes européens en discussion (Omnibus, décisions du SCoPAFF), propositions de loi, projets de loi de finances.

  • Rédiger les notes de position, propositions d'amendements et argumentaires, toujours adossés à la science et à des données indépendantes.

  • Cartographier et rencontrer les décideurs : Parlement européen, Commission européenne, Représentation permanente de la France, Assemblée nationale, Sénat, ministères, agences et régulateurs. Analyser leurs prises de position et leurs votes passés.

  • Rester strictement apartisan : nos demandes s'appuient sur la science, pas sur un camp.

  • Construire des coalitions avec les ONG, scientifiques, juristes et journalistes, et représenter Green-Got dans les coalitions françaises et européennes de la finance durable (Sustainable Banking Coalition/FEBEA, Impact France, Fair Finance). Une victoire collective reste collective : tes contacts doivent être dans toutes les ONG.

  • Devenir à terme un visage récurrent : « votre lobbyiste à Bruxelles ».

Compétences recherchées

Indispensable

  • Une expérience solide en plaidoyer, affaires publiques ou journalisme d'enquête : ONG, think tank, collaboration parlementaire, cabinet ministériel ou rédaction.

  • Un flair d'enquêteur. Tu sais où chercher l'information que personne n'a sortie (bilans, comitologie, listes de vote, thèses), et tu la vérifies avant de l'affirmer.

  • Une maîtrise en profondeur les deux arènes. Tu connais de l'intérieur le fonctionnement des institutions européennes (commissions, trilogues, comitologie) et du Parlement français (navette, amendements, PLF), et tu as déjà travaillé avec l'autre.

  • Un réseau actif de parlementaires, collaborateurs, conseillers et ONG sur ces sujets.

  • Une plume à deux registres : une note de position qui tient face à un juriste, un post LinkedIn qui tient face à un scroll.

  • De l'aisance face caméra et avec les journalistes. Tu acceptes d'incarner un combat, dans le respect strict des faits.

  • Un fibre en contenus : tu sais quels angles vont attirer l’attention, comment raconter des sujets compliqués…

Un vrai plus

  • Une culture scientifique et réglementaire sur la finance durable et la santé environnementale : taxonomie, SFDR, évaluation des risques, cadre européen d'autorisation des substances.

  • Une expérience dans une ONG de finance climat, ou une connaissance de la régulation financière (règles prudentielles).

  • Une expérience d'animation de coalitions.

Profil recherché

Green-Got est un employeur inclusif. Tous les profils qui se reconnaissent dans cette annonce sont les bienvenus, quels que soient leur parcours, leur genre ou leur origine.

  • Tu vas chercher toi-même.
    Tu ne reprends pas les enquêtes des autres : tu remontes aux sources.

  • Tu arrives avec un dossier.
    Pas seulement une dénonciation : ce qu'il faudrait changer, comment, et avec qui.

  • Tu es crédible partout.
    Dans le bureau d'un conseiller ministériel comme dans une story Instagram.

  • Tu tiens la distance.
    Le plaidoyer est lent et échoue souvent. Un échec bien raconté ne te fait pas peur : il prépare la suite.

  • Tu es rigoureux (mais genre, vraiment).
    Une seule affirmation fragile ruinerait la crédibilité de toutes les autres. Chaque chiffre est sourcé, chaque victoire attribuée à sa juste part.

  • Tu es owner.
    Tes réussites comme tes échecs t'appartiennent. Tu avances même quand c'est flou.

  • Tu veux un impact réel.
    Changer les règles, pas seulement en parler.

Le package

Lieu : Paris, avec des déplacements réguliers.

Contrat : CDI, statut cadre

Arrivée : ASAP

  • BSPCEs (equity)

  • RTTs

  • Mutuelle santé Alan

  • Déplacements à Bruxelles pris en charge

  • Une journée d'équipe tous les semestres

Nous avons hâte de te rencontrer.

title: Marketing Manager (m/w/d)
description:
Wir bauen humanoide Systeme: Full Stack, von Hardware und Elektronik über Software bis zur Fertigung, alles in-house in Berlin.

Bei Cell Labs verschieben wir die Grenze dessen, was Robotik leisten kann. Unser Ziel ist klar: Systeme bauen, die Menschen stärken statt sie zu ersetzen. Unsere Technologie ist bereits bei führenden Industriekunden und Partnern im Einsatz. Jetzt steht unser eigenes Produkt kurz vor dem Launch.

Die leise Phase ist vorbei. Wir suchen Menschen, die früh dabei sein wollen, Verantwortung übernehmen und das bauen, worüber andere nur reden.

Ort: Berlin · Start: Ab sofort · Arbeitsmodell: Vor Ort · Anstellung: Vollzeit

Deine Aufgaben

  • Marketingstrategie & Umsetzung: Du entwickelst gemeinsam mit unseren Gründer:in und dem restlichen Kreativteam die Markenstrategie von Cell Labs weiter und gestaltest u. a. den bevorstehenden Produktlaunch aktiv mit, von Messaging über Kampagnen bis zu Events.

  • Digital Marketing & Performance: Du entwickelst unsere digitale Sichtbarkeit weiter, optimierst Website, SEO und SEA und setzt zielgerichtete Kampagnen auf. Dabei testest du neue Ansätze und verbesserst kontinuierlich ihre Wirkung.

  • Content & Kommunikation: Du übersetzt komplexe Robotik-Technologien in verständliche und überzeugende Inhalte für unsere Website, Social Media, Newsletter und weitere Kanäle. Dafür arbeitest du eng mit unseren Gründern, dem Brand- und Designteam sowie den Engineers zusammen.

  • Go-to-Market: Du planst und steuerst Marketingkampagnen entlang des gesamten Funnels, entwickelst Maßnahmen zur B2B-Leadgenerierung und machst Cell Labs bei relevanten Industrieunternehmen und Partnern sichtbar.

  • Events & Kooperationen: Du planst und begleitest relevante Messen, Konferenzen und Partneraktivitäten – von der Vorbereitung der Marketingmaterialien über die Kommunikation bis zur Nachbereitung.

  • Marketing Operations & Analytics: Du definierst, misst und berichtest die Kennzahlen, die zählen: Pipeline-Beitrag, Conversion, Cost per Lead und Funnel-Entwicklung. Daraus leitest du Entscheidungen ab, statt nur Reports zu verwalten.

  • Sales Enablement: In enger Abstimmung mit unseren Gründern unterstützt du Vertrieb und Business Development mit Pitch-Materialien, Use Cases, Case Studies und Produktkommunikation für konkrete Verkaufssituationen.

Was du mitbringst

  • Erfahrung: Du hast mehrjährige praktische Erfahrung im Marketing, idealerweise im B2B-Umfeld eines Startups, Scale-ups oder Technologieunternehmens. Du hast Kampagnen eigenständig umgesetzt und idealerweise bereits einen Produktlaunch begleitet.

  • Breites Marketing-Know-how: Du kennst dich mit digitalen Marketingkanälen aus und hast praktische Erfahrung mit SEO, SEA, Content Marketing und Kampagnenmanagement. Du musst nicht alles perfekt beherrschen, weißt aber, wie du die richtigen Maßnahmen priorisierst und umsetzt.

  • Zahlenverständnis: Du setzt dir messbare Ziele und weißt, wie du sie nachhältst. Google Analytics, CRM-Software und Performance-Kennzahlen gehören zu deinem Arbeitsalltag. Du nutzt Daten, um Marketingmaßnahmen kontinuierlich zu verbessern.

  • Interesse für Technologie: Du interessierst dich für komplexe Technologien und hast Lust, tief in die Robotik einzutauchen. Du kannst technische Zusammenhänge verstehen und so vermitteln, dass sie auch für Menschen außerhalb der Entwicklung greifbar werden.

  • Kommunikation & Content: Aus einem technischen Gespräch mit einem Engineer machst du eine Case Study, Website-Copy oder einen Social-Media-Beitrag, der die richtige Zielgruppe erreicht.

  • Arbeitsweise: Du übernimmst gerne Verantwortung, arbeitest eigenständig und pragmatisch und hast Freude daran, neue Strukturen mit aufzubauen. Du wechselst zwischen Planung und Umsetzung, ohne eines von beidem aus dem Blick zu verlieren.

  • Sprachen: Deutsch und Englisch verhandlungssicher.

Benefits

  • Marketing von Grund auf: Es gibt kein fertiges Playbook und keine Altlasten. Du gestaltest gemeinsam mit unserem Marketingteam, wie Cell Labs am Markt sichtbar wird, und siehst die Wirkung deiner Arbeit direkt.

  • Alles unter einem Dach: Büro, Werkstatt und Teststände liegen im selben Gebäude in Kreuzberg. Wenn du eine Story für eine Case Study brauchst oder den Roboter in Aktion sehen willst, ist der Engineer ein paar Schritte entfernt, kein Ticket.

  • Room to Fail & Grow: Bezahlte Lernzeit mit persönlichem Budget für Kurse, Marketing-Konferenzen und die Tools, die du brauchst. Du bekommst Raum, Neues auszuprobieren, und bringst ein Produkt an den Markt, das bisher kaum jemand gesehen hat.

  • Benefits: Ein Leistungspaket, das du dir selbst zusammenstellst und das Mobilität, Gesundheit, Ernährung oder Fitness abdeckt. Dazu gibt’s einen zusätzlichen bezahlten freien Tag im Jahr für ehrenamtliches Engagement oder ein Projekt, das dir am Herzen liegt.

Bewerbung

Schick uns deinen Lebenslauf und ein paar Zeilen zu einer Marketingkampagne oder einem Projekt, das du eigenständig umgesetzt hast. Was war das Ziel, was hast du getan und was kam dabei heraus? Ein Anschreiben brauchen wir nicht.

Der Prozess: Intro Call, Deep Dive in deine bisherige Arbeit, Besuch bei uns mit einer kleinen Case Study, Angebot.

Wir bauen Roboter für alle, deshalb wollen wir ein Team, das das abbildet. Wir stellen nach Fähigkeiten ein und freuen uns ausdrücklich über Bewerbungen von Menschen, die in Marketing und Tech unterrepräsentiert sind. Wenn du nicht jeden Punkt erfüllst, aber denkst, das ist dein Job: bewirb dich.

Wir sind ein ganzheitlicher Wachstumspartner für E-Commerce-Brands im DACH-Raum. Jedes Jahr verwalten wir über 60 Millionen € Adspend und denken jedes Projekt von der Ad über den Funnel bis zur Marge. Deine Rolle und deine Ressourcen: Du übernimmst von Anfang an Verantwortung für deine eigenen Projekte, stehst damit aber nicht allein: Unsere Experten für UX-Design, Copywriting und Performance Marketing setzen deine Konzepte mit dir um. Das bringst du mit

  • Mindestens zwei Jahre Erfahrung in CRO, E-Commerce oder UX, idealerweise in einer Agentur oder einem Shop mit relevantem Traffic

  • Sicherer Umgang mit GA4, Hotjar/Clarity und A/B-Tests

  • Fundiertes Verständnis für Positionierung, Customer Journey und Conversion-Psychologie

  • Klare Kommunikation, schriftlich wie im Kundengespräch

  • Hohe Eigenständigkeit: Du priorisierst konsequent und gibst klare Empfehlungen

Der Rahmen

  • 30 Tage Urlaub

  • Zweimal jährlich Team-Events und Workations

  • Wöchentliche Team-Recaps und Coffee Chats, damit Remote nicht heißt, den ganzen Tag allein zu arbeiten

  • Betriebliche Altersvorsorge, JobRad und Firmenfitness über Wellpass

  • Steuerfreier Sachbezug von 50 € monatlich als Gutschein deiner Wahl

  • Weiterbildungsbudget sowie interne und externe Quellen und Mentoren an deiner Seite

As an AI Security Researcher, you bring deep expertise in AI/ML security, software development in Python, backed by a minimum MSc in Machine Learning, Computer Science, or related discipline. title: Product Engineering Lead
description:
Location: Remote (EMEA) · Germany/Munich preferred - CET/CEST time zone

Hi — I'm Grigory, co-founder and CTO at Secfix.

At Secfix we're building security compliance systems for teams and agents to become and stay compliant with less effort. We're already the category leader in Europe. AI is changing how software gets built, and we're shaping the tools this new era requires.

I've spent most of my career believing that the best engineering leaders aren't the ones who run the most meetings. They're the ones who make everyone around them faster, clearer, and more proud of their work — and they can do that because they've been through the hard technical problems themselves.

Since we started, I've done the engineering management myself: 1:1s, hiring, design reviews, performance conversations. The team is 8 engineers and 2 product designers, and I'm spread across too many things. If we were a football team, we'd be a good regional side that just made it to the Bundesliga — talented, hard-working, winning quite a few games. Now we need a coach who's played at Champions League level and can take us there to win every week.

That means a top-notch engineer who leads from the codebase. Someone who owns the technical decisions, sets the pace, and has product taste — who notices when a feature takes three weeks that should take one, and when it ships on time but isn't good enough. You'll ship every week and lead the team's biggest technical work — and as the team grows, you'll grow into managing it.

You'll work directly with me. Two things matter most here: speed and taste. Most teams pick one. We need both to win.

— Grigory


Why Secfix exists

Over 1.78 million SMBs in Europe need to comply with security frameworks — ISO 27001, GDPR, TISAX, SOC 2 — just to sell to enterprise customers. The process is manual, painful, and takes over a year. We automated it.

Our platform integrates with a company's full tech stack — AWS, Azure AD, Jira, GitLab, GCP, and more — automatically extracts compliance evidence, and guides teams to certification in weeks instead of months. Our fastest customer was certified in 4 weeks instead of the industry-standard 12+ months.

We've raised €17M in total (€12M Series A), backed by Alstin Capital, Neosfer (Commerzbank), and Bayern Capital. We're on a profitable trajectory, growing fast, and building the team that will take us to own European market from SMBs to mid market.

This space is not threatened by AI; it's amplified by it. Compliance requires deep domain expertise combined with automation. Our new AI product (CISO AI) is just getting started, and there's a huge amount of engineering work ahead: agentic workflows, intelligent evidence collection, context-aware policy generation, and more.


What you'll actually do in the first 3 months

This isn't a role where you show up and start running standups. There are no standups. Here's how the first quarter goes:

Month 1: Ship. Get into the codebase and ship a meaningful feature with AI alongside the team. By the end of the month, the team should be bringing you their hardest technical questions — because you've earned it, not because of the title.

Month 2: Make the team faster. Find where features take three weeks that should take one, and fix it — in tooling, in how we review and test, or in who's working on what. Start pairing and doing technical 1:1s with two or three engineers, focused on weekly output, quality, and how well they use AI.

Month 3: Own technical hiring. Take over the technical interviews and build a process that runs without my oversight. Design the technical challenges, run the screens, make the calls. The next people we bring in should raise the pace again. I will be there but switch my focus to final interviews.


What will the role look like beyond the first 3 months?

After the first quarter, the job is the technical decisions — and, as the team grows, management. You own how the team builds: how engineers test, how they review each other's code and security, how the team is organised, and who we hire next. We're 8 engineers and 2 product designers today and plan to be around 16 within 12 months — you'll run the technical side of it.

Most of your time stays in the code: you ship every week and own the specs, architecture, and reviews on our biggest projects. As the team grows, you'll take on 1:1s, growth conversations, and eventually managing the team.

Here's what you'll be close to in the next months:

  • Speed. You’ll refine our software development processes to keep the team operating at high velocity. Cycle time from spec to production is your number and accountability. Tooling, review flow, how work is split, who's on what — whatever moves it.

  • Quality. Improve how engineers test and automate, how they review each other's code and security changes, and how the zero-bug policy survives a team of 20.

  • Team and hiring. Technical interviews and mentoring now; 1:1s, growth conversations, and the EM role as we grow.

  • AI in the craft — and in the management. Engineers already work with an established set of encoded skills and rules — there's a whole playbook; you keep pushing that. Same for your own work: hiring, 1:1s, the recurring stuff.

What success looks like

At 6 months: You've led at least 2-3 major projects from spec to production. The hiring process runs without me, and we've added 2 engineers through it. Sales, CS, and product all feel the difference in how fast we ship — and in quality.

At 12 months: The team is around 12-16, the zero-bug policy is still holding at that size, and I'm not in the engineering critical path anymore. You've taken over 1:1s as the team grew, and you're ready to step into the EM role.


How we work

We've written in depth about our engineering culture. Here's the short version — read the full articles linked below if you want the real picture.

  • Focus is sacred. Engineers are in fewer than 2 hours of meetings per week. We write before we meet. We use Loom for async walkthroughs, Notion for specs, Gather for pairing, and Slack only for what's urgent or lightweight. We don't do status theatre. We wrote about our thoughtful communication and our remote culture; give it a read.

    To drive it home, here's a recent calendar of an engineer who has been with us for over a year:

  • Small, temporary teams. A designer and two engineers. A backend engineer and a CS person. The group forms around the problem, ships, and dissolves. No standing squads, no permanent team structures — at least not yet. The people closest to the problem usually shape the solution.

  • AI is already part of the craft. We use Claude for product design exploration and spec drafting. Engineers work in Cursor with encoded skills and rules that live in the codebase — component patterns, folder structure, architecture choices, and the path from Figma to Angular code. AI checks code against architecture rules before human review. We have a dedicated design QA skill that compares Figma against coded output. We don't use AI to lower the bar; we use it to reach the bar faster with more iterations behind us. In case you’re interested, we wrote a piece about it here.

  • Zero-bugs. We take this seriously - this helps us to gain customer trust faster. Especially serious customer-facing problems don't sit in a backlog competing with roadmap work. Critical issues get fixed immediately. High-severity within 48 hours. Every bug has an owner. Weekly quality review as part of Monday planning. Quality as identity, in compliance, being correct isn't a nice-to-have; it's the entire value proposition. We care about edge cases, data integrity, and getting the details right. Customers notice the speed and polish before they can name it. That kind of quality builds trust. In our category, trust is the product.

  • We build what customers need, not what they ask for. Customer feedback is signal, not instructions. Best products are built by people with great taste who treat feedback as signals, not KPIs. We stay close to customers — CS check-ins, support tickets, Mixpanel events, onboarding calls — but none of these sources makes the decision for us.

This role is for you if:

  • You've led a team technically and made it ship faster. You've set its technical direction, run its design reviews, and interviewed for it — and you can point to where cycle time dropped because of you.

  • You know what great engineers look like. You've thought deeply about what makes them productive, what holds them back, and how to move them forward — and you can spot one in a single interview.

  • You have an exceptional IC track record. You're a senior or staff engineer whose code and designs others build on — and you want to grow into managing, not escape coding.

  • You have product taste. You notice when a feature ships on time but isn't good enough, and you say so.

  • You hold people to a high standard. You're comfortable giving direct feedback and having hard conversations in code reviews and design discussions.

  • You're hands-on with AI-assisted development. You've used Cursor and Claude Code in real production work, not just toy projects. You have opinions about how AI changes the engineering workflow from ideation to release, and you want to push a team to keep getting faster.

  • You've worked in startups. You know what it feels like when there's low process, and the answer is "figure it out and ship it."

  • You think engineering culture can stay startup-like at scale. You're optimistic that a small, high-performing team can stay that way as it grows, with little process.

  • You communicate proactively in writing. In a remote team, written communication is how decisions get made and context gets shared. But you're not scared of jumping into a pair programming session either.


What we're looking for

Required

  • 8+ years as a software engineer at senior or staff level, including 1+ years as a tech lead (formal or de facto) for a team of 3+

  • You've shipped AI features to production — retrieval, RAG, agentic workflows — and you know the difference between a demo that works and one that holds up on real customer data

  • Product taste: a keen sense for what makes a product feel great, and the habit of saying so when it doesn't

  • You've built and shipped with Claude Code and Cursor in real production work, and you have opinions about where AI helps and where it quietly creates debt

  • You lead system design, not just contribute to it: you write the spec, own the architecture, and drive it to production

  • Strong OOP fundamentals; Java Spring Boot, Hibernate, or equivalent

  • Relational database design and SQL optimisation

  • Experience interviewing engineering candidates

  • You've built something zero to one at a startup, or scaled a team through the messy middle. You know what it feels like when there's no playbook

  • Able to work in European timezone (CET/CEST). EMEA-based, ideally Germany or UK

Nice to have

  • Some people management and technical interviewing experience

  • Designed a technical interview process from scratch

  • Previous experience at a fully remote company

Interview process

We want to see how you think, build, and lead — not test you on algorithms. Here's the process:

  • 30 min — Intro call with our talent team

  • 45 min — Interview with Grigory

  • 60 min — Technical interview

  • 1.5 hr — AI-assisted build session: system design for a real feature, then building part of it with AI

  • 2 hr — Leadership session with the founders

Then you’ll get the offer! If we don't make an offer, we'll tell you why.


What Secfix gives you

  • Remote: 100% remote with a real virtual office in Gather

  • Salary: Competitive, benchmarked to European market rates (we'll share specifics once we talk)

  • Equity: Generous package — we're all owners here

  • Development budget: €1,000/year — yours to spend on whatever makes you better

  • Workspace: Remote workspace support + co-working access

  • Holidays: 26 days + local public holidays

  • Health insurance: Comprehensive coverage

  • Annual retreat: Last time we went to Alicante 🇪🇸 — before that, the Austrian Alps, Portugal, Italy, and the Spanish Islands

  • Tech: MacBook, monitors, headphones — the latest

A video can't answer a question. It can't read the room. It can't role-play a tough conversation and adapt when you push back.

We're changing that. Interactive Avatars listen, talk, and respond in real time; inside your product, your website, or your internal tools. You bring the logic and the language model; we power the avatar layer: the speech, the expression, the listening, the sense that there's someone actually there.

It's early. Interactive Avatars is in closed beta today, and the teams building on it are pushing it into places we didn't expect - AI sales reps, always-on support agents, interactive trainers, onboarding guides. We're hiring a Product Manager to own it and take it from beta to a platform that thousands of developers build on.

This is a role with real scope. You'll help define what a real-time avatar API should be, the surface developers integrate against, the experience end users feel, and the commercial model that makes it a business. You'll work directly with the engineering and research teams building the real-time avatar stack, and with the design partners already live in the beta.

 

The problem you're solving

Today, a developer who wants a lifelike, real-time avatar in their product has to stitch together a streaming pipeline, a rendering layer, an agent, and a set of hard real-time problems - latency, interruption handling, listening behavior, expressiveness, consistency across sessions, most of which have nothing to do with the product they're actually trying to build.

We have the avatar technology and a working beta. What we need is a PM who can turn that into an API a developer can integrate in an afternoon, trust in production, and build a real business on top of, all while holding a quality bar high enough that the experience feels human, not uncanny.

Notre vision

  • Mettre en place des plans d’action et en piloter l’exécution.

  • Maintenir une relation de confiance, cadrer les attentes et délivrer de la valeur.

  • Déployer des plans d’action stratégiques (annuels / semestriels) avec les partenaires.

  • CSAT sur ton portefeuille.

  • Qualité de la gouvernance et autonomie des relais locaux.

  • Réduction des risques et amélioration de la rétention.

description:

We aim to become the most beloved financial Operating System of French SMEs and Accounting Firms (and soon, European ones).

Your impact

Great growth decisions start with reliable data.

At Pennylane, we're building the financial operating system for European businesses. As we grow and expand into new markets, understanding how users discover, interact with and adopt our product is becoming increasingly important.

That's where Growth Engineering comes in.

We're looking for a Growth Engineer with strong data and tracking expertise to help us build reliable, scalable tracking and analytics foundations across our digital acquisition journeys.

You'll join our Growth Engineering team and work closely with Thomas, our Growth Engineering Team Lead, within the Marketing Website squad.

Your mission ? Make sure we collect the right data, trust what we measure and turn insights into better growth decisions.

What you'll do

Build reliable tracking foundations

You'll own the technical implementation and reliability of tracking across our website and acquisition funnels.

  • Design, implement and maintain tracking plans across key user journeys.

  • Build and improve event tracking, user identification and data collection.

  • Work with tools such as Segment, Amplitude and Google Tag Manager.

  • Ensure tracking consistency, accuracy and reliability across our digital ecosystem.

  • Identify and resolve tracking issues before they impact business decisions.

Connect data across our growth ecosystem

You'll help build the technical connections between our website, internal systems and analytics tools.

  • Develop and maintain APIs and integrations between platforms.

  • Ensure reliable data flows between our acquisition, product and analytics tools.

  • Collaborate with Data teams to improve data quality and consistency.

  • Support the evolution of our tracking architecture as Pennylane scales internationally.

Power experimentation and conversion

You'll work closely with Growth, Marketing and Data teams to understand user behavior and improve acquisition performance.

  • Implement the technical foundations for A/B testing and experimentation.

  • Help measure acquisition funnels and identify opportunities for improvement.

  • Ensure experiments are properly tracked and measurable.

  • Translate business questions into clear technical tracking requirements.

  • Support data-driven decisions through reliable instrumentation.

Contribute as an engineer

This is an engineering role, not a reporting or dashboarding position.

You'll be expected to bring strong technical fundamentals and take ownership of your work.

  • Write clean, maintainable and well-tested code.

  • Build scalable and reliable technical solutions.

  • Investigate complex tracking and data issues.

  • Improve existing systems, processes and documentation.

  • Collaborate with engineers across Growth, Engineering and Data teams.

  • Contribute to technical decisions and engineering best practices.

Who are you?

We're looking for an engineer who understands both how data is collected and why it matters.

Someone who enjoys solving technical problems, working with different teams and making sure that business decisions are based on data people can trust.

You don't need to be a data scientist or a marketing specialist. But you should be comfortable working at the intersection of software engineering, analytics and growth.

We'd love to meet you if...

  • You have a software engineering experience, with hands-on exposure to tracking, analytics or data integrations.

  • You have implemented and maintained event tracking across websites, applications or acquisition funnels.

  • You're fluent in AI-assisted development : you work with coding agents, create custom skills and instructions, use worktrees to parallelize work and keep code quality high.

  • You're familiar with tools such as Segment, Amplitude, Google Tag Manager or similar platforms.

  • You understand event schemas, data layers, user identification and tracking consistency.

  • You're comfortable working with JavaScript and APIs to implement and troubleshoot tracking.

  • You care about code quality, reliability and maintainability.

  • You enjoy taking ownership of technical projects, from design to production.

  • You're comfortable working in French and English.

Bonus points if you have experience with:

  • Ruby on Rails, Vue.js or Nuxt.js.

  • SQL and data warehouses.

  • Server-side tracking and conversion APIs.

  • A/B testing and experimentation platforms.

  • Attribution, conversion measurement or acquisition analytics.

  • Privacy-conscious tracking and consent management.

  • International websites and multi-market acquisition funnels.

Our technical environment

Our Growth Engineering team works with:

  • Frontend: JavaScript, Vue.js, Nuxt.js

  • Backend: Ruby on Rails

  • Database: PostgreSQL

  • Development: Git, GitHub

  • Analytics & Tracking: Segment, Amplitude and other analytics tools, depending on the project

You'll collaborate closely with our Data teams and contribute to the evolution of our growth tracking infrastructure.

Why you'll love this role

  • Real impact: Your work will help teams understand how users discover and adopt Pennylane.

  • Technical ownership: You'll contribute to the architecture and reliability of our tracking ecosystem.

  • Engineering standards: You'll work on technical challenges that require the same level of rigor as our other engineering teams.

  • Cross-functional exposure: You'll collaborate with Growth, Marketing, Engineering and Data.

  • International scale: You'll help build the data foundations needed to support our expansion across Europe.

  • Continuous improvement: You'll have room to challenge existing implementations, propose better solutions and improve how we measure growth.

If you enjoy building reliable data foundations and want to see your engineering work directly influence growth decisions, we'd love to meet you.

What do we do to make your work life easier

🌴 Wherever you are based, you will get 25 vacations days paid by Pennylane

💵 You’ll have a competitive compensation package

📈 You'll get company shares to enjoy a piece of the success story you're building with us

If you are based in France, you will have a French contract following French regulation on top of the additional perks : 6 to 12 RTT, 5 weeks PTOs, lunch credits (Swile), Alan Blue healthcare cover and regular events in cities where Pennylaners are mostly presents (Lyon, Bordeaux, Nantes…)

We're working on providing those last advantages to our people based outside of France as well, but it can be quite more complex depending on different countries.

Who are we looking for ?

description:
Qui sommes-nous ? 

Q ENERGY France est un acteur majeur du marché des énergies renouvelables en France. Autrefois affilié au groupe RES, l’entreprise œuvre depuis 27 ans dans le développement, la construction et l’exploitation de projets éoliens et photovoltaïques.  

 

Aujourd'hui également positionnée sur le marché du stockage d'énergie, Q ENERGY poursuit son expansion vers de nouveaux domaines afin de proposer des solutions intelligentes et complètes pour la production et la fourniture d’énergie durable en France. 

 

L'entreprise compte près de 300 collaborateur.rice.s et 6 agences sur le territoire ainsi qu'un siège social basé à Avignon. Q ENERGY France est une entreprise de la holding européenne Q ENERGY Solutions, créée en 2021 par Hanwha Solutions dans l'objectif de conduire à la prochaine génération de production d'énergie verte et flexible en Europe. Basée à Berlin, Q ENERGY Solutions est une société sœur de Q CELLS, fabricant de modules photovoltaïques reconnu à travers le monde. Les deux sociétés constituent la division Energie du groupe Hanwha Solutions, basé à Séoul. 

 

Vos missions : 

Vous serez support au pilotage et à l'animation d'études d'impacts sur l'environnement de parcs éoliens et centrales solaires comprenant notamment le volet naturel, le volet paysager et des études spécifiques.  

Vous serez en lien avec l'équipe projet, les autorités et les spécialistes pour identifier et traiter l'ensemble des risques environnementaux des projets. 

Vous participerez à la concertation de tous les acteurs permettant de réaliser la conception de projets la plus adaptée au territoire.  

Vous proposerez des axes d'amélioration sur les mesures E-R-C-A (Eviter, Réduire, Compenser, Accompagner) des projets éoliens et solaires. 

En particulier les axes d'amélioration suivants ont été identifiés :  

  • Amélioration du bilan carbone des projets (outils, méthodologies) et proposition de mesures de réduction de l’impact carbone des projets. 
  • Amélioration de la gestion des risques dans les projets solaires développés en SIS (sites et sols pollués). 
  • Amélioration de la synergie entre projets solaires et stockage batterie-BESS (projets d’hybridation). 

Vous participerez au dépôt des dossiers de demande de permis de construire et à leurs instructions (Commission CDPENAF, Enquête Publique, Réponse avis MRAe,...). 

Vous aurez l'occasion de suivre la mise en place concrète de mesures environnementales en phase chantier/construction sur une centrale solaire. 

HSE : 

Contribution à la culture Santé, Sécurité et Environnement de l’entreprise via :  

  • Réalisation du travail dans le respect des mesures de prévention mises en place au sein de l’entreprise et reprises notamment dans le Document Unique, les Politiques Santé, Sécurité et Environnement, procédures, modes opératoires et guides 
  • Déclaration de tout événement ou situation pouvant représenter un danger pour les personnes y compris collègues et prestataires et/ou l’environnement  
  • Participation aux événements de formations et de sensibilisations traitant de ces thématiques 

Qualité : 

  • Respect et mise en œuvre de la politique d’entreprise et des procédures qualité  
  • Participation à la mise à jour des documents du système de management de la qualité  
  • Déclaration des non-conformités et participation à la mise en place d’actions correctives 
  • Participation aux actions et projets d’amélioration continue et de partage des savoirs

Requirements

Votre profil : 

  •  Vous préparez un bac + 5 dans une formation d’ingénieur.e en environnement, agriculture, agronomie ou un Master en Ecologie, Biodiversité, Développement Durable 
  • Vous utilisez quotidienne le pack office et êtes à l’aise dans l’utilisation des outils informatiques d’une manière générale. 
  • Vous êtes rigoureux.se, curieux.se et force de propositions. Vous savez évoluer en autonomie dans vos recherches. Vous êtes doté.e d’un excellent relationnel.   

 

Localisation et déplacements 

Durée : 6 mois  

Localisation : Nantes - déplacements ponctuels en Bretagne / Pays de la Loire / Centre Val de Loire 

Benefits

Comment faisons-nous la différence ? 

  • Des valeurs fortes et incarnées   
  • Un management de proximité   
  • Une dynamique d’organisation apprenante   
  • Une entreprise en constant développement  
  • Valorisation et développement des compétences

  • Flexibilité et bien-être : jusqu'à 1 jour de télétravail et flexibilité des horaires 
  • Prise en charge à 100% des frais de transports collectifs  
  • Forfait mobilité durable pour les déplacements en mobilité douce (vélo...) ou en covoiturage et aides à l’écomobilité

Lemrock builds the infrastructure of agentic commerce.

Tomorrow, consumers won't just buy on e-commerce websites. They will discover, compare and purchase directly inside conversational AI interfaces like ChatGPT, Perplexity, and a growing long tail of specialized AI assistants.
