  • 150+ brand clients

  • a $100B market structuring at high speed

Context

You'll join a small, high-ownership engineering team (software, AI, data) building production systems that serve millions of users. We care deeply about code quality and clean architecture, and we intend to keep it that way as we scale.

Lemrock is accelerating and the team is about to grow. As our VP Engineering, you own how engineering runs: the team, the way we deliver, and the technical roadmap. You report to our CTO, who keeps the product and technical vision.

Your mission

Team & hiring

  • Grow the engineering team: build the hiring plan with the founders, run the process and hold the bar

  • Manage the engineers day to day: 1:1s, feedback, career paths, then the first layer of leads as the team grows

  • Keep a culture where ownership, code quality and speed go together

Delivery & process

  • Take the product inputs, prioritise with the CTO, staff each project and commit to dates you hold

  • Set up the process the team needs at its size, no more: planning, rituals, code review, incident handling

  • Make capacity and trade-offs visible to the founders, early

Technical direction

  • Own the technical roadmap and turn new product bets into scoped, staffed projects

  • Make the architecture, infrastructure and tooling calls with the CTO and the senior engineers

  • Own reliability, security and infrastructure costs as traffic and integrations grow

  • Stay close to the code: design reviews, code reviews, and shipping yourself when it unblocks the team

AI-native engineering

  • Scale the way the team builds with AI agents (Claude Code, Cursor): shared practices and tooling, so we go faster without lowering the quality bar

After 6 months

  • The team has grown with engineers who raise the bar, and everyone ships every week

  • Delivery is predictable: the founders know what lands when, and it lands

  • The technical roadmap runs through you, and the CTO is back on product and vision

Candidate profile

  • 10+ years of software engineering, including 3+ years managing engineers

title: Head of Business Unit Solaire H/F
description:

Octopus Energy, fournisseur d’énergie verte présent à l’international, a lancé sa filiale Octopus Energy Services pour accompagner ses clients dans la décarbonation complète de leur foyer. Déjà bien implantée au Royaume-Uni, cette entité propose un ensemble de solutions techniques : installation de panneaux photovoltaïques, de bornes de recharge pour véhicules électriques et de systèmes de chauffage décarboné, le tout avec une approche centrée sur la qualité, l’innovation et sans sous-traitance.
 
Tu veux un job qui a du sens ? Octopus Energy Services a démarré son activité en 2024, avec un objectif clair : aider les particuliers à réduire leurs factures énergétiques tout en participant activement à la transition énergétique. Et aujourd’hui on a besoin de toi pour propulser notre croissance !

Nous sommes aujourd’hui une cinquantaine de salariés et nous visons 10 M€ de chiffre d'affaires en 2027, ce qui nous placera parmi les leaders du marché. Le cap derrière : que tout client qui veut s'équiper pense à nous en premier, parce que nous sommes la référence sur la qualité de l'accompagnement et des produits que nous vendons.

Pour tenir ce cap, nous nous structurons en trois BU : 

  • La BU Solaire reste notre activité historique et notre cœur de métier : vente et pose avec nos propres installateu·rices.

  • Notre réseau de Partenaires Certifiés, pour accompagner les clients sur des travaux que nous ne proposons pas en propre (vente et pose de pompe à chaleur notamment).

  • Le matériel, afin de lancer sur le marché français les produits fabriqués par le groupe, comme sa pompe à chaleur Cosy, que l’on souhaite proposer à nos Partenaires Certifiés. 

Guillaume, Directeur Général Délégué, qui a lancé la filiale, supervisera les trois et cherche la personne qui dirigera la BU Solaire, notre activité historique.

Ta mission :

Tu diriges la BU Solaire comme un·e véritable dirigeant·e de business : tu fixes le cap, tu portes les résultats et tu construis l'organisation qui nous fera passer à l'échelle. Ton premier chantier : monter en cadence de pose, sans dégrader la qualité, tout en améliorant la rentabilité de la BU en 2027. Tu le fais depuis le terrain autant que depuis le bureau.

Tes responsabilités seront les suivantes : 


1. Stratégique : Définir le cap et faire grandir la BU.

Tu portes la vision, la stratégie de développement de la BU et tu prends les arbitrages structurants, notamment :

  • Fixer la trajectoire de la BU et trancher les décisions qui font avancer le business ;

  • Décider, le moment venu, des extensions : nouvelle zone géographique, nouvelle ligne de produit ;

  • Représenter la BU en interne et faire l'interface avec Octopus Energy France (fourniture d'énergie, offre bundlée pose + contrat + pilotage batterie), les fonctions support partagées et les deux autres BU.


    • 2. Économique : Piloter le P&L, la rentabilité et les investissements

    Tu es owner des chiffres de la BU, tu devras notamment :

  • Suivre la rentabilité à chaque maillon de la chaîne (vente, étude, pose, SAV) et les faire suivre à chaque manager ;

    • 3. Managériale et opérationnelle : Faire grandir les managers et structurer l'organisation.

    Tu fais monter les responsables de chaque équipe pour qu’ils portent la montée en cadence de la BU dans une organisation qui grandit : 

  • Accompagner les managers d’équipe au quotidien pour qu'ils·elles fassent grandir ses équipes, y compris dans les moments difficiles ;

  • Structurer, avec les équipes techniques, la montée en cadence de pose ;

  • Animer le collectif et incarner la culture de l'entreprise : exigence de qualité, jalons, victoires célébrées.


    • Ce qu'on cherche :

    Ce qui compte d'abord, c'est qui tu es : 

  • Tu t’intéresses vraiment aux gens, tu es exigeant·e et tu dis les choses clairement, dans le respect de la personne en face.

  • Tu sais engager des équipes pluridisciplinaires : commerce, administratif, technique et terrain ne parlent pas la même langue, tu fais le lien.

  • Tu prends ton sujet en main et tu as le courage managérial de dire les choses.

  • Tu es proactif·ve, tu trouves des solutions en autonomie et tu fais s'activer les équipes autour de toi.

Recognized as a leader by Gartner, Scality software is reliable, secure, and sustainable.


The job context

The team

Our IT & Security team builds, runs and secures Scality's IT infrastructure. It also supports the whole Scality community: employees, contractors, consultants and freelancers. We make sure everyone works in a secure, compliant and up-to-date environment. We also bring security expertise to our products (RING, ARTESCA, ADI) and to our customers.

You will join a team of 4 to 5 people with varied backgrounds (development, security, IT operations, helpdesk) and 2 to 30+ years of experience.

The mission

You will own Scality's information security compliance program and coordinate the team's security operations. You will lead our ISO 27001 and ISO 42001 (AI management system) certifications and manage vulnerability (CVE) follow-up with Engineering. 

You will answer customer security requests and audits. You will also help our products meet new regulations such as the EU Cyber Resilience Act (CRA).

The role is about 70% governance, risk and compliance (GRC) and product security, and 30% hands-on security operations.


The job description

You will own (Responsible)

  • Security operations coordination: be the point of contact for incoming IT & Security requests, prioritize them and dispatch them within the team.
  • Vulnerability management: Assess product exposure to CVEs by leveraging internal tools powered by our Software Bills of Materials (SBOMs).. Handle customer security requests (RD tickets) with Engineering and Support until a fix version or a customer answer is delivered. Track scan and pentest reports through remediation.
  • ISO 27001 and ISO 42001 programs: maintain the framework, policies and procedures in our GRC tool. Run risk analysis and treatment plans, objectives and indicators, and the Statement of Applicability. Prepare internal and external audits and follow up on nonconformities and improvement opportunities.
  • Control management: run the monthly, quarterly and annual controls (account and access reviews across HR system and SSO, application access, offboarding checks), automate them in Jira and keep audit evidence.
  • ISMS processes: run security incident management and change management in Jira (workflows, fields, records), and the business continuity part of customer requests (ISO 22301-type questionnaires).

  • AI governance: maintain the AI systems inventory, review the AI features of tools before use, and follow regulatory changes (EU AI Act).
  • Personal data: maintain the personal data inventory and processing records (GDPR, CNIL guidance) together with the data protection contact.
  • Customer trust: answer security questionnaires and RFPs, and prepare evidence packages for customer audits (banking, telecom and public-sector customers).
  • Security awareness: plan and run awareness and phishing campaigns, and track participation and click rates for managers.

Also contribute to CISA Secure by Design commitments and UK Cyber Essentials. Bring security input to the product roadmap, the development teams and the product documentation.

  • Building and managing effective relationships with senior stakeholders across the business, providing clear advice, challenge and escalation on financial crime matters

  • Providing oversight of financial crime risks associated with existing and emerging products and services, ensuring appropriate mitigation strategies are developed and implemented

title: Senior Product Analyst
description:
Who we are:

We're one of Europe's fastest-growing fintech companies – on a mission to create the world's most empowering way to pay.

We launched the product in 2020 and achieved double unicorn status, valued at $2 billion, and since then have taken on more than 6 million customers.

Our mission is to become the best way to pay for anything, anywhere and say goodbye to credit costs for everyone. This is huge. Want to join us?

About the role.

The Senior Product Analyst, Merchant will be the dedicated analytics lead for Zilch’s Merchant domain - the space where shopping discovery, merchant-funded advertising, paid display, paid search, affiliate conversion, and customer engagement come together.

Reporting into Product Analytics and partnering closely with the Senior Product Manager for Merchant, you’ll help build the analytical foundation for Zilch’s intelligent commerce platform. This is a two-sided problem: we need to improve the customer shopping experience while helping merchants drive measurable ROAS through Zilch’s closed-loop payments and behavioural data.

Here, paid display and paid search refer to advertising inventory we sell to merchants, not media we buy. You’ll help define how this inventory is measured, targeted, optimised, and monetised across the Zilch app.

You’ll analyse the full shopping journey - from browsing and search, through merchant discovery, unlocks, clickouts, transactions, and repeat engagement - to understand where users drop off, what drives intent, and which product features can improve engagement, conversion, and monetisation.

This is not a reporting-only role. The analysis, experimentation, and models you build will directly shape what customers see, how merchants are surfaced, and how we move from static merchandising towards data-driven discovery, allocation, and personalisation.

Day to day responsibilities.

  • Own analytics for Zilch’s Merchant domain, covering shopping discovery, customer browsing behaviour, merchant-funded paid display and paid search, affiliate conversion, merchant ROAS, and marketplace performance.

  • Analyse the customer shopping journey across browsing, search, merchant discovery, unlocks, clickouts, transactions, and repeat usage to identify opportunities to improve engagement, conversion, and monetisation.

  • Design and analyse experiments across merchant placements and shopping features, including targeted vs random allocation, paid display exposure, search ranking, storefront changes, offer discovery, and journey improvements.

  • Build the measurement framework for merchant-funded growth, including incrementality, attribution windows, exposed vs control logic, ROAS, CPA, conversion, revenue per impression, and margin impact.

  • Partner with Product and Commercial to shape audience packages and targeting strategies, ensuring they are commercially sellable, analytically measurable, and grounded in customer behaviour.

  • Develop segmentation approaches for merchant-funded display and search, including category affinity, value bands, browsing intent, cross-sell audiences, lapsed users, and future lookalike opportunities.

  • Support the evolution from simple segment-based targeting towards more advanced allocation logic, recommendation systems, and marketplace decisioning.

  • Work with Data Science, Data Engineering, and Engineering on the data foundations for merchant personalisation, including event tracking, feature creation, experimentation infrastructure, and model evaluation.

  • Translate complex analysis into clear recommendations for Product, Commercial, and senior leadership.


What we're looking for...

  • Ideally, 5+ years of experience in product analytics, growth analytics, marketplace analytics, retail media analytics, performance marketing analytics, data science, or a closely adjacent role.

  • Strong commercial judgement and fluency in ROAS, CPA, incrementality, attribution, LTV, conversion, margin, and marketplace trade-offs.

  • Deep data skills. You’re fluent in SQL, comfortable working with large behavioural datasets, and able to independently investigate ambiguous problems, define the right metrics, and produce robust analysis.

  • Rigorous experimentation experience. You can design clean A/B tests, reason about incrementality and power, interpret results honestly, and know when data is good enough to act on.

  • Experience analysing digital funnels, browsing behaviour, search behaviour, clickouts, conversion, paid placements, shopping discovery, or marketplace dynamics.

  • Experience with segmentation, targeting, personalisation, recommendation systems, ranking, marketplace allocation, retail media, or paid media measurement would be highly valuable.

  • Strong product instincts, with the ability to recommend and evaluate shopping features that improve customer engagement, discovery, conversion, and monetisation.

  • Commercially minded and comfortable working across Product and Sales. You can understand both customer value and merchant performance, and translate analysis into decisions that improve both.

  • Strong communicator who can explain complex analytical concepts clearly to Product, Commercial, and Executive stakeholders.

  • A proactive, growth-minded operator who is comfortable building analytical foundations in a new domain where the questions, data model, and product strategy are still evolving.

title: Directeur Exploitation Datacenters – Infrastructures Critiques (H/F)
description:
Head of DC Operations (H/F)

Région parisienne

Votre mission

Dans un environnement où la disponibilité et la fiabilité des infrastructures sont essentielles, Isatalent recherche un(e) Head of DC Operations pour piloter les opérations de ses data centers en région parisienne.

Rattaché(e) à la direction, vous êtes garant(e) de la performance opérationnelle, de la continuité de service et de la fiabilité des infrastructures. Vous encadrez les responsables de site et travaillez en étroite collaboration avec les équipes d'expertise centrales, les clients et les partenaires de maintenance.

Dans un contexte de croissance de l'entreprise et d'exigences opérationnelles, vous jouez un rôle clé dans l'harmonisation des pratiques, la structuration du pilotage des activités et l'accompagnement du changement auprès des équipes.

Votre objectif : construire une vision opérationnelle consolidée, maîtriser les risques et fédérer les équipes autour d'exigences communes de performance, de sécurité et de qualité de service.

Important – Nature du profil recherché

Nous recherchons un/e professionnel/le de l'exploitation technique de datacenters (Data Center Operations / Critical Facilities), et non un Directeur des Systèmes d'Information ou un Directeur des infrastructures IT.

Une expérience concrète du pilotage opérationnel des infrastructures physiques critiques est indispensable : installations électriques (HT/BT), UPS, groupes électrogènes, systèmes de refroidissement (CVC), maintenance préventive et corrective, gestion des incidents et continuité de service.

Les profils exclusivement orientés IT, systèmes, réseaux, cloud, hébergement ou gestion de projets informatiques ne correspondent pas au périmètre du poste.

Vos responsabilités

Piloter la stratégie et la performance des opérations multisites

  • Élaborer une feuille de route opérationnelle à court et moyen terme, en définissant les priorités, les plans d'action et les ressources humaines et financières nécessaires.

  • Définir et harmoniser les méthodes de pilotage des activités opérationnelles sur l'ensemble des sites.

  • Consolider et faire évoluer les KPI et tableaux de bord portant notamment sur la disponibilité des infrastructures, la maintenance, la communication client et le respect des procédures.

  • Analyser les résultats, identifier les écarts de performance et piloter les actions correctives.

  • Produire un reporting structuré à destination de la direction et éclairer les décisions stratégiques.

Manager les responsables de site et accompagner la transformation

  • Encadrer et accompagner les responsables de site dans le pilotage de leurs activités et le développement de leurs compétences.

  • Apporter une expertise opérationnelle et technique permettant de challenger les choix, les priorités et les plans d'action.

  • Favoriser l'autonomie, la responsabilisation et la coopération des équipes.

  • Organiser l'allocation des ressources et le suivi des plans de charge.

  • Accompagner la réorganisation du périmètre, harmoniser les pratiques et contribuer à l'intégration de nouveaux sites.

  • Travailler en transversalité avec le responsable du pôle Expertise et les autres fonctions de l'entreprise.

Garantir la fiabilité des infrastructures et maîtriser les risques

  • Garantir la disponibilité, la résilience et la continuité d'exploitation des infrastructures critiques.

  • Superviser la maintenance préventive, corrective et réglementaire, ainsi que les travaux, extensions, rétrofits et changements réalisés en environnement exploité.

  • Reprendre et consolider la cartographie des risques opérationnels et techniques, notamment les points uniques de défaillance (SPOF) et les obsolescences critiques.

  • Hiérarchiser les risques, définir les plans de traitement, en évaluer les impacts financiers et humains et identifier les investissements nécessaires.

  • Piloter les incidents majeurs, les escalades, les analyses de causes et le suivi des actions correctives et préventives.

  • Garantir le respect des exigences de sécurité, de conformité et de continuité de service.

Développer la relation client et le partenariat avec les mainteneurs

  • Garantir le respect des engagements contractuels, des SLA et des standards de qualité attendus par les clients.

  • Renforcer la qualité de la communication opérationnelle et la confiance avec les interlocuteurs clients.

  • Développer une relation constructive et partenariale avec les mainteneurs et les prestataires.

  • Améliorer la coordination des interventions, le suivi des engagements et la qualité des prestations.

  • Identifier les axes de progrès et piloter les actions d'amélioration de la performance des partenaires.

Piloter les budgets et l'amélioration continue

  • Élaborer et suivre les budgets OPEX et CAPEX du périmètre.

  • Arbitrer les priorités de maintenance, de renouvellement et d'investissement en fonction des risques, des capacités et des engagements clients.

  • Garantir le respect des exigences réglementaires, environnementales, HSE, ICPE et des référentiels ISO applicables.

  • Déployer des standards, procédures et méthodes de travail homogènes.

  • Contribuer à l'amélioration de la performance énergétique des installations, notamment du PUE, et à la maîtrise des coûts d'exploitation.

Votre profil

Formation et expérience

  • Formation supérieure, idéalement Bac +5, de type ingénieur ou master spécialisé en génie électrique, énergétique, climatique, maintenance industrielle ou management des opérations. Un Bac +3 technique pourra être étudié au regard d'une expérience particulièrement solide.

  • Expérience significative dans l'exploitation, la maintenance ou la direction technique d'infrastructures critiques.

  • Expérience significative en management de managers, en pilotage multisite ou dans une fonction de responsabilité opérationnelle comparable.

  • Expérience confirmée dans un environnement critique fonctionnant 24h/24 et 7j/7, avec de fortes exigences de disponibilité, de sécurité et de conformité.

  • Expérience en gestion d'incidents majeurs, pilotage de budgets, gestion des risques et conduite de transformations opérationnelles.

Compétences techniques

  • Bonne maîtrise des enjeux d'exploitation des data centers et compréhension des architectures électriques, mécaniques, CVC, de protection incendie, de GTB/BMS et des systèmes de contrôle.

  • Maîtrise du pilotage de la maintenance préventive, corrective et réglementaire.

  • Connaissance des SLA, KPI de disponibilité, capacité, qualité de service et performance énergétique.

  • Capacité à analyser et challenger les risques techniques, les plans de maintenance et les investissements.

  • Maîtrise des enjeux budgétaires OPEX/CAPEX et des exigences réglementaires applicables.

Qualités personnelles

  • Leadership et capacité à manager des responsables expérimentés.

  • Crédibilité technique et sens des responsabilités.

  • Capacité à structurer une organisation, harmoniser les pratiques et conduire le changement.

  • Aptitude à fédérer les équipes et à développer la coopération transverse.

  • Capacité de décision, d'arbitrage et de priorisation.

  • Sang-froid en situation de crise, rigueur et orientation résultats.

  • Sens du client et capacité à construire des relations de partenariat durables.

Langues : français courant et anglais professionnel, à l'oral comme à l'écrit.

Les enjeux de réussite

Au cours des premiers mois, vous aurez notamment pour objectifs de construire une feuille de route opérationnelle claire, de consolider le pilotage par les indicateurs, de hiérarchiser les risques et de définir les moyens nécessaires à leur traitement.

Vous contribuerez également à renforcer la cohésion managériale, à harmoniser les pratiques entre les sites et à accompagner l'évolution de l'organisation dans une logique durable de performance et d'amélioration continue.

title: Telecom security trainer
description:
About P1 Security

Founded in 2011, P1 Security is on a mission to secure critical and sovereign mobile networks by providing services and technologies to identify, detect, and recover from critical threats and vulnerabilities.

We address telecom security challenges across 5G, cloud-based infrastructure, OpenRAN, network slicing, edge computing (MEC), and legacy telecom systems (2/3/4G), including Diameter, SS7, SIGTRAN, GTP, and related attack surfaces.

Our team includes telecom operators, security professionals, and researchers who regularly share cutting-edge work at international security conferences and GSMA working groups. P1 Labs, our R&D branch, also shares open-source initiatives with the telecom security community (GitHub).

Job Description

Freelance Telecom Security Trainer — Worldwide Onsite Missions

We are seeking an experienced Freelance Telecom Security Trainer to deliver high-impact, onsite technical training for mobile network operators (MNOs), regulators, and enterprise clients worldwide.

Working on a per-mission basis, you will adapt and present established course content and practical lab materials from P1 Security’s training platform. You will help engineering and security operations center (SOC) teams understand telecom protocol vulnerabilities, assess their impact, and apply effective detection and defense strategies.

This role combines deep telecom security expertise with strong classroom facilitation skills and a practical, hands-on approach to learning.

Responsibilities

  • Deliver multi-day onsite technical workshops worldwide, adapting your approach to participants’ technical backgrounds and learning objectives.

  • Prepare for each mission by reviewing the course scope, audience prerequisites, learning objectives, and practical lab requirements with the P1 Security team.

  • Adapt existing online curriculum, presentations, exercises, and lab materials for engaging live classroom delivery.

  • Explain signaling flows, trust boundaries, protocol vulnerabilities, attack scenarios, and defensive controls clearly and accurately.

  • Facilitate hands-on exercises in authorized, controlled lab environments and help participants troubleshoot technical issues.

  • Answer participant questions on telecom security, including detection, mitigation, and operational defense strategies.

  • Check participants’ understanding through practical exercises, discussion, and knowledge checks.

  • Coordinate classroom and lab readiness with P1 Security and the client before delivery.

  • Gather participant feedback and share recommendations to improve course content and delivery.

  • Respect client confidentiality, intellectual property, and agreed rules of engagement throughout each mission.

Required qualifications

  • Deep telecom security expertise in one or more of the following domains:

  • SS7 / SIGTRAN: MAP/CAP signaling, common abuse scenarios, and signaling security controls. Related course: TS-201 — 2G, 3G and SS7 Mobile Network Security.

  • LTE / Diameter: S6a, Gx, and Gy interfaces, protocol vulnerabilities, and defensive measures. Related course: TS-401 — LTE Security and Insecurity.

  • GTP-C: Versions 1 and 2, control-plane procedures, security risks, and mitigation strategies. Related training tracks: TS-201 — 2G/3G and TS-401 — LTE / EPC, depending on the mission scope.

  • IMS / SIP: Signaling fundamentals, protocol weaknesses, and protection mechanisms. Related course: TS-250 — IMS Security.

  • 5G: Service-based architecture (SBA), HTTP/2 and JSON-based APIs, and interconnect security involving N32 and the Security Edge Protection Proxy (SEPP). Related course: TS-501 — 5G Telecom Security hands-on course.

  • You do not need to cover every domain to apply. Specialists in one or several domains are welcome. Missions will be matched to your demonstrated expertise; please indicate the courses and topics you are confident teaching independently.

  • Proven experience delivering technical training, workshops, or hands-on instruction to engineering or SOC teams.

  • Ability to explain complex technical concepts, manage classroom discussion, and adapt to mixed levels of experience.

  • Practical experience analyzing telecom signaling traces and using packet-analysis tools such as Wireshark.

  • Confidence working with Linux-based lab environments and troubleshooting connectivity or exercise issues.

  • Professional preparation, reliable delivery, and clear communication with clients and the P1 Security team.

  • Willingness and ability to travel internationally for short-term onsite engagements: typically around five days per mission including travel, with some engagements requiring up to two weeks onsite.

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience in telecom security consulting, penetration testing, incident response, signaling monitoring, or mobile core network operations.

  • Familiarity with 3GPP security specifications and relevant GSMA signaling security guidance.

  • Experience with signaling firewalls, roaming and interconnect security, or telecom threat detection.

  • Experience adapting digital learning content into instructor-led courses and practical exercises.

  • Familiarity with virtualized or containerized lab environments and scripting for lab preparation.

  • Experience teaching international audiences or working across different cultural and organizational contexts.

Language requirements

  • Fluent professional English, with the ability to deliver technical instruction and facilitate discussions.

  • Additional languages are a plus, including French.

Engagement details

  • Contract type: Freelance, on a per-mission basis.

  • Delivery location: Onsite at client locations worldwide.

  • Mission duration: Typically around five days including travel; some engagements may require up to two weeks onsite.

  • Headquarters: Paris, France.

  • Training materials: Established curriculum and lab materials from P1 Security’s training platform, adapted for each classroom engagement.

  • Commercial arrangements: Scope, preparation time, delivery dates, fees, and travel and accommodation arrangements to be agreed for each mission.

Hiring process

  • First contact call (10-20min)

  • Direct manager call (30min)

  • Capability assessment exercice (depending on position)

  • C-level & Director call (30 min)

Contact

If you are a motivated and experienced professional who is passionate about cybersecurity and driving innovation, we would love to hear from you! Join P1 Security and be part of a fascinating mission to protect critical infrastructure and work alongside industry experts in the cybersecurity field.

To apply, please send your CV or professional profile and a short introduction highlighting your telecom security expertise and training experience. Include the protocols and courses you can teach, examples of previous workshops or audiences, your availability, your location and travel flexibility, and your indicative daily rate. Please do not include confidential client information.

title: Engineering Internship - Deep Learning for Infrared Thermography Antenna Measurements
description:
THE POSITION

ANYFIELDS measures antennas by infrared thermography: a thermosensitive film heated by the radiated field is imaged by an infrared camera, giving a 2D map of the electric field, nonintrusive and very close to the antenna. Two limits remain: the maps are noisy (dynamic range of 25 to 30 dB at best, 35 to 40 dB needed to retrieve side lobes and cross-polarization), and they are blurred by the response of the detector (film and optics), whose resolution is not explained by the theory.

This internship develops physics-driven neural networks, trained without any clean reference, to restore the maps, and compares them rigorously with the conventional methods already implemented.

Missions :

  • Benchmark synthetic and measured datasets, reproduction of the conventional methods (wavelet denoising, drift removal, deconvolution, slanted edge).

  • Estimate PSF of the detector: neural network constrained by the film heat diffusion and the optics, estimated from a few measurements; explain the gap between the theoretical (about 1 mm) and measured (4 to 8 mm) resolution. Compare with conventional methods.

  • Implement Denoising by self-supervised deep denoising of the maps, quantified gain in dB towards 35 to 40 dB, ranking of the limiting factors of the setup.

  • Validate by test whether the imaging resolves the individual elements of array antennas in the Ku and Ka bands, before and after improvement. Report on the retained methods.

You will work at the crossroads of electromagnetics, imaging and deep learning, with the engineers of the Innovation team.

Location: Toulouse (city centre)

Start: As soon as possible

Duration: 6 months

Profile

  • Bac+5 - Engineering school / Master in applied mathematics, signal and image processing, machine learning and/or electromagnetics

  • Programming skills (preferably Python), experience with a deep learning framework

  • Knowledge of inverse problems or infrared cameras is a plus

  • Team spirit, proactive attitude and good communication skills in an interdisciplinary team

As a Prediction Model Expert, you bring deep expertise in AI forecasting, software development in Python, backed by a dissertation on prediction models or time series forecasting. You have hands-on experience with foundation models for forecasting, multi-modal prediction frameworks (can be across disciplines like medicine), cloud environments. You will be one of Haste's first senior AI researchers pioneering prediction models that anticipate stealthy threats across HPC clusters, AI and quantum workloads before they strike.

  • Predictive Model Development & Engineering: Designing, building, and deploying Machine Learning (ML) and Foundation models to forecast potential security breaches.

title: Full-Stack Engineer - Data, Infrastructure & AI
description:
About Agent F

Agent F is building an autonomous finance function: software that takes on the work of keeping a company’s finances in order. That means bringing information together from different systems, recording transactions correctly, preparing useful reports, and helping people understand what needs their attention.

Today, much of this work depends on spreadsheets, repeated data entry and people checking one system against another. Our ambition is to make that work increasingly automatic, while keeping every number explainable and every consequential action under clear control.

We are building towards a complete business management system for growing companies. These founding roles will shape both the product and the way we build it.

About the role

You will be a full-stack engineer, shipping customer features across the interface, application services and database. Your particular strength will be the data and infrastructure that make those features dependable: how records are stored, how imports and background jobs run, and how information moves between Agent F and a customer’s other tools. You will help build and operate the whole product, with deeper ownership of this foundation.

This is hands-on full-stack engineering. A typical piece of work could involve extending a data model, implementing an application service, connecting it to a screen, testing it against a real database and following the release into production. You will also investigate slow reports, failed imports and jobs that stop halfway through, then improve the system so it handles those situations reliably.

That foundation also supports our AI work. As we add document extraction, connected customer knowledge and software that takes actions for customers, you will build the services and data access those features need. The immediate priority is dependable software that customers can use, with more capable automation developed around specific tasks.

What you will build and improve

  • Application services and customer features. Build the logic and application programming interfaces (APIs) that connect records, business rules and screens. Take features through implementation, testing, release and production support.

  • The database foundation. Design clear data models, enforce relationships and transaction boundaries, and improve slow queries. Manage schema changes through reviewed migrations, preserve financial history and keep each customer’s data isolated.

  • Imports and integrations. Connect accounting tools, business systems and spreadsheets to a consistent model. Validate incoming records, handle changing source formats, and check that imported totals and reports agree with the source.

  • Reliable background processing. Build scheduled jobs and workers that process work outside a user request. Handle retries without creating duplicates, resume interrupted runs, and make progress and failures visible to the team.

  • Performance and recovery. Diagnose expensive queries, processing bottlenecks and partial failures. Test changes against real databases, plan for growing workloads, and build procedures to recover processing safely with the platform engineer.

  • Practical AI automation. Add features such as extracting invoice fields or preparing an order from approved business data. Give models access through controlled services, check the result and require approval where needed. Develop connected customer knowledge when a feature needs those relationships, and measure whether it improves the result.

For example, a large customer import stops halfway through and the same records arrive again on the next run. You would make processing resume safely, prevent duplicate records, verify the resulting totals and expose the job’s status in the product. You would also investigate whether database queries or worker capacity caused the failure and ship the necessary fix.

What you bring

You have seven or more years of software engineering experience, including substantial ownership of production applications and data systems. You have designed relational data models, built services and processing pipelines, and stayed responsible for them after release. You are comfortable delivering across the stack and using AI tools in your daily work.

You can explain how you diagnosed a slow query, recovered a failed job or shipped a database change safely. You understand what happens when two requests arrive at once, a dependency becomes unavailable or a process restarts halfway through its work. You can follow a problem from a source record through the application to the result a customer sees.

Core experience

  • Full-stack development with TypeScript, Node.js, React and PostgreSQL, or closely comparable technologies.

  • Relational data modelling, SQL, query optimisation, indexes, transactions and reviewed database migrations.

  • Application services and APIs, including permissions, validation and handling concurrent requests.

  • Data imports, integrations and background jobs, including queues, safe retries and recovery from partial failures.

  • Production debugging, service monitoring and performance work on systems used by real customers.

  • Automated tests against real databases and other service dependencies.

  • Practical use of AI in software, with an understanding of how to check outputs and control access to customer data.

  • Daily use of AI coding agents, with direct responsibility for code review and verification.

  • A computer science or computer engineering degree, or equivalent practical depth.

Useful additional experience

Financial or operational systems where correctness and traceability matter; larger data migrations; cloud storage and container-based workloads. Experience putting document extraction or features using large language models (LLMs) into production would be valuable. Knowledge graphs, which connect related company records, and privately hosted or adapted models are useful as we develop that part of the product.

What early progress could look like

In your first months, you would take ownership of an existing service or data flow, understand how it runs in production and ship a customer-facing improvement through it. You would address a concrete reliability or performance problem, such as a slow report, a fragile integration or a job that cannot recover cleanly after interruption.

We would look for working features, faster and more predictable processing, fewer failed or manually repaired jobs, and useful tests and monitoring. An early automation feature could follow where the data and services are ready and its benefit can be measured.

Operational excellence and customer commitments

You take pride in a dependable application backbone: processing completes, records reconcile and customers can trust the results. When a job fails or figures disagree, you take ownership of the investigation and recovery. Missing transactions, duplicate entries or unexplained balance differences can be financial emergencies even while every service appears available. You assess the impact, contain affected processing, trace the cause and verify the repaired result before treating the incident as resolved.

Customer commitments shape how we work. You are willing to interrupt planned work, respond promptly and stay engaged when an urgent issue puts a service-level agreement (SLA), onboarding commitment or financial deadline at risk. That requires flexibility beyond normal working hours as part of agreed on-call coverage and coordinated incident response. You keep people informed and see the issue through to a verified recovery or an explicit handover. Afterwards, you improve the system so the same emergency becomes less likely.

How you will work

This is a senior founding role in a small team. You will own the application and data infrastructure for your work, and carry a full share of customer feature delivery. You will collaborate across infrastructure, operations and product design to deliver complete customer outcomes. You will use coding agents to implement changes and remain responsible for reviewing, testing and operating the result.

Everyone shares responsibility for the whole product and the customer outcome. You will pick up the most important work or whatever is on fire, including tasks outside your specialty. You take initiative, bring in the right expertise and stay involved until the problem is resolved. Customer impact and urgency determine where you focus.

The role is full-time and in-person in Berlin. German is not required.

description:
About CircuitHub

CircuitHub is reshaping electronics manufacturing with The Grid, a factory-scale robotics platform that makes small-batch, high-mix electronics assembly radically more efficient. What you'll do

CircuitHub builds circuit boards on demand, every order different. Each day thousands of decisions are made: which orders run on which machines, which parts to buy and when, what to promise a customer and what to charge. You'll build the models behind those decisions.

  • Plan the factory. Schedule orders, panels and machines across our factories for throughput and on-time delivery, and know days ahead when we will run out of work or capacity.

  • Buy smarter. Decide what parts and consumables to stock, when to order them, and how much risk of a shortage to accept.

  • A quantitative background in operations research, applied maths, statistics, quantitative finance, economics or a similar field, and a record of models that changed real decisions.

  • Optimisation: linear and integer programming, constraint programming, or heuristics, and judgement about when a simple rule beats a solver.

  • Simulation and forecasting: building a model of a messy system, calibrating it to data and saying how far to trust it.

  • Strong Python and SQL. You write code other people can run and rely on.

  • You use coding agents to move faster and take full ownership of what they produce.

  • Curiosity about how things are physically made. You'll spend time in our factories in the US and UK.

Manufacturing experience is welcome but not required. If you have priced risk, optimised a portfolio or forecast demand, the problems here will feel familiar.

You will run hands-on, authenticated security testing across a real attack surface: public partner-facing booking APIs, payment flows, web and mobile apps used by millions of travellers, and the cloud infrastructure behind them. You’ll plan and run your own testing, work directly with our engineering squads to get findings fixed, and see your impact in production within weeks.

What you will do:

  • Test our partner-facing booking APIs against the OWASP API Security Top 10, with a focus on object- and function-level authorization, tenant isolation, mass assignment, data exposure and rate limiting.

  • Assess API authentication and integrity end to end, including OAuth 2.0/OIDC, API keys, JWTs, webhooks and request signing.

  • Hunt for business-logic abuse in booking, checkout, payment and refund flows, including race conditions and pricing manipulation.

  • Run authenticated tests of traveller-, partner- and operator-facing web and mobile apps following OWASP WSTG and ASVS, including how passenger personal data is stored, shown and exported.

  • Review cloud, Kubernetes and CI/CD configurations and secrets handling for attack paths that could be chained from an application bug.

  • Map and regularly test our internet-facing attack surface.

  • Red-team our AI features (assistants, agents, support bots) against the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications.

  • Write clear, reproducible, risk-rated findings with practical remediation guidance, walk engineers through fixes and verify them with retests.

Workplace:

We are a remote-first company with teams located around the Globe and a HQ in Berlin.


Who you are:

  • You bring 5+ years of hands-on penetration testing, mainly of web applications and APIs, and can point to recent engagements you’ve led end to end.

  • You have deep, practical knowledge of the OWASP API Security Top 10, WSTG and ASVS, including authentication/authorization models (OAuth2/OIDC, JWT), IDOR/BOLA, mass assignment, SSRF, injection and XSS.

  • You have found business-logic and race-condition vulnerabilities in transactional systems such as booking, e-commerce, payments or fintech.

  • You are fluent with Burp Suite Pro (or similar) and write your own scripts and tooling (Python, Go or similar).

  • You are comfortable assessing cloud and container environments (GCP preferred, Kubernetes) and CI/CD pipelines.

  • You work independently: you scope, prioritise, test and report with minimal guidance, and you explain complex risks plainly to engineers and leadership.

  • You are available to start at short notice.

  • Bonus Points: OSCP, OSWE, BSCP or similar certifications; experience red-teaming LLM applications or AI agents; testing in PCI-DSS environments.

  • You will join a fast-paced travel tech company with a flat organizational structure.

title: Gap-Year-Student (m/w/d) im Office der Geschäftsführung
description:
Ihre Aufgaben

Eigene Projekte mit echter Verantwortung: Du übernimmst über die Monate hinweg mehrere klar abgegrenzte Initiativen, von der Konzeption bis zur Umsetzung.

KI-Anwendungen bauen: Du nutzt KI nicht nur als Tool, sondern entwickelst eigene Anwendungen für unser Team und unsere Kunden, von Automatisierungen über Custom GPTs bis zu kleinen Webanwendungen.

Strategische Mitarbeit: Du arbeitest an OKR-Planungen, Investorenpräsentationen, Marktanalysen und Operational-Excellence-Themen mit.

Cross-funktionale Einblicke: Du bekommst Zugang zu allen Bereichen (Tech, Fulfillment, Marketing, Sales) und verstehst nach einem Jahr, wie ein wachsendes Unternehmen wirklich funktioniert.

Sparring auf Augenhöhe: Du wirst behandelt wie ein vollwertiges Teammitglied, mit allen Rechten und Pflichten.

Ihr Profil

Du hast Dein Abitur mit sehr guten Leistungen abgeschlossen oder befindest Dich zwischen Bachelor und Master.

Du bringst hohe intrinsische Motivation mit und Lust, ein Jahr lang wirklich etwas zu lernen statt es einfach zu überbrücken.

Echte Begeisterung für KI und Technologie: Du arbeitest selbstverständlich mit Tools wie ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor & Co., probierst Neues aus und schreckst nicht zurück, wenn ein Projekt technisches Neuland ist.

Keine Angst vor technischen Herausforderungen: Wenn ein Workflow automatisiert werden muss oder ein neues Tool evaluiert werden soll, legst Du los und lernst beim Tun.

Analytisches Denkvermögen, Hands-on-Mentalität und unternehmerisches Gespür.

Reife, Eigenverantwortung und Lust, schnell zu lernen, auch wenn vieles neu ist.

Verhandlungssichere Deutschkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift.

Warum wir?

Unser Ziel: ein faires, datengetriebenes Wertgutachten für jede Immobilie in Deutschland. Bei Certa ersetzen wir das klassische Sachverständigenwesen durch eine KI-gestützte Bewertungsplattform, die schneller, präziser und transparenter ist als alles, was der Markt heute kennt.

Du planst ein Gap Year zwischen Schule und Studium oder zwischen Bachelor und Master und willst diese Zeit nicht mit Backpacking-Klischees, sondern mit echter Verantwortung füllen? Bei Certa bekommst Du eine Rolle, die Du in einem Jahr nirgendwo sonst bekommst.

Das Office der Geschäftsführung arbeitet direkt mit den beiden Gründern und Geschäftsführern (Alexander Rausch & Matthias Mertens) an den Top-Themen, die Certa als Unternehmen entscheidend voranbringen. Vom OKR-Framework über Marktexpansion und Operational Excellence bis zum Aufbau skalierbarer Backoffice-Strukturen. Trotz der Nähe zur Geschäftsführung leben wir eine entrepreneuriale, pragmatische Arbeitskultur: kurze Wege, schnelle Entscheidungen, hohe Umsetzungstiefe.

Ein Gap Year bei Certa ist kein Praktikum mit Abstrichen, sondern eine vollwertige Rolle mit eigenen Verantwortungsbereichen. Du bekommst Zeit, in mehrere Themen tief reinzukommen, eigene Projekte aufzubauen und mit der Zeit echte Ownership zu übernehmen.

Ein Jahr, das Dich prägt: Du lernst in 12 Monaten mehr über Wirtschaft, Technologie und Unternehmensführung als in den ersten zwei Studienjahren.

Direkte Linie zu den Gründern: Du arbeitest täglich mit den beiden Gründern und Geschäftsführern. Keine Layer, keine Politik, keine Slide-Schlachten.

Spielwiese für KI-Enthusiasten: Bei uns ist KI kein Buzzword, sondern Arbeitsalltag. Du bekommst Zugang zu allen relevanten Tools und Modellen.

Echte Verantwortung: Du arbeitest an Themen, die wirklich zählen, nicht an Beschäftigungstherapie.

Faire Vergütung: Anders als bei vielen Gap-Year-Programmen wirst Du bei uns als vollwertiges Teammitglied bezahlt.

title: AI & Automation Lead (f/m/x)
description:
About lemon.markets 🍋

We grow investing opportunities for all European customers and businesses, providing seamless access to capital markets. We enable everyone to be an investor.

lemon.markets builds infrastructure for financial services and technology companies powering the next generation of investment products. From enabling a FinTech to launch their first investment product, over allowing e.g. a Neobank to embed investing into their product to bringing investing into a completely new context. Our API-first infrastructure makes launching an investment product customer-centric and compliant. We abstract all complexity for our partners through a well documented API, a self-service customer operations portal and operating in a clear regulatory framework. Enabling partners to launch in weeks, not months.

We have experienced first hand that brokerage infrastructure is broken. Building an investment product used to be highly expensive, challenging and cumbersome. We ease this pain by shielding our partners & their customers from the underlying complexity - and with that we make investing more accessible to everyone. Because that’s exactly what we enjoy, going to places nobody else dares and solving hard problems. This not only creates tons of value when done right, but attracts the smartest minds - because outlier companies are built by exceptional (& diverse) people like you.

Your Mission:

As AI & Automation Lead, you will establish and lead lemon.markets’ first dedicated AI function, making AI a safe, practical and measurable part of how the whole company works. Reporting directly to the VP Engineering and operating across the first line, you will identify high-value opportunities across Engineering, Finance, Operations, Compliance, Product, Sales, Partner Management and People and turn them into solutions that improve efficiency without compromising quality or control.

You will build on the foundations already being established, including a governed AI platform, an inventory of current use cases and an initial risk assessment aligned with the EU AI Act. A key part of your role will be creating the standards, measurement framework and decision processes that determine which use cases are scaled, improved or stopped.

Working closely with Engineering, Finance, Risk Management and Compliance, you will balance innovation with data protection, operational resilience, cost discipline and regulatory expectations. This is your opportunity to shape how a regulated financial company adopts AI responsibly, while building a function that leaves lasting capability across the organisation.

In this role you will

  • Lead the AI function and work with department heads across lemon.markets to identify, prioritise and deliver use cases that create measurable business value beyond Engineering.

  • Build a transparent, evidence-based portfolio of AI initiatives with business owners, baselines, success metrics and appropriate guardrails, ensuring that promising ideas become sustainable improvements.

  • Enable teams across the company to use AI effectively themselves by developing practical workflows, guidance and capabilities that reduce manual effort without creating dependency on the AI function.

description:
Who we are:

We're one of Europe's fastest-growing fintech companies – on a mission to create the world's most empowering way to pay.

We launched the product in 2020 and achieved double unicorn status, valued at $2 billion, and since then have taken on more than 6 million customers.

Our mission is to become the best way to pay for anything, anywhere and say goodbye to credit costs for everyone. This is huge. Want to join us?

About the role.

The Senior Product Analyst, Merchant will be the dedicated analytics lead for Zilch’s Merchant domain - the space where shopping discovery, merchant-funded advertising, paid display, paid search, affiliate conversion, and customer engagement come together.

Reporting into Product Analytics and partnering closely with the Senior Product Manager for Merchant, you’ll help build the analytical foundation for Zilch’s intelligent commerce platform. This is a two-sided problem: we need to improve the customer shopping experience while helping merchants drive measurable ROAS through Zilch’s closed-loop payments and behavioural data.

Here, paid display and paid search refer to advertising inventory we sell to merchants, not media we buy. You’ll help define how this inventory is measured, targeted, optimised, and monetised across the Zilch app.

You’ll analyse the full shopping journey - from browsing and search, through merchant discovery, unlocks, clickouts, transactions, and repeat engagement - to understand where users drop off, what drives intent, and which product features can improve engagement, conversion, and monetisation.

This is not a reporting-only role. The analysis, experimentation, and models you build will directly shape what customers see, how merchants are surfaced, and how we move from static merchandising towards data-driven discovery, allocation, and personalisation.

Day to day responsibilities.

  • Own analytics for Zilch’s Merchant domain, covering shopping discovery, customer browsing behaviour, merchant-funded paid display and paid search, affiliate conversion, merchant ROAS, and marketplace performance.

  • Design and analyse experiments across merchant placements and shopping features, including targeted vs random allocation, paid display exposure, search ranking, storefront changes, offer discovery, and journey improvements.

  • Build the measurement framework for merchant-funded growth, including incrementality, attribution windows, exposed vs control logic, ROAS, CPA, conversion, revenue per impression, and margin impact.

  • Partner with Product and Commercial to shape audience packages and targeting strategies, ensuring they are commercially sellable, analytically measurable, and grounded in customer behaviour.

  • Develop segmentation approaches for merchant-funded display and search, including category affinity, value bands, browsing intent, cross-sell audiences, lapsed users, and future lookalike opportunities.

  • Support the evolution from simple segment-based targeting towards more advanced allocation logic, recommendation systems, and marketplace decisioning.

  • Work with Data Science, Data Engineering, and Engineering on the data foundations for merchant personalisation, including event tracking, feature creation, experimentation infrastructure, and model evaluation.

  • Translate complex analysis into clear recommendations for Product, Commercial, and senior leadership.


What we're looking for...

  • Ideally, 5+ years of experience in product analytics, growth analytics, marketplace analytics, retail media analytics, performance marketing analytics, data science, or a closely adjacent role.

  • Strong commercial judgement and fluency in ROAS, CPA, incrementality, attribution, LTV, conversion, margin, and marketplace trade-offs.

  • Deep data skills. You’re fluent in SQL, comfortable working with large behavioural datasets, and able to independently investigate ambiguous problems, define the right metrics, and produce robust analysis.

  • Rigorous experimentation experience. You can design clean A/B tests, reason about incrementality and power, interpret results honestly, and know when data is good enough to act on.

  • Experience analysing digital funnels, browsing behaviour, search behaviour, clickouts, conversion, paid placements, shopping discovery, or marketplace dynamics.

Infrata has strong technical expertise and established client relationships. We are looking for someone who can help us build on these strengths by developing new consulting services, winning work and leading projects.

  • Develop services. Work with clients and colleagues to identify problems we have the expertise to address but do not currently advise on. Develop services we can deliver consistently, with a clear scope, team, price and evidence of their value.

Service development

  • Understand the team's expertise and identify opportunities to offer advisory services beyond due diligence.

Engagement leadership

You will advise owners, operators, developers and public bodies on areas including market entry and growth strategy, asset and portfolio strategy, business planning, governance and assurance, policy and regulatory positioning, and investment case development.

title: Head of Platform & Infrastructure Engineering
description:
Hi 👋🏾, I’m Abhik, Ashby’s Co-Founder and CTO. Ashby is growing fast, which means exponential growth across every product metric: jobs, applications, interviews, you name it. We’re not slowing down, and as a result, keeping Ashby performant and reliable is a company priority. We need your leadership to do that now and in the future.

We’ve already assembled a fantastic Platform & Infrastructure team of 11 engineers (all Senior+, >70% Staff), and they’ve done an excellent job handling our growth, but the management and leadership of Platform & Infrastructure have been diffused across our Engineering leaders. As we hit our next level of scale, it’s time for us to hire an Engineering leader responsible for performance and reliability, and for building out the team that ensures those. Hopefully, that’s you!

 

The Role

In this role, you will report directly to me, and your responsibilities will include:

  • Building and maintaining a long-term vision and 6-month roadmap for Platform & Infrastructure.

  • Growing the Platform & Infrastructure team. You’ll hire ICs, managers, and build out a headcount plan. This will include determining if more specialized roles need to be established (e.g., DB Admin).

  • Building and maintaining an excellent relationship with Product Engineering. The ideal state is that Product Engineering can move incredibly fast independently without breaking performance or reliability, and Platform & Infrastructure doesn’t feel like they’re always cleaning up someone else’s “mess.” Today, there’s a great relationship, but there’s always room for improvement!

  • Assessing and improving our monitoring and incident management process. Again, we’re doing relatively well here, but there’s always room to improve. For example, making uptime measurement easier and improving coordination with Support during incidents.

  • Maintaining vendor relationships and negotiating pricing for our critical hosting and observability infrastructure, including AWS, ClickHouse, Datadog, and Braintrust. They have a meaningful impact on gross margin and need to be kept in check.

  • You’ve managed managers. Managing other leaders is a very different ball game, and not everyone enjoys it or thrives in it. Within your first 6 months, you’ll most likely have to hire a manager underneath you.

  • If you have experience managing developer experience and developer tools, building out a dedicated team for DevEx. If you don’t have experience here, DevEx will report into Product Engineering. Happy to discuss once we meet!

A big part of our secret sauce is how we run Engineering. We achieve incredible speed and quality by discarding many industry norms and being optimistic about Engineers. We consider what makes exceptional Engineers exceptional, then figure out how to hire them and build an environment that gives them the freedom and agency to be exceptional. You’ll be a key leader in ensuring that continues!

 

The Qualifications

We’re entrusting you with a company priority, so we want you to know how to scale products and build the great teams that do that. This means:

  • You played an important role leading a company through a high-growth period (either as an IC Lead or Engineering Leader). You had to make high-quality decisions under pressure. That often meant striking a balance between short-term fixes to keep the product from falling over and long-term investments to ensure it didn’t happen again.

  • You have experience hiring and building hiring processes, and enjoy it! You’ve designed interviews, interview loops, and led hiring strategy.

  • You have a track record of excellent collaboration with other departments. You were a key contributor to company-level initiatives that involved Product Engineering, Product, Sales, or Support. Those departments felt heard and supported, yet positively challenged by you.

  • You are knowledgeable about platform and infrastructure technologies, networking, and hardware. You know how Kubernetes goes beyond a Container Orchestration Platform, how traffic flows between Load Balancers and Pods, and how the intricacies of the underlying hardware can cause Cloud abstractions to break, etc.

  • You are a great communicator, particularly in writing. You’ll need to be able to go deep with Infrastructure Engineers in conversations while also communicating those concepts to folks like myself who have much less experience.

You should be comfortable managing a team spanning from the Americas West Coast to Europe. You’ll be able to hire managers to focus on specific time zones, but I expect you to have skips with some engineers (and you should want to, too!). To ensure a reasonable work schedule, we’re only hiring candidates who live in the PST-GMT time zone.

 

What We’re Building

As engineers, we are used to tooling that makes us better at what we do. When we started Ashby, we saw the opposite with Talent Acquisition software. Recruiting teams were leveling up how they did their work, but instead of software meeting this new standard, it held them back.

Scheduling a final round is an excellent example. Recruiting teams wanted to schedule candidates faster, track interviewer preparation and quality, and do it with half the headcount. A recruiter needed to manually collect availability from the candidate, identify qualified interviewers, perform “Calendar Tetris” to find who is available to interview the candidate, schedule on the earliest date possible, and make any last-minute adjustments as availability changed. They must do this while considering the interview load on each individual and whether interviewers need to be trained and shadowing others. 🥵 TA software didn’t help.

As hiring managers, we know TA is a critical function, and as engineers, we know software can do better. So, we built and continue to build Ashby to give TA teams the highest standard of tooling. Software that’s intelligent and powerful. Software that provides insights into where they’re failing and automates or simplifies many of the tasks they’re underwater with. We want other functions and departments to be jealous of what TA teams can do with Ashby, and today they often are!

 

Why You Shouldn’t Apply

  • You’ve always been a line manager or never led a department within Engineering. You haven’t led the definition and evolution of culture and processes.

  • You don’t enjoy coding or don’t find time to stay up-to-date on technology. We believe great leaders are folks who were great engineers themselves. That starts with loving the craft and never giving it up.

  • You went into management because it was the only growth path available. We want folks who could have been Principal engineers (or were one!).

  • You're happy with a team of engineers who are predominantly early-career or mid-career or don't thrive with ownership or autonomy. You believe that with enough guardrails, the team can get things done.

  • To you, a Staff or Principal Engineer is someone who spends most of their time project managing or conducting architecture reviews. You don’t believe staff and principal engineers could lead by the example they set or the leverage they create through their work.

  • You’re not optimistic or convinced that we can build a large engineering team that functions differently from the status quo. You think, at some size, common processes need to be implemented to ensure consistent delivery (e.g., sprint planning, product managers writing in-depth specifications). You might not say it out loud, but you think, at some size, compromises have to be made for the sake of hiring numbers or consistency.

 

Engineering Culture

Our engineering culture is motivated by Benji’s (Co-founder and CEO) and my belief that a small, talented team, given the right environment, can build high-quality software fast (and work regular hours!). We do it through:

  • Minimal process with ownership over decisions normally made by product and design

  • Natural collaboration and deliberate communication

  • Investing in tools and abstractions that give us leverage, including LLM-driven dev tooling.

  • Putting effort into building a diverse team

 

Minimal Process & Lots of Ownership

The best engineers we’ve worked with delivered reliably magical outcomes. They often discovered problems, prioritized the right ones, and relentlessly drove them to solutions that were not only successful but often brilliant and creative. While they did this with minimal oversight, stakeholders were never in the dark as to what was going on, and no setback was a surprise.

Traditional development processes aren’t meant for the best engineers. Their purpose is to create consistent outcomes regardless of the engineer’s skill. But consistency comes at the expense of an engineer’s time and freedom—both ingredients necessary to generate those magical outcomes. As a result, process stifles the best engineers and doesn’t give others the opportunity to practice the behaviors that made the best engineers the “best.”

At Ashby, we want to build an environment that encourages every engineer to be their best. So, every Engineer runs their project. Product Managers (and Designers) build strategy, do customer research, and hand off problem briefs to Engineers. Engineers take on the rest: they research the problem, write product specs, build wireframes, and implement their solution end-to-end. We rely on engineers, not process, to push information outward to the relevant folks (e.g., Product Managers) and pull folks in to help (e.g., Designers, Infra). It’s a new level of ownership for many engineers, but we’d rather an engineer fail a bit and coach up their skills than use process as a crutch. Not everyone succeeds in our culture, but those who do thrive.

 

Collaboration is Natural & Communication is Deliberate

Our engineering team consists of lifelong learners who are talented but also humble and kind (meet them here!). These attributes create an environment where collaboration happens naturally. We combine this with research, prototyping, and written proposals to see around corners and get feedback from the team across time zones. Focus time is something that we hold sacred, and, with thoughtful and deliberate communication, engineers are in <2h meetings per week (I wrote about it here).

To drive it home, here's a recent calendar of an engineer who has been with us for over 4 years. ~34 hours of focus time, 2.5h of interviews, and 3.5 hours of meetings:

We also meet in person at least twice a year, once as a department and once as a company. You also have a small budget to meet up with folks in your city/region.

Increase Leverage, not Team Size

We built Ashby with the quality, breadth, and depth that many customers would expect from much larger teams over larger time scales. We’ve done this through investment in:

  • Great developer tooling. For example, our CI/CD takes ~10m, we deploy at least 15x a day, and our debugger works out of the box. Everyone on the team has contributed to our developer experience 💪🏾.

  • Building blocks to create powerful and customizable products fast. At the core of Ashby is a set of common components (analytics modeling and query language, policy engine, workflow engine, design system) that we constantly improve. Each improvement to a common component cascades throughout our app (short video below).

  • AI-powered tooling. We think of AI as a way to automate the mundane parts of building and maintaining high-quality software. We use a combination of third-party and internally built tools that, for instance, auto-triage customer issues, suggest fixes, prototype ideas, generate production-ready code, and conduct code reviews. Engineers have an unlimited token budget (but are not measured on it). We write in detail about our philosophy, current use of AI, and future plans for AI in Engineering here.

Here’s an impromptu quote from Arjun in our company Slack of what it’s like to build a feature at Ashby:

And a demo of one of these building blocks:

Put Effort into Diversity

Diverse teams drive innovation and better outcomes. Having seen my mother and partner build their careers as minority women in non-diverse fields, I want to make sure Ashby creates opportunities for the next generation of engineers from underrepresented groups.

Today, 30% of engineers and 50% of our engineering leaders at Ashby are from underrepresented groups. We actively maintain and improve these numbers by sourcing diverse candidates, providing generous paid family leave, banning leetcode interviews, providing guidance and coaching to candidates, and more.

 

Work-Life Balance: It’s A Marathon, Not a Sprint

The intensity of work at Ashby should feel like a marathon, not a sprint (nor speed-walking). We work with urgency and ambition to build excellent software, but we don’t need to prove out a new software category or product-market fit. That requires ingenuity and thoughtfulness, and that doesn’t happen with unrealistic deadlines or sleepless nights.

Our remote, low-meeting, high-ownership culture gives engineers (and to a similar degree, you) a lot of flexibility in how they structure their days and weeks. In practice, that means they keep their own hours, but there will be moments of intensity, like launching their feature at our annual user conference. We offer unlimited PTO, and they actually get to use it. Some of our most exceptional engineers take almost 30 days of vacation per year.

This way of working allows many of us on the team to be active parents, including Benji and me. I block off 1.5 hours every morning to spend with my daughter and drop her off at school. Mujda (Product Engineer) puts it best in an article about us: “I can say that Ashby is a great place to be a mom… No one bats an eye if I have to take my kid to a doctor’s appointment or have to work weird hours because childcare fell through.”

 

Interview Process

This is an important role that will lead our Platform & Infrastructure teams now and for the foreseeable future. The interview process reflects that in both challenge and length (5 rounds, ~6.5h):

  1. Introduction call with me (30m, live)

  2. A technical screen where we pair in our actual codebase (1h, live)

  3. An interview to explore your past experience as a leader (1h, live)

  4. Interview with Colin, our Head of EMEA Engineering (45m)

  5. Final round where you meet various folks on the team and explore leadership and technical topics (3h)

I’ll have a strong read on whether we’re trending toward an offer by Round 3. Near the end of the process, we’ll do reference checks with a former manager, two direct reports, and a peer in Engineering. Depending on my bandwidth, we may start with an additional 30m screen with a recruiter.

This is also an important decision for you, so once you start interviewing, I’m always happy to have coffee chats in person or over Zoom to get to know each other.

 

Your First Six Months at Ashby

Your first three months at Ashby will be spent learning about Ashby Engineering and easing into leadership. While most of your onboarding will be driven by a 6-month plan you put together (and refine over time), you’ll also ship some product changes, features, and infra changes. What better way to learn how ICs work than to be one! Don’t worry if you’re not familiar with our technologies. The team is really helpful, and our dev environment is pretty awesome: it sets up in a single script, and you’ll be able to push your first product change on day one.

You and I will do 30-day, 60-day, 90-day, and 6-month reviews to calibrate on our unique culture and how you, I, and the team will work together.

 

Benefits

  • Competitive salary and equity.

  • 10-year exercise window for stock options. You shouldn’t feel pressure to purchase stock options if you leave Ashby —do it when you feel financially comfortable.

  • Unlimited PTO.

  • A minimum of 12 weeks of fully paid parental leave, covered by Ashby. For folks outside the US, it may be longer to be in line with regional requirements.

  • Generous equipment, software, and office furniture budget. Get what you need to be happy and productive!

  • $100/month education budget with more expensive items (like conferences) covered with manager approval.

  • If you’re in the US, we offer top-tier health insurance for you and your dependents, with 100% of premiums covered by Ashby. In other countries, we provide high-quality supplemental health insurance for you and your dependents, also fully covered by us.

Ashby’s success hinges on hiring great people and creating an environment where we can be happy, feel challenged, and do our best work. We’re being deliberate about building that environment from the ground up. I hope that excites you enough to apply.

The team

The New Customers team owns everything from a business's first application to a funded loan: the application flow, the logic that routes each application, the documents we ask customers for, and the models that set loan amounts and pricing. The team sets its own goals and direction. It brings together engineers, data scientists, and product and strategy people. It partners closely with credit risk on the trade-offs behind every lending decision.
